items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: This paper constructs a textual dataset for training large language models (LLMs) to learn analog circuit knowledge and customizes LLM training techniques. For dataset construction, high-quality textbooks are collected and decomposed into fine-grained learning nodes, which are then used to construct structured question-thinking-solution-answer (QTSA) quadruples using a multi-agent framework to capture both final answers and thought processes. The resulting dataset consists of 7.26M tokens of unlabeled data for continual pre-training (CPT) and 112.65M tokens of labeled data for supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Instruct models are identified as suitable training initialization points, an SFT-centric training paradigm is established (finding that CPT provides marginal benefits compared with SFT due to imbalanced data distribution), and SFT with KL divergence regularization can achieve a 2.71 percentage-point improvement over SFT alone. items.abstract_text: This paper constructs a textual dataset for training large language models (LLMs) to learn analog circuit knowledge and customizes LLM training techniques. For dataset construction, high-quality textbooks are collected and decomposed into fine-grained learning nodes, which are then used to construct structured question-thinking-solution-answer (QTSA) quadruples using a multi-agent framework to capture both final answers and thought processes. The resulting dataset consists of 7.26M tokens of unlabeled data for continual pre-training (CPT) and 112.65M tokens of labeled data for supervised fine-tuning (SFT). We customize the training techniques including initial model selection, training paradigms, regularization techniques, and practical implementation references. Instruct models are identified as suitable training initialization points, an SFT-centric training paradigm is established (finding that CPT provides marginal benefits compared with SFT due to imbalanced data distribution), and SFT with KL divergence regularization can achieve a 2.71 percentage-point improvement over SFT alone. A practical training implementation method is provided for resource-constrained scenarios. Experiments demonstrate that the dataset and training techniques enhance LLMs’ analog circuit knowledge. The trained 32B instruct model achieves 84.59% accuracy on the AMSBench-TQA benchmark, showing a 15.67 percentage-point improvement over the initial model. The trained model also shows capability in the operational amplifier design task based on the Atelier framework.

items.abstract_text: Video data are widely used in AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things) systems, where maintaining reliable operation under hardware-induced decoding faults is increasingly important. In practical deployments, decoder-side faults—such as persistent circuit defects caused by aging, voltage variations, or wear-out—may lead to corrupted video reconstruction and temporal error propagation. A major challenge is that no golden reference video is available during normal operation, making online reliability evaluation difficult. Existing studies primarily focus on human-vision–oriented perceptual quality assessment and provide limited support for task-level correctness in computer-vision pipelines. This paper presents a lightweight, calibration-driven, no-reference error-tolerability testing framework from a computer-vision perspective. The proposed framework performs decoder-side online decision-making without requiring golden references, using hardware-friendly structural-variation and extreme-value–variation features to characterize decoding-induced distortions. Unlike prior perceptual-quality approaches, acceptability is explicitly defined according to downstream task performance, and the framework supports task adaptation through recalibration. Using QCIF (176 × 144) videos together with YOLOv3 and YOLOv7 object-detection systems as case studies, the proposed framework achieves average test accuracies of 89.48% and 93.21%, and precisions of 91.53% and 95.08%, respectively, outperforming prior no-reference testing approaches under the evaluated settings. In addition, we further demonstrate a deployment-dependent adaptive enhancement mechanism based on encoder-side GOP/I-frame adjustment, which converts more than 50% of previously unacceptable videos into acceptable ones under the evaluated scenarios. We further present a streaming-compatible hardware implementation of the proposed framework. The synthesized core testing logic requires approximately 11.7k logic gates (6.92% overhead relative to an open-source H.264 decoder core under the evaluated integration assumptions) and operates at 312.5 MHz, supporting real-time online testing for 30 fps Full HD video streams. Overall, this work presents a task-oriented and deployment-aware framework for decoder-side online video error-tolerability testing and adaptive reliability enhancement under hardware-induced decoding faults without requiring golden reference videos.

items.abstract_text: Aging-aware timing analysis is becoming increasingly important in advanced technology nodes, where devices are more susceptible to aging-induced degradation and reliability margins are tighter. However, efficient design-stage aging-aware timing analysis remains challenging because it requires accurate prediction of delay and slew degradation without exhaustively running aging-aware SPICE simulations across workloads, process corners, PDKs, and timing paths. Existing methods either model transistor-level degradation without extending naturally to path timing or estimate path-level aging using coarse signal-probability approximations rather than fine-grained transistor-level stress behaviors. However, no practical framework currently combines fine-grained transistor-level aging-stress modeling with reusable full-chip-scale path-timing estimation across process corners and PDKs. To address this gap, we propose RelFACT, a rel iable and f ast a ging-aware c ell-to-path t iming analysis framework that combines input-signal correlation with standard-cell topology analysis to model transistor aging stress at fine granularity. It further integrates aging-related operating conditions into an effective aging-aware standard-cell graph representation. A graph attention model predicts aged cell delays and output slews, which are then propagated through post-layout timing paths to provide aging-aware timing indications and practical signoff guidance. Once trained or adapted for a target process technology/library, RelFACT can be reused for newly encountered paths without per-path retraining. On an industrial sub-20nm FinFET PDK, RelFACT achieves less than 2.5% MAPE for both aged cell delay and slew prediction, improving over existing state-of-the-art cell-level aging-aware predictors by reducing delay and slew prediction errors by 3.16 × and 3.99 ×, respectively. RelFACT further demonstrates efficient adaptation to new process corners and a 45-nm PDK with limited target-domain post-training data. Beyond cell-level modeling, RelFACT delivers substantial gains in path-level aging-aware timing estimation, achieving 4.62% MAPE on unseen designs, reducing prediction error by 9.36 × over existing path-level predictors, and providing a 106.58 × speedup over aging-aware SPICE simulation. Leveraging its aging-aware timing predictions, RelFACT supports preliminary guardband-aware margin estimation and aged-critical path identification, providing guidance for timing screening and subsequent signoff verification.

items.abstract_text: High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) has become a fundamental component in high-performance computing, artificial intelligence acceleration, and networking, offering unmatched bandwidth and energy efficiency. However, the development of optimized HBM-based architectures is hindered by the proprietary nature of existing HBM controllers, which restricts configurability, transparency, and the ability to explore novel memory management strategies. This paper presents an open-source HBM controller designed to address these limitations by providing a configurable and flexible alternative to proprietary solutions. The proposed controller enables fine-grained memory command scheduling, dynamic bandwidth allocation, and workload-specific optimizations while maintaining compatibility with FPGA-based architectures. Moreover, we introduce a combined hardware/software approach to verification and validation, leveraging software-assisted profiling and debugging techniques to streamline performance analysis, correctness verification and integration in realistic settings. In addition to detailing the architecture and implementation, the paper discusses the challenges encountered during design and verification, highlighting key lessons learned that can aid practitioners working on similar projects. Hence, this work also serves as a reference for engineers and researchers aiming to build custom HBM controllers or optimize memory subsystems in FPGA-based designs. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed controller achieves competitive performance while providing the configurability and transparency required for advanced research and real-world deployment.

items.abstract_text: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) is fundamental for spectral analysis and popular in deep learning for efficient feature extraction. However, its performance hinges on memory access optimization where matrix transposition is crucial. Conventional CPU/GPU platforms typically implement FFT algorithms by relying on libraries or manually optimized code, yet remain constrained by inefficient data access patterns and high human-intervention dependency. Existing specialized transposition accelerators still exhibit limitations in multi-granular data support and leave room for further performance enhancement. In this paper, we present DFC-Trans, a dataflow-centric architecture for efficient matrix transposition, rather than a software-level optimization or GPU kernel tuning technique. Its key innovations are: (1) a hardware-based auto-blocking method which is tightly coupled with DMA(Direct Memory Access) for large-scale matrix transposition, which fundamentally eliminates software-driven chunking and distinguishes DFC-Trans from library-based (e.g., MKL, cuFFT) and manually optimized implementations; (2) a multi-granularity mapping method which supports the transposition of 16/32/64/128-bit data granularity, aligning with deep learning demands for mixed-precision quantization in FFT computations; (3) a register rotation structure that enables pipelined transposition through dynamic read/write switching in direction, achieving nearly 2× higher matrix transposition throughput compared to conventional methods. Experimental results demonstrate that DFC-Trans achieves up to 2.26× and 3.47× speedup over Intel MKL and NVIDIA cuFFT, respectively, for 128K-point FFT, while maintaining only 3.57% additional area overhead and 0.796% additional power consumption overhead of the single core.

items.abstract_text: HLS has become a promising approach for increasing logic design productivity. However, several challenges prevent HLS from being widely adopted by the industry. One of such challenges is the added abstraction layer, which hinders designers’ ability to efficiently estimate the current design’s Quality of Results (QoR) and consequently increases reliance on lengthy implementation flows in order to acquire such estimations. In recent years, neural network-based methodologies have shown the ability to provide accurate QoR estimation at the HLS level and consequently reduce the need for the complete implementation flow. While such approaches have shown promising results, most of the currently available datasets used for their training not only lack complete power, performance, and area (PPA) information, but also are limited in their optimization directive support, which reduces their usefulness in real-world designs and might prevent the discovery of efficient configurations in certain applications. Thus, we propose MLDHLS, a novel dataset containing 10 applications from standard HLS benchmarks suites with over 3000 fully implemented variations, including overlooked loop-related directives. Our experimental results show that such directives have significant impact on design space exploration (DSE): on average, 27.7% of the Pareto-optimal designs depend on loop merging or loop flattening to remain competitive in terms of performance and resource usage. Additionally, we present a case study that demonstrates our dataset in practice by training two state-of-the-art QoR estimator models which have better average accuracy than the standard Vitis HLS estimation.

items.title: スループットを毎時140枚から235枚へ、キヤノンが24年ぶりにArFドライ露光装置の新製品を投入
items.summary: キヤノンは、24年ぶりとなるArFドライ半導体露光装置の新製品「FPA-6300AS6」の受注を2026年12月上旬に開始する。実績のあるKrF露光装置のプラットフォームに、新開発のNA 0.93投影レンズとArF向け照明系を組み合わせ、スループットを従来の毎時140枚から235枚へ、重ね合わせ精度を15nmから4nmへ向上。メモリに加え、パワーデバイスやセンサ、化合物半導体、ウェハ貼り合わせなどへ用途を広げ、i線、KrF、ArF、ナノインプリントリソグラフィをそろえた前工程向けラインアップを構築する。

items.title: Z2RAM Claims SRAM Memory Speeds at Much Greater Density
items.summary: Pat Gelsinger is familiar with the graveyard of failed memory technologies. “We haven’t had a new memory for three decades,” says the former Intel CEO. SRAM, DRAM, and flash memory still dominate. Gelsinger has witnessed the rise and fall of several potential alternatives—most recently Optane, Intel’s failed attempt to create “universal memory.” But Gelsinger, who is now a general partner at venture capital firm Playground, believes that AI is forcing a rethink of the entire computing stack—and that memory is a key part of that shift. Playground has backed Nagare Labs, a company spun out of Georgia Tech working on a prototype memory technology called Z2RAM. Instead of replacing existing memory, Z2RAM will attempt to offer a new layer in the existing memory stack that could prove useful for AI workloads and for other tasks that benefit from low latencies. …

items.summary: JEDEC has unveiled the first specifications for DDR6 memory. Targeting over twice the bandwidth of DDR5, and with DIMMs 44% smaller, DDR6 is slated to be the biggest change in generations to the server memory standard The post JEDEC Previews DDR6 Memory Standard: 2.35x More Bandwidth, 44% Narrower DIMMs appeared first on ServeTheHome.
items.abstract_text: JEDEC has unveiled the first specifications for DDR6 memory. Targeting over twice the bandwidth of DDR5, and with DIMMs 44% smaller, DDR6 is slated to be the biggest change in generations to the server memory standard The post JEDEC Previews DDR6 Memory Standard: 2.35x More Bandwidth, 44% Narrower DIMMs appeared first on ServeTheHome.

points.label: 发生了什么
points.text: JEDEC 公布了下一代 DDR6 内存规格预览，拟提高单条内存模组的带宽，并推出更紧凑的模组。

points.label: 带宽从哪来
points.text: DDR6 拟把数据位宽从 64 位扩大到 96 位，同时提高每个引脚的传输速率。按报道的规格测算，DDR6-14400 单条带宽可达 172.8 GB/s，约为 DDR5-9200 的 2.35 倍。

points.label: 现在到哪一步
points.text: 目前处于规格预览阶段，带宽是按拟议规格计算的理论值。后续看正式规范何时发布，以及服务器平台和内存模组何时支持。

items.title: 2027年3月期上期の電子材料売り上げは35.8％増の1228億円、JSRが韓国MOR工場を年度内量産へ
items.summary: TECH+ 根据 JSR 说明会梳理了前后道材料业务和 EUV 金属氧化物光刻胶（MOR）供给。韩国工厂已竣工，报道所述投产目标为 2027 年初。
items.abstract_text: JSRの2027年3月期上期業績は、売上収益が前年同期比27.8％増の2651億円、コア営業利益が同130.7％増の563億円となり、いずれも半期ベースで2期連続の過去最高を更新した。成長をけん引した電子材料事業の売上収益は、AI関連を中心とする先端半導体需要を背景に同35.8％増の1228億円へ拡大。ArFフォトレジストやEUV用レジスト、多層材料に加え、低誘電樹脂材料や厚膜フォトレジストなどの先端パッケージング材料も伸長した。韓国で竣工した世界初のMOR量産工場は、2026年度末から2027年初頭に量産を開始する予定で、旺盛な需要に対応するため供給能力の増強を加速する。

items.abstract_text: 11月18日，迈特芯MEGA188（国产3D-TPU）端侧AI芯片成功点亮，跑通3B~120B主流模型，向量产迈出关键一步。

points.label: 现场进展
points.text: 爱集微报道，迈特芯在 11 月 18 日公布 MEGA188 回片点亮进展。厂商披露已完成上电、主机识别、核心算子和堆叠存储读写验证，并开展了开源模型端到端适配。

points.label: 技术路线
points.text: 这颗端侧推理协处理器将 3D DRAM 与分布式 TPU 集成，用较短的数据路径提高内存带宽，并通过高速接口与现有主控分工。

points.label: 现有证据
points.text: 目前可确认的是厂商披露的样片验证阶段。机型适配、模型吞吐与整机功耗还需在明确测试条件下比较，量产交付仍待后续披露。

items.news_genre: 专业媒体报道与行业观点
items.summary: 报道关注可拆卸光纤连接器如何影响硅光模块的组装、测试和维护，以及共封装与近封装光学面临的接口挑战。
items.abstract_text: Multiple designs are emerging for CPO and NPO, but standardization and high-volume manufacturing are still not ready. The post Detachable Fiber Connectors Pose New Challenges For Photonics appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.

points.label: 报道焦点
points.text: 光学引擎从面板移向交换芯片附近后，电信号走线可以缩短，但光纤要接入板内或封装。报道比较了固定尾纤和可拆卸连接器的取舍。

points.label: 工程价值
points.text: 可拆卸接口让芯片测试、系统组装和失效件更换更容易，尤其能减少带尾纤封装在托盘和自动搬运环节的约束。代价是连接器仍需要可靠的光学对准与锁定。

points.label: 规模化条件
points.text: 报道显示已有不同厂商方案。跨厂互换性、反复插拔后的损耗，以及与散热器和量产测试设备的兼容性，仍需共同验证。

items.abstract_text: Dynamic IR-drop induced by large-scale synchronous register switching has become a critical power-integrity challenge in modern high-performance ICs. Highly balanced clock networks can trigger simultaneous switching, causing transient current surges, localized voltage drops, timing-margin loss, and potential functional failures. Existing clock-skew and Clock Arrival Time (CAT) optimization methods mitigate this issue by expanding CAT distributions to desynchronize register switching, but recent reinforcement-learning-based approaches often rely on aggregated TNS-only timing observations, which obscure the directional timing impact of CAT perturbations. This work proposes Direction-Aware Timing Modeling (DATM) for reinforcement-learning-based CAT optimization. DATM explicitly separates launch-side and capture-side timing behaviors, resolving the directional ambiguity of TNS-only formulations and enabling the agent to better infer how CAT adjustments affect timing. The proposed framework is evaluated on seven 28nm designs with diverse timing and structural characteristics. Results show that DATM achieves substantially larger CAT-distribution expansion than the evaluated baselines while maintaining stable setup timing. A comprehensive timing-surrogate audit quantifies model fidelity, and CAT-transfer analysis shows that physical implementation preserves CAT ordering while attenuating target amplitude. Industrial validation with ICC2 and RedHawk further demonstrates an average peak-current reduction of 50.57% and dynamic IR-drop hotspot reduction, with limited timing degradation and average total-area and total-power overheads of 9.33% and 8.63%, respectively. These results establish DATM as a practical EDA method for power-integrity-aware physical design.

points.label: 主要发现
points.text: 在 7 个 28 nm 设计的 ICC2 与 RedHawk 评估中，平均峰值电流下降约 50.6%，总面积和总功耗分别平均增加约 9.3% 和 8.6%。

points.label: 研究问题
points.text: 寄存器集中翻转会造成瞬时供电压降。作者研究如何错开翻转时刻，同时维持建立时间裕量。

points.label: 怎么做
points.text: 在强化学习优化时钟到达时间时，分别描述发起端和捕获端的时序响应，让模型能区分同一次调整对不同路径的影响。

points.label: 适用范围
points.text: 结果来自给定设计和工具流程。布线实现保留了相对到达顺序，但实际调整幅度弱于目标。评估时应同时看瞬时电流、面积和总功耗。

event_briefs.reading_question: 把 DRAM 叠到逻辑裸片上，什么时候能看到实测？
event_briefs.what_happened: PFN 与 SEMIFIVE 公布 MN-Core L2000 联合开发方案，将 DRAM 垂直堆叠到逻辑裸片上。THE ELEC 跟进了方案，thebell 采访了 SEMIFIVE 负责人。计划于 2027 年第一季度提交流片。
event_briefs.why_it_matters: 缩短存储连接提供了增加带宽的路径，也让供电、热和堆叠良率成为同一设计问题。

items.summary: 当AI推理负载从云端走向边缘，VPU正跃升为算力体系“第三极”。集微咨询发布《AI产业系列报告之VPU芯片（2026）》，设行业概述、产业链分析、代表企业、未来展望四大篇章，系统梳理VPU技术演进、市场格局与国产化路径。报告指出，2026年一季度全球端侧与边缘AI芯片出货量同比增长45%，约为云端增速的四倍；瑞芯微、星宸科技、富瀚微、地平线、爱芯元智等国产厂商2026年上半年业绩集中兑现，边缘推理正成为AI芯片市场增量主战场。

items.abstract_text: Automated RF amplifier sizing is challenging because the design process is inherently hierarchical, the parameter space is high-dimensional and strongly coupled, and high-fidelity circuit simulation is expensive. Conventional optimization and reinforcement learning methods typically require many iterations and make limited use of RF domain knowledge, making them costly under tight simulation budgets. Large language models (LLMs) provide broad prior knowledge and reasoning capabilities, but are unreliable for direct numerical optimization. This paper presents RFAmpDesigner, a two-level optimization framework for automated schematic-level sizing of differential CMOS RF amplifiers. At the outer level, the circuit-parameter space is abstracted into a resource-allocation space, where LLMs make high-level allocation decisions and adjust them according to feedback from the inner level. At the inner level, RF design knowledge is used to decompose the flat sizing problem into a sequence of low-dimensional subproblems. Conventional optimizers then solve these subproblems to find circuit implementations consistent with the assigned resources. This structure allows numerical optimizers to focus on low-dimensional searches in the circuit-parameter space, while the LLM reasons and acts over a physically meaningful design space using simulation feedback. The main evaluation covers low-noise amplifier (LNA), driver amplifier (DA), and power amplifier (PA) designs within the target differential CMOS RF amplifier family. Experimental results show that it achieves a higher success rate under a limited simulation budget in both easy and hard regimes.

points.label: 主要发现
points.text: 作者评估了低噪声放大器、驱动放大器和功率放大器。在固定仿真预算下，容易和困难两类任务的求解成功率都有提高。

points.label: 研究问题
points.text: 差分 CMOS 射频放大器的参数相互牵制，直接让模型搜索大量连续参数会消耗许多电路仿真。

points.label: 怎么做
points.text: 由大模型根据反馈分配高层资源，再由传统优化器利用射频知识求解拆分后的低维参数问题。

points.label: 适用范围

items.title: Low-power Charge-domain In-FeRAM Computing
items.journal: National Science Review
items.venue_name: National Science Review
items.summary: The growing energy demands of large-scale model training and scientific computing have inspired interest in low-power computing paradigms. In-memory computing (IMC) reduces data movement overheads, but resistive devices suffer from high static power and Joule-heating. Here, we introduce a charge-domain computing paradigm based on Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 ferroelectric random-access memory (HZO FeRAM), in which computation is enabled by linear accumulation of charge associated with the anti-orientated ferroelectric polarization. We experimentally demonstrate this concept using a 16-kbit HZO FeRAM array, where key computational characteristics execute directly within this array, gradient calculations are performed with errors below 6×10 − 3, and in-memory difference operations solve partial differential equations with 98% accuracy after only 21 iterations. Hybrid FeRAM-digital training of a single-layer neural network for letter recognition is also shown. Furthermore, a 1 μm2 HZO ferroelectric capacitor exhibits a measured switching energy of only 1.66×10 − 12 J, implying the potential of HZO FeRAM for energy-efficient charge-domain computing.

items.abstract_text: Heterogeneous multicore embedded systems can handle complex tasks such as data collection, processing, and wireless communication. However, these systems often face constraints due to limited computational resources, requiring efficient task deployment strategies to manage dependent and real-time tasks. Despite advancements, existing methods rarely address the deployment of Imprecise Computation (IC) tasks on heterogeneous multicore platforms that utilize both Dynamic Voltage/Frequency Scaling (DVFS) and Dynamic Power Management (DPM). This article introduces a novel QoS-aware task deployment methodology to enhance the Quality of Service (QoS) under resource limitations. The proposed approach simultaneously optimizes frequency assignment, processor state transitions, task allocation, scheduling, and task execution cycle adjustments to maximize system QoS while adhering to time, energy, and dependency constraints. The problem is initially formulated as a Mixed Integer Non-Linear Programming (MINLP) model, then transformed into a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation to obtain optimal solutions. We developed a heuristic method with low computational complexity to address scalability challenges, employing problem decomposition and a greedy algorithm. The process operates in two stages: task allocation and frequency assignment, followed by task scheduling and cycle adjustment. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior system performance compared to existing approaches, particularly in QoS (41.30%), task schedulability (58.67%), and execution efficiency.

items.title: Effective Concurrent Attack Detection Framework through Laser Fault Informed Balanced Optical Neural Network Observation
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: Silicon Photonics-based AI Accelerators (SPAAs) have been considered as promising AI accelerators achieving high energy efficiency and low latency. While many researchers focus on improving SPAAs’ energy efficiency and latency, their physical security has only recently received attention. While it is essential to deliver strong optical neural network inferencing approaches, their success and adoption are predicated on their ability to deliver a secure execution environment. Towards this end, this article extends PrometheusFree to PrometheusFreev2 , an optical neural network framework that is capable of concurrent detection of laser fault injection attacks. This article first presents an illustrative threat of laser fault injection attacks on SPAAs, capable of subjecting the optical neural network to misclassifications. PrometheusFreev2 then addresses this threat by developing techniques for concurrent detection of the laser fault injection attacks. Furthermore, PrometheusFreev2 introduces an application of the Wavelength Division Perturbation (WDP) technique where wavelength-dependent Vector Matrix Multiplication (VMM) results are utilized to boost fault attack detection accuracy.
items.abstract_text: Silicon Photonics-based AI Accelerators (SPAAs) have been considered as promising AI accelerators achieving high energy efficiency and low latency. While many researchers focus on improving SPAAs’ energy efficiency and latency, their physical security has only recently received attention. While it is essential to deliver strong optical neural network inferencing approaches, their success and adoption are predicated on their ability to deliver a secure execution environment. Towards this end, this article extends PrometheusFree to PrometheusFreev2 , an optical neural network framework that is capable of concurrent detection of laser fault injection attacks. This article first presents an illustrative threat of laser fault injection attacks on SPAAs, capable of subjecting the optical neural network to misclassifications. PrometheusFreev2 then addresses this threat by developing techniques for concurrent detection of the laser fault injection attacks. Furthermore, PrometheusFreev2 introduces an application of the Wavelength Division Perturbation (WDP) technique where wavelength-dependent Vector Matrix Multiplication (VMM) results are utilized to boost fault attack detection accuracy. This article goes on to introduce a novel optical vulnerability that overpowers the PrometheusFree detection capability, the swapping attack that exploits an architectural vulnerability of SPAAs. To address this practical and critical attack, PrometheusFreev2 features a dummy padding technique which injects random values to weight matrices to improve attack detectability. Simulation results show that PrometheusFreev2 achieves over 92% attack-caused misprediction recall as the use of the WDP technique squashes the attack success rate by 31–47% on average by using three wavelengths. Compared with prior art, PrometheusFreev2 constricts the average attack success ratio to 0.030, yielding a 92.8–95.0% reduction. The experimental results confirm the superiority of the concurrent detection and the boost in attack detection abilities imparted by the WDP and the dummy padding approaches.

items.abstract_text: Leveraging the robustness of deep neural networks (DNNs), fixed-point mixed-precision models have effectively reduced hardware costs in edge in-memory accelerators. However, existing studies on multipliers are poorly suited to mixed-precision models. On the one hand, most of them employ fixed bit-widths or offer only limited configurations, lacking the fine-grained reconfigurability required by mixed-precision models. On the other hand, layers with smaller retained bit-widths can tolerate larger multiplication errors to achieve lower hardware costs, as the inaccurate bits are discarded. However, existing approximate multipliers cannot achieve low-cost dynamic error control, resulting in this optimization potential being wasted. To address these issues, this study proposes a fixed-point approximate multiplier with fine-grained reconfigurability. By breaking full multiplication into small 2-bit/3-bit operations and discarding non-critical ones selectively, the proposed multiplier ensures high hardware utilization across varying bit-widths while enabling low-cost fine-grained error control. Building on this multiplier, a DDR5-oriented near-memory accelerator architecture is proposed, incorporating extended dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) commands and semi-SIMD scheduling schemes. Compared to state-of-the-art processing-in-memory (PIM) architectures, the proposed architecture achieves a reduction of 40.8% in area, 16.3% in power consumption, and 6.5% in latency, respectively.

items.title: Flexible Error Modeling and Analysis of SiPho JTC Accelerators for CNNs
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: This article describes a system for modeling nonidealities in a silicon-photonic joint transform correlator (JTC) used as an accelerator for convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The system is used to determine which nonidealities have the greatest impact on end-to-end model accuracy, which helps determine what design choices can be made at the block and system level to improve performance. We create a digital twin of the on-chip 1D JTC using transfer functions fitted from simulations, then introduce a scalar α that mixes ideal and realized behaviors. We quantify the α-dependent model accuracy on CIFAR-10 and SNDR differences at both the joint power spectrum (JPS) and the JTC output. The framework allows quantification of block- and system-level sensitivities, informing design choices by isolating the accuracy bottlenecks within the system.

items.abstract_text: Link prediction for circuit completion is a crucial task in Electronic Design Automation (EDA), aiming to infer missing connections in incomplete circuits to accelerate design workflows and ensure Printed Circuit Board (PCB) reliability. However, due to the practical reality that circuit connectivity is defined by nets that connect specific pins of component instances, existing methods that rely on homogeneous representations and scalar shortest path distances collapse pin-level constraints into a single proximity signal. This collapse obscures component identities and pin semantics, and fails to capture long-range functional paths, which can slow design closure and potentially compromise PCB reliability by increasing the risk of electrically invalid links and subsequent rework. Addressing these challenges, we present a T ype-aware H eterogeneous G raph network for C ircuit link prediction ( THGC ), which enables accurate circuit link prediction by explicitly preserving component functional semantics and modeling type-aware dependencies. Specifically, THGC constructs a circuit-aware heterogeneous graph from netlists to preserve physical connectivity and component semantics, and refines representations through a multi-view encoder with Type-Aware Distance Encoding (TADE) to capture non-local dependencies. It then performs circuit-oriented link prediction using a heterogeneous graph network with dense convolutions and global sort pooling, optimized by a composite objective enforcing topological and semantic consistency, to predict electrically feasible missing connections for circuit completion. Comprehensive experiments are performed on 6,195 circuits collected from three benchmarks, and the results demonstrate that THGC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to a 47.51% relative improvement in terms of AUC. These results confirm that THGC effectively preserves component functional semantics and captures type-aware non-local dependencies for accurate circuit link prediction. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/THGC .

items.abstract_text: To address the growing computational demands of high-performance computing (HPC) and machine learning (ML) applications, Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) have transitioned from single-chip designs to multi-chip module (MCM) architectures, driven by manufacturing constraints. Simultaneously, GPUs are increasingly deployed in cloud environments to accelerate a wide range of applications for multiple users. Spatial multitasking, which allows multiple applications to run concurrently on a single GPU by executing them on different sets of streaming multiprocessors (SMs), offers an efficient method for sharing GPU resources. However, effectively supporting multitasking in the emerging MCM-GPU architecture presents a significant challenge that remains an open problem. This article presents the key observation that the placement of co-executing applications in MCM-GPUs plays a critical role in system performance. Specifically, for certain multiprogram workloads, co-executing applications achieve better performance when located on the same GPU chip to maximize memory bandwidth utilization. Conversely, other workloads benefit from being distributed across different GPU chips to mitigate memory contention. To address this, we propose a Location-Aware Scheduler (LA-Scheduler) that identifies application characteristics and makes optimized scheduling decisions. The LA-Scheduler performs lightweight workload classification using a k-means-based clustering method and applies multitasking scheduling rules during runtime to determine the optimal placement of applications within the MCM-GPU architecture. Evaluation results show that the proposed LA-Scheduler improves system throughput (STP) by an average of 38.67% compared with single-task operation. Compared with the traditional methods intra-chip scheduling and inter-chip scheduling, the system throughput is improved by an average of 13.51% and 7.14% respectively.

Chiplet-Escape requires all nets to be moved within each stage to ensure that the routing results of all nets at this stage are determined. Thus, the routing solution for the next stage can be accurately evaluated and decided based on the existing routing results of all nets, avoiding frequent rip-up and reroute operations caused by incomplete routing perspectives in traditional sequential routing methods and improving routing efficiency. Experimental results show that Chiplet-Escape can achieve high routability and a significant 88% runtime reduction compared with a state-of-the-art (SOTA) commercial router.

items.abstract_text: The exponential growth of Deep Neural Network (DNN) has precipitated a crisis in inter-chiplet communication, where traditional electrical interconnects struggle to meet the bandwidth density and energy efficiency requirements of massive-scale inference. While Silicon Photonics (SiPh) inherently offers the high bandwidth density and distance-independent energy efficiency required to transcend these metallic barriers, existing optical architectures remain fundamentally constrained by static topologies and prohibitive thermal reconfiguration latencies. This rigidity renders them ill-suited for the dynamic, phase-varying traffic patterns inherent in DNN workloads. To this end, we introduce APEX, a reconfigurable photonic-electrical interconnection architecture with dynamic logical topology reconfiguration algorithm engineered to resolve these scalability barriers. Central to APEX is a novel state-aware randomized greedy heuristic algorithm, which dynamically orchestrates wavelength allocation to adapt to the phase-varying traffic patterns inherent in DNN workloads. We validate the proposed approach against an optimal Integer Linear Programming (ILP) baseline, demonstrating that our linear time heuristic achieves near-optimal fidelity with a marginal energy overhead of only 5.6% in the early stages. Furthermore, it demonstrates robust scalability to synthesize full-layer network configurations where ILP solvers face combinatorial explosion. Evaluation across representative workloads reveals that APEX delivers a substantial leap in energy efficiency, achieving 0.69 pJ/bit for the BERT model—an approximate 41% reduction compared with Simba’s 1.17 pJ/bit.

Conventional SLM approaches rely on off-chip or software-only analytics, which lack on-die interpretability. We present X-OCTANE, an explainable on-chip telemetry-based anomaly notification engine. For the 7 nm ASAP technology, X-OCTANE achieves competitive anomaly detection performance with less than 0.50% CPU die area and 1.0% non-idle power overhead. In addition, X–OCTANE improves anomaly-driven diagnosis accuracy by over 7% on average. Experimental validation using the PAMPAR benchmark suite on two separate experimental platforms demonstrates enhanced anomaly detection and diagnosis through the proposed explainable feature-rank-and-selection method. X–OCTANE establishes a scalable and transparent foundation for on-chip SLM analytics, unifying detection fidelity with causal interpretability.

items.abstract_text: Small language models (SLMs) are increasingly deployed in resource-constrained environments, motivating the development of specialized accelerators. However, designing efficient SLM accelerators remains challenging due to diverse application requirements and complex interplay among architectural parameters and workload characteristics. This article proposes a closed-form analytical model that accurately evaluates latency and energy consumption for SLM accelerators across different dataflows and technology nodes (e.g., 28 nm CMOS and 7 nm FinFET). The model accounts for repeated data accesses, inter-processing element (PE) interconnections, and the energy costs of different DRAM operations, resulting in high simulation accuracy. Validation results show an average accuracy of 96.0% for latency, 96.8% for PE array energy, and 97.1% for DRAM energy. Using the proposed model, we conduct extensive design space exploration (DSE) and derive empirical formulas for optimized PE array sizes, along with analytical methods for memory capacities that minimize redundant memory accesses. We also examine optimized combinations of PE array size, memory capacity, bandwidth, and dataflow. Furthermore, we investigate area-constrained scenarios (2 mm 2 , 7 mm 2 , 30 mm 2 ) and provide guidelines for allocating computation and memory resources. Results show that the optimized PE array size is around 240× 240 for IS and OS, while WS requires at least 300× 300, but with lower memory demands. Under relaxed area constraints, at least 30 GB/s of bandwidth is needed for full area utilization, whereas strict area limits favor maximizing the PE array. Overall, this work provides practical guidelines for hardware parameter selection, enabling optimized SLM accelerator deployment across diverse applications.

items.title: LightSim: A Flexible, Fast Modeling Framework for Holistic Photonic Computing Systems
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: Photonic computing presents a promising alternative for accelerating neural network (NN) computation. However, the effective evaluation and design of these next-generation systems necessitate a thorough understanding of the complex interplay between their electronic and photonic components. In this work, we propose LightSim , a holistic and flexible modeling framework aimed at guiding the design and optimization of photonic computing systems. LightSim features a hierarchical and modular structure that provides users with a customizable and user-friendly interface. Its photonic-specific models offer in-depth insights into critical aspects like dataflow, mapping, and system performance. Furthermore, its fast modeling capability facilitates rapid exploration of the design space. LightSim supports co-design and fair architectural comparisons across all levels, thereby fostering the agile, iterative design process crucial for the development of high-performance and efficient photonic computing hardware. Validation across both incoherent and coherent photonic computing designs demonstrates a high correlation between our results and the reference data.

items.title: ASAPatch- Automated, Scalable And Programmable Framework For Post-Silicon Security Remediation
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: As Systems-on-Chip (SoCs) grow increasingly complex, the validation space expands exponentially, making fully-validated SoCs difficult to attain. This challenge is particularly critical for addressing security bugs related to hardware security. Recent research has shifted towards the possibility of remediating hardware security bugs in the field. In this article, our goal is to formalize this approach by introducing an automated, scalable, and programmable remediation framework. We present a novel architecture and corresponding programming languages designed for crafting remediation programs, along with an automated framework for “pragma”-based source code transformation and a compiler for the remediation programs. The remediation architecture demonstrated in this article can observe up to 143 Kbits and control up to 26 Kbits per mm 2 of logic area with the NanGate 45nm cell library, demonstrating its relevance to be used with modern SoCs.

items.title: SSR: A Swapping-Sweeping-and-Rewriting Optimizer for Quantum Circuit Transformation
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: Quantum circuit transformation (QCT), necessary for adapting any quantum circuit to the qubit connectivity constraints of the NISQ device, often introduces numerous additional SWAP gates into the original circuit, increasing the circuit depth and thus reducing the success rate of computation. To minimize the depth of QCT circuits, we propose a Swapping-Sweeping-and-Rewriting optimizer. This optimizer rearranges the circuit based on generalized gate commutation rules via a genetic algorithm, extracts subcircuits consisting of CNOT gates using a circuit sweeping technique, and rewrites each subcircuit with a functionally equivalent and depth-optimal circuit generated by an SAT solver. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared with existing post-QCT optimization approaches such as CBIR and Q-Synth, SSR achieves superior performance, improving circuit depth by up to 29.04% and 16.59% on average across all benchmark circuits, whereas the depth reduction of CBIR and Q-Synth are, respectively, 12.17% and 16.63% at most and 6.45% and -0.53% on average on the same benchmarks.

items.abstract_text: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables secure computation directly over encrypted data, making it highly valuable for domains such as healthcare, finance, and cloud services. However, its deployment is still constrained by immense computational overheads and critical memory bandwidth limitations, particularly in CKKS bootstrapping and the Number Theoretic Transform (NTT). While recent hardware accelerators have improved arithmetic throughput, they remain constrained by inefficient memory transfers and off-chip communication overhead. To overcome these limitations, we introduce OptoLink , a photonic interconnect architecture at the chiplet scale. By exploiting Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) and Space Division Multiplexing (SDM), OptoLink delivers ultra-high throughput and low-latency data transfer. Our design achieves up to 1.6 TB/s of bandwidth across 128 optical channels, representing a 300× latency reduction compared with conventional electronic network. In addition, OptoLink provides efficient broadcast and multicast capabilities, significantly reducing redundant data movement. Using an extended FHE simulation framework, we show that OptoLink improves CKKS bootstrapping throughput by up to 11× on HEAX and 1.6× on F1 and ARK, while reducing memory transfer delays by orders of magnitude. Furthermore, encrypted machine learning workloads, including logistic regression training and ResNet-20 inference, benefit from higher throughput and alleviated bandwidth pressure, demonstrating the potential of OptoLink to enable practical large-scale FHE acceleration.

items.abstract_text: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) is transforming computing paradigms while introducing new challenges in hardware security vulnerability detection. Existing hardware performance counter (HPC)-based detectors demonstrate high efficacy for conventional applications (e.g., editing Office files, and playing videos) as well as web-accessible LLMs; however, our novel observation reveals that locally deployed large-scale LLMs exhibit access patterns with striking similarity to Spectre attacks. This similarity causes a dramatic deterioration in attack detection accuracy, plummeting from 99.86% to just 66.16% for DeepSeek-7b. To effectively mitigate detection performance degradation, we propose for the first time, LLMsafe-Spectre, a novel intelligent HPC event selection methodology designed for efficient Spectre attack detection in LLM environments. LLMsafe-Spectre is composed of two phases: (1) AI-assisted clustering of HPC events to efficiently narrow the search space, (2) ANOVA-based statistical analysis of inner-group and inter-group variances to pick out Top-K Spectre attack-LLMs discriminative events under limited registers in processors. This approach uniquely addresses the interference caused by LLM access while maintaining detection robustness. We comprehensively evaluate LLMsafe-Spectre across diverse Spectre variants, hardware architectures, web accessible LLMs and locally deployed large-scale LLMs scaling up from 1.5b to 14b. Experimental results demonstrate that our novel solution achieves superior detection accuracy up to 99.91% on average of scaling LLMs, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art approaches.

items.abstract_text: Large language models (LLMs) have great potential to enhance productivity in many disciplines, such as software engineering. However, it is unclear to what extent they can assist in the design process of electronic circuits. This article focuses on the application of LLMs to switched-mode power supply (SMPS) design for printed circuit boards (PCBs). We present multiple LLM-based workflows that combine reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a custom toolkit that enables the LLM to interact with the SPICE circuit simulator to receive physical feedback. Two benchmark experiments are presented to analyze the performance of LLM-based assistants on various design tasks. These include parameter tuning and topology adaption, as well as design optimization of SMPS circuits through optimal catalogue component selection to maximize circuit efficiency or balance multiple objectives like size, ripple, and component loss. Experiment results show that SPICE simulation feedback and current LLM advancements, such as reasoning, significantly increase the solve rate on 269 manually created benchmark tasks from 15% to 91%. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that most parameter tuning design tasks can be solved, while limits remain for certain topology adaption and multi-objective optimization tasks. Our experiments offer insights for improving current concepts, for example by adapting text-based circuit representations.

Traditional logic locking techniques are vulnerable to the satisfiability (SAT)-based attack method, also known as SAT attack, which decrypts circuits by quickly isolating incorrect keys. Consequently, recent methods employ one-point functions, such as AND-trees, in encrypted circuits to ensure that only one incorrect key is pruned per SAT attack iteration, thereby slowing decryption exponentially. However, these defense methods result in minimal output corruption. Subsequently, solutions like CAS-Lock have emerged, designed to enhance SAT attack resilience and maintain high output corruption, but they remain susceptible to structural attacks. In this work, we introduce the Big+little trees encryption framework to improve output corruption and strengthen resilience against SAT attacks, while effectively concealing structural vulnerabilities to prevent structural attacks. Experimental results show that our method maintains resilience against SAT, Valkyrie, KRATT, and FALL attacks while ensuring significant output corruption.

items.venue_name: arXiv
items.summary: Large language models have improved Verilog generation, yet functional correctness remains difficult to optimize because simulation commonly provides a coarse module-level pass/fail outcome. Such feedback discards useful evidence from partially correct RTL modules and cannot determine whether a source statement is functionally responsible for an observed output behavior. We present a new method named Causal Signal Credit Assignment (CSCA), which is a counterfactual preference-optimization framework for Verilog generation. CSCA first performs continuous signal-level behavioral verification on sampled candidate modules. It then locates output-driving assignment spans and applies five interventions while holding the remaining module and testbench fixed. The resulting changes in signal-level errors are combined with behavioral agreement to form a continuous statement credit, which is mapped to response-token weights for strict weighted direct preference optimization. This enables CSCA to learn from locally supported statements without uniformly reinforcing an otherwise incorrect response. items.abstract_text: With the growing interest in using AI (Artificial Intelligence) for RTL (Register-Transfer Level) hardware development, robust and comprehensive verification has become more important than ever. As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly assist in creating and modifying RTL designs, ensuring that these changes preserve existing functionality is paramount for building trust in AI-driven workflows. We present SVApshot, a fully automated framework that leverages LLMs to generate and systematically attempt to correct SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) for RTL modules, completely removing the human from the generation loop. SVApshot introduces a novel snapshot methodology that captures the current functionality of a design as a comprehensive set of formal assertions, creating a regression suite for validating future changes--whether made by humans or AI. The framework features automated duplicate detection, assertion set expansion, and iterative repair of failing assertions using LLM-guided debugging with formal verification feedback. Our experimental evaluation across diverse RTL modules demonstrates high coverage for complex modules, with successful detection of both manually-injected and AI-introduced bugs. Additionally, this framework opens the door for automatic generation of formal testbenches to benchmark LLMs for hardware design, moving beyond binary pass/fail metrics towards nuanced assertion-based scoring.

items.abstract_text: This paper introduces a budget-aware, multi-objective framework (called PRISM) for RTL optimization that improves power, performance, and area (PPA) while sharply limiting expensive commercial synthesis tool calls. Starting from a synthesizable baseline and functional testbench, the method iterates through LLM-driven rewrite generation, fast compile/simulation equivalence filtering, low-cost proxy feature extraction, and selective commercial synthesis tool (Synopsys Design Compiler (DC)) evaluation. To prioritize which candidates deserve high-quality synthesis, we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes, and combine ensemble uncertainty with a diversity-aware acquisition rule to avoid early bias and redundant evaluations. A key advantage is that PRISM maintains a best-tradeoff set G of non-dominated designs throughout the run: G preserves the best solutions found so far, is fed back into generation and refinement, and enables consistent, cumulative improvements rather than repeatedly restarting from the baseline. Across RTLLM v2.0 modules, the approach consistently yields post-synthesis gains under fixed commercial synthesis tool call budgets, and ablations confirm that reward-guided selection and candidate dropping are central to sample-efficient progress. PRISM efficacy is evaluated across multiple technology nodes (7 nm, 15 nm, and 45 nm) using identical pipelines without retraining.

items.title: CU-3D: A Scalable Legality-Aware RTL-to-GDS Flow for 3D-IC Physical Design
items.venue_name: arXiv
items.summary: Face-to-face (F2F) hybrid bonds shorten interdie connections, but data, clock, and power-grid (PG) connections must be realized together. CU-3D is a RTL-to-GDS physical design flow based on commercial EDA tools. It derives role-compatible hybrid-bond (HB) sites from a 17-metal ASAP7-based technology model, complete HB footprints, and constructed PG geometry. To coordinate partitioning with placement flexibility, Scaled refines an inherited 2D placement, whereas Fresh places the receiving die first and uses its pin locations and clock loads to guide placement of the other die. Data and clock HB assignments are jointly optimized while retaining alternative data sites and reserving capacity for subsequent PG assignment. The selected HB sites and stacks are preserved during 3D clock-tree synthesis, supply-aware cell insertion, and routing. Across eleven designs, including a 133-macro processor, the flow achieves zero backend DRC violations and passes signal-connectivity checks. Nine paired designs admit lower-footprint, lower-power implementations; four improve setup WNS. On JPEG, early joint planning gains 87 ps and mobility-aware partitioning gains 346 ps. Path analysis explains why

items.abstract_text: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) are rapidly increasing in scale and routing complexity, driven by photonic computing, optical switching, programmable interferometer meshes, wavelength-routed optical networks-on-chip, and chip-to-chip optical interconnects. Manual waveguide planning becomes increasingly impractical as designs approach hundreds to thousands of photonic components, because routing must satisfy geometric, optical, electrical, and manufacturing constraints. This paper presents Photonic Routing Optimization and Placement Engine (PROPEL) , a memory-driven, native-accelerated adaptive vector-flow-field routing framework with process-aware waveguide generation for large-scale PIC physical design. PROPEL builds a routing kernel based on a bounded vector-flow-field algorithm and design-rule checking (DRC) validation. The same kernel supports passive optical routing, active optical–electrical routing, and topology-driven net assignment. C++ accelerates computationally intensive field and routing calculations, while Python performs detailed DRC replay, legality checking, route commitment, and GDSFactory-based geometry generation. Compared with state-of-the-art routing solutions, PROPEL is faster on 17 of 18 shared passive-routing cases, with a median speedup of 2.6 × and a geometric-mean speedup of 2.5 ×, while maintaining zero final design-rule violations. PROPEL also supports active optical–electrical routing, topology-driven net assignment, length, delay, and optical-path-length matching, process-map-aware waveguide generation, route-memory reuse, selective rip-up/reroute, and Graphic Data System (GDSII)-level legality replay. These capabilities address heterogeneous PIC layouts where optical, electrical, process, topology, matching, and manufacturability constraints must be handled together. In incremental-layout experiments, PROPEL restores more than 95% of previously verified routes after small local component movements and reroutes only the affected subset, reducing modified-design routing from tens or hundreds of seconds to a few seconds while maintaining zero final design-rule violations.

items.abstract_text: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Recovering high-level RTL from such representations therefore helps engineers understand a circuit's functionality and enables RTL rewriting and resynthesis. A plausible function model is also insufficient unless the generated RTL is equivalent to the original circuit for all input combinations. In this paper, we present RTLREX, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools for function recovery, RTL generation, independent verification, and cost-guided rewriting. Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit. The LLM uses tool feedback to select further analyses, revise candidate RTL, and propose syntax-cost reductions. Experiments on 30 benchmarks from Problem A of the ICCAD 2022 CAD Contest show that RTLREX recovers equivalent high-level RTL for all benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art method WolFEx in recovery coverage. On benchmarks recovered by both methods, RTLREX reduces mean syntax cost by 20.5% relative to WolFEx. On complete truth-table benchmarks from the IWLS 2026 Contest, our framework reduces mean syntax cost by 95.7% relative to an LLM agent baseline on the benchmarks validated by both methods.

items.abstract_text: High-level synthesis (HLS) can translate C/C++ kernels into register-transfer level (RTL) designs, yet generating high-quality hardware still relies heavily on manual pragma tuning and repeated synthesis evaluation. We propose AutoC2V, a C++-to-Verilog generation framework driven by real synthesis feedback that enables large language models (LLMs) to directly generate RTL with improved quality of results (QoR) from synthesizable C++ kernels. We construct training data from real synthesis results, including synthesizable C++ source code, the corresponding Verilog RTL, QoR metrics, and optimization objectives. Using this dataset, we align the model toward synthesis-aware RTL generation through Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To reduce the high cost of repeatedly invoking real synthesis during GRPO, we design the QoR Prediction Reward Model (QoR RM), which predicts latency and resource metrics by encoding RTL into long-context semantic representations, thereby providing low-cost and continuous QoR reward signals for policy optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that AutoC2V not only substantially improves RTL functional pass rates, but also achieves superior latency and resource optimization compared to the unfine-tuned base model, representative HLS optimization approaches (HLSPilot, LLM-DSE, and AutoDSE), and advanced general-purpose commercial models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek v4 Pro, and GLM-5.2). These results indicate that combining real synthesis data with efficient QoR reward modeling can further improve the ability of LLMs to generate high-quality RTL.

items.abstract_text: Structural obfuscation has been a widely used hardware security technique that is used to transform the internal structure of a high-level synthesis (HLS) digital signal processing (DSP) intellectual property (IP) design such that it becomes unobvious and obscure. The intent is to thwart deobfuscation/reverse-engineering (RE) attempts. These transformations in structurally obfuscated DSP designs are elusive and non-intuitive, making them arduous to identify and detect from an attacker's perspective. In this article, we for the first time, present a novel strategy for detecting structural obfuscation in HLS based DSP designs using machine learning (ML) frameworks. This article presents a novel technique called ‘DECODE’ : DE tecting Stru C tural O bfuscation in HLS based D SP Designs using Machine L E arning Framework . The presented approach introduces a set of unique/distinct features that can successfully classify between structurally obfuscated HLS DSP designs and its non-obfuscated versions. The article also presents a novel ML database consisting of several instances of structurally obfuscated and un-obfuscated DSP HLS designs that can be fed into our ML framework (logistic regression and random forest classifier). Results of the proposed approach revealed successful detection of structurally obfuscated DSP designs with high accuracy.

items.title: A CNN-Based Technique to Assist Layout-to-Generator Conversion for Analog Circuits
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: We propose a technique to assist in converting a reference layout of an analog circuit into the procedural layout generator by efficiently reusing available generators for sub-cell creation. The proposed convolutional neural network (CNN) model automatically detects sub-cells that can be generated by available generator scripts in the library, and suggests using them in the hierarchically correct places of the generator software. In experiments, the CNN model examined sub-cells of a high-speed wireline receiver that has a total of 4,885 sub-cell instances including 145 different sub-cell designs. The CNN model classified the sub-cell instances into 51 generatable and one not-generatable classes. One not-generatable class indicates that no available generator can generate the classified sub-cell. The CNN model achieved 99.3% precision in examining the 145 different sub-cell designs. The CNN model greatly reduced the examination time to 18 seconds from 88 minutes required in manual examination. Also, the proposed CNN model could correctly classify unfamiliar sub-cells that are very different from the training dataset.

items.title: ModelAuflow: A Highly Scaffolded LLM-Orchestrated Framework for RF Passive Device Parameter Extraction
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: Accurate parameter extraction for RF passive devices is a critical step in semiconductor design because compact models directly determine the reliability of circuit simulation. Conventional extraction remains highly iterative and depends on substantial expert intervention for parameter grouping, optimizer selection, range adjustment, and curve-quality assessment. This article presents ModelAuflow, a highly scaffolded LLM-orchestrated framework for RF passive-device parameter extraction. items.abstract_text: Accurate parameter extraction for RF passive devices is a critical step in semiconductor design because compact models directly determine the reliability of circuit simulation. Conventional extraction remains highly iterative and depends on substantial expert intervention for parameter grouping, optimizer selection, range adjustment, and curve-quality assessment. This article presents ModelAuflow, a highly scaffolded LLM-orchestrated framework for RF passive-device parameter extraction. The framework combines structured LLM reasoning with deterministic strategy conversion so that high-level optimization decisions are mapped into executable commands for commercial extraction tools. To improve convergence efficiency, the system integrates sensitivity-aware parameter filtering, historical self-reflection, and a classification knowledge base. Across the evaluated RF passive-device cases, the framework reduced the RMSE of a complex inductor below 3.5%, a capacitor below 2%, and a resistor below 1%. Under favorable initial conditions, the shortest successful extraction required 134 seconds and one optimization attempt. These results indicate that schema-constrained LLM orchestration can substantially reduce continuous manual intervention while maintaining accurate extraction for the evaluated RF passive-device workflows.

items.abstract_text: Network-on-Chip (NoC)-based Multi-Processor Systems-on-Chip (MPSoCs) are increasingly required to execute multiple real-time applications simultaneously. Each application is modelled as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of dependent tasks, and the platform supports Dynamic Voltage and Frequency Scaling (DVFS). While existing task-mapping methods address energy efficiency, reliability, and network contention for a single DAG, they do not capture the inter-DAG contention that arises when communication flows from independent applications compete for shared NoC links, nor the cross-DAG resource sharing that forces tasks from different applications to be serialised on the same Processing Element (PE). In this paper, we formulate the multi-DAG contention- and reliability-aware task mapping problem as a Mixed-Integer Nonlinear Program (MINLP). To handle the quartic constraint growth that renders exact solvers impractical for realistic workloads, we propose MERC , a polynomial-time heuristic for the multi-DAG setting. MERC performs (i) global task placement with cross-DAG load balancing and (ii) joint V/F selection and edge scheduling via greedy list scheduling with worst-case contention slack, optionally followed by a contention refinement phase that computes precise inter-DAG slack and exploits recovered time for frequency reduction. Extensive simulations on random DAGs over 2 × 2 to 6 × 6 mesh topologies demonstrate that MERC provides the best multi-objective balance among all compared methods: 60% lower energy than round-robin placement, 10– \(56\% \) lower energy than an adapted multi-DTG heuristic (SAFLA-N), robust feasibility where independent single-DAG scheduling collapses at scale, and polynomial-time execution that is two orders of magnitude faster than a metaheuristic baseline. A cycle-accurate Noxim cross-check supports the reserved-path delay model under concurrent DAG traffic, and a case study of three edge applications confirms the same multi-objective reading.

items.abstract_text: Analog compute-in-memory (CIM) enables energy-efficient AI inference by performing in-situ matrix multiplication. The growing demand for deploying larger models motivates chiplet integration to expand CIM capacity. However, simulation abstractions based on local operator costs and aggregate communication metrics obscure the impact of weight-mapping topology when CIM system scales up. We develop a phase analysis that quantifies how strongly mapping topology affects system performance across hardware configurations and how mapping optimization translates into latency gains. To evaluate and exploit this design space, we present Isobar, a simulation platform integrating CIM decompositions, heterogeneous execution, and resource modeling. Validated against silicon measurements and cycle-accurate simulation, Isobar provides reliable cost estimates that enable effective mapping search across model and hardware configurations. For Gemma-7B prefill, Isobar-guided mapping reduces communication time by 23.3% and end-to-end latency by 18.6% relative to the strongest baseline. items.title: Hybrid integration of a SESAM with a silicon nitride photonic integrated circuit
items.venue_name: arXiv
items.summary: The realization of high-performance femtosecond lasers on photonic integrated circuits (PICs) requires robust, low-loss coupling between a saturable absorber and a photonic waveguide. In this work, we demonstrate the hybrid integration of a semiconductor saturable absorber mirror (SESAM) with a silicon nitride (SiN) PIC by micro-assembly. This micro-assembly strategy transfers the non-linear functionality of the absorber onto the PIC. We characterize the linear and non-linear performance of an unbonded SESAM and of a SESAM bonded to inverse-tapered SiN waveguides. At 1560~nm, the bonded device shows a waveguide-coupled modulation depth of 5.2\%, a maximum reflectivity of 37.2\%, and a saturation fluence of 47~\textmu J/cm$^2$. This work demonstrates that SESAMs can be integrated directly onto silicon nitride-based PIC platforms and provides a pathway towards fully integrated, self-starting, chip-scale ultrafast lasers.

items.abstract_text: Circuit design for analog integrated circuits (ICs) is challenging because circuit topology, device sizing, and circuit performance are tightly coupled. Existing large language model (LLM)-based methods either rely on inference-time correction around frozen models or train on limited circuit types without directly using simulation outcomes as training signals. A key bottleneck is that existing datasets do not provide sufficient task information for training LLMs on end-to-end specification-conditioned design. To fill this gap, we first construct a large-scale simulation-grounded dataset with 8,626 design tasks across 10 different types of analog circuits, where each task includes a textual description, labeled I/O ports, loading condition, target specifications, a testbench, and a reference netlist. Using this dataset, we present SAFTAC, a simulation-augmented fine-tuning framework that trains LLMs to generate and revise analog circuit design. SAFTAC combines three-stage supervised fine-tuning, which progressively builds the capabilities required for analog circuit design and feedback-guided correction, with simulation feedback-augmented reinforcement fine-tuning, which further optimizes models using simulation-grounded rewards. We evaluate SAFTAC under single-pass generation and two-pass generation with simulation feedback, showing improvements over the strongest closed-source LLM by 15.9% and 7.8%, respectively.

items.title: Iteration-Free Candidate Pruning and an Index-Domain VLSI Architecture for Sort-Free MIMO Box Decoding up to 1024-QAM
items.venue_name: arXiv
items.summary: Wi-Fi~7 and 5G NR use constellations up to $4096$-QAM and $1024$-QAM at multi-gigabit peak rates. The MIMO detector must sustain these rates at a low cost. Linear MMSE detection meets these rates at low cost but loses several dB in SNR. $K$-Best detection recovers this loss, but its per-layer sorting grows with the modulation order and needs large sorting networks or deep pipelines at these rates. Box Decoding is a sort-free tree-search detector whose complexity does not depend on the QAM order, and its deterministic pruning keeps the cost fixed as the MIMO size grows. Single-step candidate pruning (SCP) is fully parallel but less accurate, while iterative candidate pruning (ICP) is more accurate, but its selection loop costs either throughput or area. This paper proposes Max-Min-Exchange Candidate Pruning (MMECP), which replaces the selection loop of ICP with a single max-min exchange without a feedback path and keeps \mbox{near-$K$-Best} performance. The paper also presents a VLSI architecture that represents each candidate by its integer constellation index, so that candidates and their distances are obtained by bit selection instead of operations on symbol values. items.abstract_text: Wi-Fi~7 and 5G NR use constellations up to $4096$-QAM and $1024$-QAM at multi-gigabit peak rates. The MIMO detector must sustain these rates at a low cost. Linear MMSE detection meets these rates at low cost but loses several dB in SNR. $K$-Best detection recovers this loss, but its per-layer sorting grows with the modulation order and needs large sorting networks or deep pipelines at these rates. Box Decoding is a sort-free tree-search detector whose complexity does not depend on the QAM order, and its deterministic pruning keeps the cost fixed as the MIMO size grows. Single-step candidate pruning (SCP) is fully parallel but less accurate, while iterative candidate pruning (ICP) is more accurate, but its selection loop costs either throughput or area. This paper proposes Max-Min-Exchange Candidate Pruning (MMECP), which replaces the selection loop of ICP with a single max-min exchange without a feedback path and keeps \mbox{near-$K$-Best} performance. The paper also presents a VLSI architecture that represents each candidate by its integer constellation index, so that candidates and their distances are obtained by bit selection instead of operations on symbol values. A $4\times4$ detector synthesized in TSMC $16$\,nm detects one vector per cycle at $1$\,GHz for $64$- to $1024$-QAM and produces up to $40$\,Gb/s, while its gate count grows by $63\%$ over this range. Its normalized hardware efficiency is $2.3\times$, $12\times$ and $14\times$ that of the best compared hard-output detector at $64$-, $256$- and $1024$-QAM.

items.abstract_text: Early access to accurate congestion information can effectively optimize the physical design flow of modern very large scale integration (VLSI) circuits. Existing unimodal models suffer from limited feature utilization and insufficient prediction accuracy, while current multimodal approaches typically involve large parameter sizes, slow inference, and high computational complexity, making them difficult to apply in time-critical tasks. To address these limitations, we propose CGNet, a novel lightweight multimodal model for congestion prediction that simultaneously processes feature maps and heterogeneous graphs. To enable efficient feature fusion without significantly increasing model complexity, we incorporate a cross-stitch module. Furthermore, we propose a heterogeneous graph compression method that significantly simplifies the graph structure, thereby reducing the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous graphs and improving the prediction speed of the model. Additionally, we design a composite loss function that jointly captures global structures and local details. For a more comprehensive evaluation, we propose a localized metric, intersection over union (IOU), and integrate the predicted congestion maps into the downstream design rule check (DRC) violation prediction task. Experimental results in the CircuitNet-N28 dataset demonstrate that CGNet consistently outperforms the best-performing model in both prediction accuracy and prediction speed.

items.title: EnVector: Encoding using Pattern based Vectors for Energy Efficient Non-Volatile Main Memories
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: Non-Volatile Memories (NVMs) provide new opportunities for scalable main memory due to their great scalability and other favorable attributes. However, considering their inherent write defects (long latency, high energy consumption), combined with their limited write endurance, their inclusion into the memory hierarchy requires careful handling. This not only shortens the lifespan of NVMs but also renders them as an expensive option. In this work, we propose a technique called EnVector that exploits the intrinsic uniformity in memory data to encode the cacheline data before the memory write takes place. By using well-designed fixed vectors, it minimizes the variation between the incoming and the stored data. This saves a lot of possible bit flips, reducing the likelihood of any memory failure from an excessive number of writes. Consequently, improving performance and lowering latency and energy requirements. We empirically demonstrated that EnVector upgrades the NVM lifetime by 37% and accelerates its performance by 15% over the baseline.

items.title: DSETune: An Efficient Design Space Exploration Approach for Logic Synthesis
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: As a critical step in the chip design flow, logic synthesis generates target circuits by iteratively applying various optimization algorithms. In practical applications, engineers must adjust the combination of optimization algorithms based on expert knowledge to meet diverse design requirements. However, existing approaches lack a multi-objective optimization perspective and exhibit poor solving efficiency. In light of this, we propose DSETune, the first synthesis flow search approach capable of thoroughly exploring the design space. First, a discrete particle swarm optimization algorithm incorporating genetic operators significantly improves search efficiency of design space. Second, a domain knowledge-driven initialization strategy of particles accelerates convergence and enhances solution quality. Finally, an update mechanism integrating a customized elite strategy enables more comprehensive solution space exploration, yielding superior Pareto-optimal solutions. items.title: CHARIOT: A Communication-Aware Exploration Framework for 2.5D/3D Silicon Interposer Design
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems

items.title: Path Delay Faults Through Transition Faults with High Functional Switching Activities
items.journal: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.venue_name: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
items.summary: Chip aging results in defects that are initially likely to appear as small delay defects. Path delay faults are used for detecting small delay defects. Because of the number of paths, path selection procedures are used for identifying a subset of path delay faults that are important to detect. A recent path selection procedure addresses small delay defects that are likely to occur because of chip aging. The procedure identifies a set of functionally possible path delay faults, from which it selects a subset based on an aging aware metric. This article studies this problem when the requirement for the path delay faults to be functionally possible is removed. The problem becomes that of selecting path delay faults through the largest numbers of transition faults with the highest susceptibilities to aging, and performing test generation for the selected path delay faults. Experimental results of path selection and test generation for benchmark circuits demonstrate the effectiveness of the procedures, and the differences from the case where the path delay faults are required to be functionally possible.
