In this work, we present BACON, a hardware collision detection framework that generates high-precision, high-efficiency accelerators for rigid-body robots with arbitrary degrees of freedom and structures. BACON streamlines the design process with a parameterized template that can be rapidly tuned for new scenarios. Our framework introduces three key innovations: a dynamic-static decoupled design for efficient detection in highly dynamic environments; a Monte Carlo tree search-based optimization strategy that automatically tailors parameters for diverse robotic morphologies and scenarios; and a body-aware scheduler that balances workloads and eliminates redundant computations via early exit mechanisms. When validated on six robotic systems and implemented on Xilinx VCU118 and ZU15EG FPGA, BACON demonstrates an average speedup of 17.85× over CPUs and 2.62× over GPUs in collision detection tasks, highlighting its capability to enable scalable, high-performance robotic accelerators for a new generation of agile robotic systems.

items.abstract_text: The memristor crossbar array is a promising circuit architecture of neuromorphic chips, which, however, has signal integrity issues such as delays, crosstalk, and voltage drop due to parasitic effects during signal transmission. This paper presents an efficient and high-precision training-inference strategy for solving these issues, with a particular focus on integrating signal distortion analysis for memristor crossbar arrays. A fast partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC)-based circuit modeling method is introduced, which significantly improves the simulation speed of large-scale arrays by leveraging matrix decomposition and sparse matrix techniques. The impact of parasitic effects on the readout signal is analyzed, leading to the development of an improved read scheme that enables accurate and rapid signal analysis based on quasi-steady-state arrival time. Additionally, a novel training method is proposed that incorporates an unstructured dynamic pruning strategy and parasitic effect correction, addressing the influence of data patterns on parasitic paths and signal distortion, while minimizing accuracy loss in hardware deployment. The application of the proposed method in an image classification task validates its ability to maintain high precision, stability, and effectiveness, offering valuable insights for the rapid analysis and efficient hardware deployment of large-scale memristor crossbar arrays.

items.title: A Novel Embedded Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Nonisothermal Current Discretization of 3-D Semiconductor Devices
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: We present a stable embedded discontinuous Galerkin (EDG) method for scalable electrothermal simulation of 3D semiconductor devices. The framework extends the robust hybridized discontinuous Galerkin method developed for purely electric paradigm to resolve fully coupled electrothermal drift-diffusion equations, addressing a critical gap in existing harmonic-averaging formulations that lack non-isothermal current modeling. It is believed that for the first time, we derive a consistent discretization of thermally coupled current terms within the EDG scheme, ensuring stability under strong convection and Joule heating. A parallel solver is further developed and implemented via the JAUMIN framework using domain decomposition, enabling extreme-scale 3D simulations of semiconductor devices. The validations on p-n junctions, NLDMOSFET and multi-finger FinFET demonstrate superior Newton convergence and comparable accuracy in comparison with that of commercial software COMSOL. It can achieve 79.2% strong scaling efficiency (20×cores) and 59.0% weak scaling efficiency (8× problem size) in the 8-Finger FinFET electrothermal simulations.

items.title: Low-Cost Testing of 2.4 GHz Receiver on Standard Digital ATE: Practical Implementation
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: In this paper, we present the implementation of a low-cost solution for the test of 2.4GHz receivers on a standard Automatic test Equipment (ATE). The approach relies on the use of a customized binary signal generated by a digital tester channel as the test stimulus. This binary signal is specifically defined such that it presents similar spectral characteristics in the frequency band of the Device Under Test (DUT) as a conventional analog test stimulus generated by an RF tester channel. Dedicated scripts are developed that permit (i) the selection of an appropriate sampling frequency for the digital channel to avoid spectral corruption in the DUT frequency band, and (ii) the automatic conversion of the I/Q data computed by the ATE in case of a conventional RF stimulus into a binary sequence to be stored in the vector memory of the digital tester channel. Experimental results are provided that validate the efficiency of the proposed solution, under different communication protocols (ZigBee and Bluetooth Low Energy) and signal strengths.

items.abstract_text: Video transformers (VidTs) have demonstrated powerful spatio-temporal modelling capabilities in various video understanding tasks. However, their practical deployment remains constrained by high computational and memory overheads, primarily caused by the quadratic complexity of spatio-temporal self-attention and the intensive demands of processing high-frame-rate video streams. While recent efforts have attempted to leverage spatio-temporal similarity to eliminate redundant computation, they either rely on expensive similarity recognition or support only limited reuse, resulting in limited performance gains. In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of the potential opportunities and challenges in exploiting spatiotemporal similarity within VidTs. Building upon these insights, we propose SimVidT, a novel VidT accelerator that leverages spatio-temporal similarity to reduce computational redundancy. SimVidT is supported by an algorithm and architecture codesign. At the algorithm level, we introduce a locality-aware similarity identification method and a redundancy-eliminated attention mechanism to efficiently identify and eliminate redundant computations at multiple granularities. At the architecture level, we develop a dedicated accelerator featuring a customized hierarchical memory management unit and specialized compute units, which adapts to the complex execution flow of VidTs and translates redundancy reduction into performance gains. We implement a cycle-accurate simulator for performance evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that SimVidT achieves 1.7×speedup and 2.5× better energy efficiency on average compared to the state-of-the-art VidT accelerator CMC.

items.abstract_text: In this paper, we propose a design framework for a 3D near-memory computing architecture in high bandwidth memory (3D NMC-HBM) considering signal/power integrity (SI/PI) and computing performance. The design framework enables the physical co-design of the 3D interconnect and power distribution network (PDN) based on an electrical performance evaluation, while integrating the extracted interconnect-level parameters into a cycle-accurate simulator for a system-level performance evaluation. Each component of the 3D NMC-HBM architecture including the NMC processor die, interconnect channels, and a hierarchical 3D PDN is modeled considering the physical dimensions of the conventional graphics processing unit (GPU)-HBM module. The electrical performance of the 3D NMC-HBM architecture is analyzed using a detailed methodology considering SI for providing the extended bandwidth, and PI to ensure stable power delivery for high performance operation of the NMC processing units. Furthermore, the efficacy of the proposed framework is verified through a system-level evaluation. Integrated with a cycle-accurate GPU simulator, the computing performance and power consumption of the 3D NMC-HBM architecture is evaluated, considering the effects of reduced interconnect length, bandwidth extension, and higher core utilization. The results show that the 3D NMC-HBM architecture achieves higher computing performance and lower power consumption when computing memory-bound workloads, compared to the GPU-HBM.

Complex background patterns in scanning electron microscope (SEM) images and diverse defect textures pose significant challenges. Traditional methods usually suffer from insufficient data, labels, and poor transferability. In this paper, we propose a novel zero-/few-shot learning approach, SEM-CLIP 2.0, based on our SEM-CLIP framework [1], for accurate defect classification and segmentation. By leveraging learnable text prompts, SEM-CLIP 2.0 fully utilizes large-scale external data sources to facilitate robust cross-domain knowledge transfer. By alleviating the need for manual prompt engineering and extensive data annotation, SEM-CLIP 2.0 significantly reduces labor costs. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that our model achieves impressive classification and segmentation results under zero-/few-shot learning scenarios.

items.title: Tradeoff-Aware Analog Circuit Sizing Based on a Multitask Surrogate Model-Assisted Evolutionary Algorithm
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: Identifying the trade-off relations among various performances is essential in analog integrated circuit sizing, and multiobjective optimization is a routine method. However, mature multiobjective optimization algorithms are available for problems with up to 3 objectives, which is insufficient in many real-world design cases. To address this challenge, for the first time, the trade-off-aware analog IC sizing is formulated as a multitask single-objective constrained optimization problem. A method, called Multitask Efficient Surrogate Model-assisted Sizing Method for High-performance Analog Building Blocks (MT-ESSAB), is proposed, which simultaneously solves multiple design tasks with stringent and diverse specifications, each reflecting different trade-offs. The key innovations include a new knowledge-transfer-enabled surrogate model-assisted evolutionary search framework and a dynamic computing budget allocation method. Experiments using an amplifier and a voltage-controlled oscillator, considering 5 and 4 performance metric trade-offs, respectively, show the effectiveness and efficiency of MT-ESSAB.

items.title: Advancing Quantum State Preparation Using Decision Diagram With Local Invertible Maps
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: Quantum state preparation (QSP) is a fundamental task in quantum computing and quantum information processing. It is critical to the execution of many quantum algorithms, including those in quantum machine learning. In this paper, we propose a family of efficient QSP algorithms tailored to different numbers of available ancilla qubits — ranging from no ancilla qubits, to a single ancilla qubit, to a sufficiently large number of ancilla qubits. Our approach exploits the power of Local Invertible Map Tensor Decision Diagrams (LimTDDs) — a highly compact representation of quantum states that combines tensor networks and decision diagrams to reduce quantum circuit complexity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our methods significantly outperform existing approaches and exhibit better scalability for large-scale quantum states, both in terms of runtime and gate complexity. Furthermore, our method shows exponential improvement in best-case scenarios.

items.abstract_text: In hardware accelerators used in data centers and safety-critical applications, soft errors and resultant silent data corruption significantly compromise reliability, particularly when upsets occur in control-flow operations, leading to severe failures. To address this issue, we introduce two methods for monitoring control flows: a method using specification-derived Petri nets and a method using behavior-derived state transitions, targeting applications where the control flow is independent of the datapath, with the assumption of manageable operation patterns. We validated our method across four designs: convolutional layer operation, Gaussian blur, AES encryption, and a router in Network-on-Chip. Our fault injection campaign targeting the control registers and primary control inputs demonstrated high error detection rates in both datapath and control logic. Synthesis results show that a maximum detection rate is achieved with a few to around 10% area overhead in most cases. The proposed detectors quickly detect 48% to 100% of failures resulting from upsets in internal control registers and perturbations in primary control inputs. The two proposed methods were compared in terms of area overhead and error detection rate. By selectively applying these two methods, a wide range of area constraints can be accommodated, enabling practical implementation and effectively enhancing error detection capabilities.

items.abstract_text: As the automotive industry advances toward intelligent systems, the risk of chip failures in automotive applications has grown. Functional safety has thus become essential to ensure the reliability of automotive-grade chips. Sequential circuit fault simulation is a key part of functional safety and a major bottleneck in safety verification. The concurrent fault simulation (CFS) method is the most widely used algorithm for this purpose and is adopted in the leading commercial tool Z01X. While recent academic efforts have primarily extended CFS to the RTL level simulation, the fundamental gate level CFS algorithm has seen little improvement, despite its critical role in simulation performance. Two main issues in concurrent fault simulation are inefficient storage and computation of logic values, and performance limitations in its core component, the concurrent fault list. To address these issues, we propose a dual optimization strategy: (1) a bit-compression method that reduces memory overhead and enables fullyO(1) time gate evaluation, and (2) a scan list-based concurrent fault list implementation that improves efficiency with low time/space complexity and superior space locality. Experimental results show that our method achieves an average speedup of 6.10× over commercial tool Z01X, with gains exceeding 3× on large circuits, and 2.58× over academic simulator VISION, proving its strong practical value.

items.title: FARFLAG: Fully Automatic Radio Frequency Layout Generation and Its Application to Design of CMOS Millimeter-Wave Low-Noise Amplifiers
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: The design of millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated circuits (ICs) is traditionally a slow process that requires extensive iterations and computationally intensive full-wave electromagnetic (EM) simulations. This paper presents a fully automatic radio-frequency layout generation (FARFLAG) method for the end-to-end synthesis of mmWave ICs, from device generation to final layout. The proposed method utilizes a mixture of machine-learning-assisted optimization, lookup tables, and fixed parameters for device generation. We introduce a hybrid placement and routing algorithm tailored for mmWave ICs, which is enhanced with a two-restart mechanism to improve placement robustness and exploration. The synthesis is driven by an improved Bayesian optimization approach with constrained multi-acquisition functions to navigate the design space efficiently. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework by synthesizing two mmWave low-noise amplifiers. By integrating high-fidelity EM simulations, the FARFLAG method significantly reduces the search space compared to conventional methods, enabling the rapid synthesis of complex mmWave ICs with superior performance.

items.abstract_text: Tracing host–peripheral interactions is essential for optimizing edge and latency-sensitive systems, yet existing non-invasive MMIO tracing can impose prohibitive overhead under load. We present DevTrace, a low-overhead tracing framework that records semantically stable control-plane boundary events (e.g., submission, receive aggregation, interrupt entry) together with derived data-plane metrics (e.g., bytes, direction, identifiers such as queue/vector ids when available, and timestamps). Dev- Trace uses lightweight driver-level reporting stubs, a contention-optimized ring buffer, and a user-space handler that performs heavy correlation and analysis, yielding an OS-feature-light design that applies to both kernel- and user-space driver stacks. In NIC micro-benchmarks, DevTrace achieves lossless capture with 8KB buffers (50 ms polling) and 0.6–2.6% CPU overhead, whereas MMIOtrace requires up to 4–8MB buffers and 22–31% CPU overhead. In end-to-end macro-benchmarks co-locating Nginx with six model inference workloads, DevTrace keeps HTTP-serving p99 latency inflation within ∼6% and throughput degradation within 35%; inference slowdown is single-digit for Stable Diffusion workloads and generally within the tens of percent for the remaining models (with one outlier under r8169). In contrast, page-fault-based tracing can collapse co-located performance, degrading inference by over 200% and increasing p99 latency by over 500% in our settings.We further demonstrate portability via a Zephyr RTOS port and a user-space Vulkan-layer integration on QNX, and show that a Rust implementation of the core ring buffer incurs no meaningful runtime performance penalty.

items.abstract_text: Digital microfluidic biochips (DMFBs), renowned for their programmable and digital manipulations of droplets, have been extensively applied in the automation of bioassays. However, constrained by factors such as electrode size, quantity, and addressing methods, conventional DMFBs face challenges in deploying large-scale biochemical applications. In contrast, the next-generation active-matrix digital microfluidic biochips (AM-DMFs), leveraging their powerful capabilities in cross-addressing and parallel droplet manipulations, have emerged as a key alternative platform for high-throughput bioassays. Nevertheless, the execution of large-scale bioassays on the AM-DMF platforms poses significant challenges for droplet routing. For example, in single-cell proteomics assays, to facilitate high-throughput processing of numerous samples, hundreds and thousands of split droplets need to be transported in parallel to designated areas while avoiding on-chip obstacles. This gives rise to the large-scale obstacle-avoiding routing problem, which existing approaches prove inadequate to effectively address. In this paper, we propose the first obstacle-avoiding routing method called SwarmRouter for large-scale droplet swarms, which enables efficient path planning for droplets while ensuring conflict-free and deadlock-free operations. The proposed method includes the following key techniques: 1) A geometric-temporal coupled preprocessing strategy integrating droplet spacing optimization and priority scheduling for conflict and deadlock elimination, 2) a path preselection strategy for both path length reduction and conflict avoidance, and 3) a timing-driven parallel routing method with dynamic checkpoints for waiting time minimization. Experimental results on an ACXEL AM16K biochip system demonstrate that SwarmRouter successfully realizes conflict-free path planning for all given droplets, while achieving significant reductions of 25.13% in total path length, 19.6% in maximum arrival time, and an improvement of 12.63% in average droplet velocity compared to a baseline method.

items.abstract_text: Read reclaim (RR) is used to avoid read disturb errors by periodically migrating all valid data pages of the RR block to other free blocks. In order to reduce the negative effects of RR that will block user I/O requests for a long time, existing RR optimization schemes migrate the hot read data pages in advance before the appearance of read disturb errors, if there are idle intervals between two I/O requests. Such advanced RR schemes, however, employ page-level counters for tracking read frequency on the pages in the RR block to direct early hot read data migrations, which must require considerable space overhead and then impact I/O responsiveness. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel RR scheduling scheme, calledPhasedRR. Instead of using page-level access counters,PhasedRRincrementally constructs working sets over successive time windows to track the read frequency of recently accessed pages in RR blocks, thus reducing the space overhead caused by maintaining the counters. Furthermore,PhasedRRsupports phased migration for moving the data pages having varied levels of read hotness in the RR block to another block(s) in different phases before the hard RR threshold, meanwhile the cold data pages remain in the RR block until the block read count reaches the threshold. Through a series of simulation experiments based on several realistic disk traces, we illustrate that our proposal can reduce the overall I/O latency by 31.9% on average, in contrast to existing RR scheduling methods.

items.abstract_text: Researchers use high-level synthesis (HLS) to develop large-scale accelerators, leveraging extensive resources to handle intricate computational tasks. Recent Multi-Die FPGAs feature several super logic regions (SLR) within one device to meet the high resource demands of advanced computation. However, implementing a large-scale accelerator on multi-die FPGAs presents three obstacles. The first is the considerable delay penalty caused by the interconnectivity of accelerator modules across multi-die boundaries. The second is the congestion caused by modules’ excessive use of local resources. The third is that the increasing number of accelerator modules expands the design space, making it difficult to find the optimal design point. All of these pose limitations on the maximum achievable frequency for developing large-scale accelerator designs on multi-die FPGAs. Therefore, this paper proposes a frequency-oriented design exploration with the congestion-aware module mapping algorithm, FrqBooster. It combines modules’ location and resource consumption to provide coarse-grained floorplanning optimization. Firstly, we analyze the connections between accelerator modules and build optimization objectives. Secondly, we analyze the resource cost of each module in accelerator design and propose a two-stage resource-balancing strategy, combined with resource consumption, to alleviate local congestion. Finally, we design a congestion-aware algorithm to complete the overall exploration for achieving higher potential performance. In the experiments, results show that FrqBooster achieves maximum frequency improvements of 73.15% and 81.22% on the U250 and U280 platforms, respectively, compared to the default implementation in Vivado. Compared to related works on accelerator DSE scenarios, FrqBooster achieved a maximum improvement of 25.84×, resulting in better overall performance.

items.abstract_text: To address the demands of modern artificial intelligence (AI) applications, heterogeneous architectures have gained widespread adoption, ranging from embedded devices to high-performance computing systems. These applications often involve tasks with timing constraints, which are commonly categorized into hard real-time (HRT) and soft real-time (SRT) domains. HRT tasks require strict deadline guarantees, whereas SRT tasks can tolerate occasional deadline misses. The coexistence of HRT and SRT tasks is prevalent in multi-functional systems like autonomous driving. However, scheduling such mixed real-time workloads on heterogeneous architectures remains challenging due to the divergent timing objectives between the two task types, the non-preemptive execution model on GPUs that aggravates blocking, and the CPU-GPU alternating execution inherent to heterogeneous platforms. To address these challenges, OptMRT (Near-Optimal Partitioning for Mixed Real-Time Tasks) introduces a bi-partition mechanism, incorporating a dual-mode mapping policy, an Streaming Multiprocessors (SM) allocation strategy guided by a unified timing metric, and a scheduling strategy tailored for mixed HRT and SRT workloads. Leveraging end-to-end response time analysis, OptMRT achieves near-optimal performance for both HRT schedulability and SRT timing performance. Extensive experiments show substantial improvements in schedulability, up to 2.25× for HRT and 2.33× for SRT, over state-of-the-art approaches.

items.abstract_text: The development of accurate and robust compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures is a central research focus for accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) tasks, particularly deep neural networks (DNNs). Significant interest has emerged in analog and mixed-signal CIM architectures to improve the efficiency of data storage and computation, as well as to manage the large data volumes required by DNNs. Recent advances in emerging non-volatile memory (eNVM) solutions have driven progress in resistive mixed-signal CIM cores. However, mixed-signal CIM computing cores continue to face integration and robustness challenges that limit their widespread adoption in end-to-end AI computing systems. From an integration perspective, resistive and eNVM-based CIM cores require integration with a control processor to enable programmable acceleration. Additionally, SRAM-based CIM architectures remain more efficient and easier to program than eNVM-based alternatives. In terms of robustness, analog circuits are more susceptible to variations, leading to computation errors and reduced accuracy. This study addresses both challenges by introducing a self-calibrated mixed-signal CIM accelerator system-on-chip (Acore-CIM), fabricated using 22-nm FD-SOI technology. Integration is achieved through (1) a CIM architecture that combines the density and programmability of SRAM-based weight storage with multi-bit computation using linear resistors, alongside (2) an open-source programming and testing strategy for CIM systems. Accuracy and robustness are enhanced through automated RISC-V-controlled on-chip calibration, which improves compute signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) by 25–45 % across columns (reaching 18–24 dB) and reduces process-induced multiply-and-accumulate (MAC) error spread by up to 82 %. To demonstrate scalability, the proof-of-concept system-on-chip (SoC) is shown to be extendable to recent high-density linear resistor technologies, further enhancing computing performance.

items.title: DAG Scheduling and Analysis in Multicore Real-Time Systems via Subgraph Division
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: The worst-case response time of a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) on a multi-core system is strongly influenced by its scheduling and timing analysis. A scheduling method aligned with DAG topology would better utilize the multi-core computing resource, and a timing analysis method would produce a worst-case response time of the scheduling. Most existing approaches perform scheduling and bound the makespan based on complete paths, leading to overly pessimistic analysis results, especially in DAGs with complex topologies. To address this, we propose a DAG scheduling and timing analysis method via sub-graph division, to minimize the makespan while providing a tighter timing bound. The nodes in DAG are grouped into a series of sub-graphs based on data dependencies. Based on the sub-graph division scheme, a fine-grained scheduling method is proposed to minimize the makespan. Additionally, the pessimism by complete paths is reduced in the proposed division-based analysis by accumulating relative response times of smaller blocks. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces the worst-case makespan by 30.1% on average compared to the state-of-the-art methods.

items.abstract_text: It is known that the number constraint of the used layers becomes more important for cost reduction of chip designs. Based on the insertion of necessary vias onto the routing nets on the constrained layers inside a bottleneck channel, an efficient routing algorithm including layer-constrained global routing for area minimization and layer-constrained detailed routing for area minimization can be proposed for layer-constrained bottleneck channel routing (BCR). Based on the reassignment of the routing segments in Manhattan routing model, our proposed routing algorithm is the first algorithm for the layer-constrained BCR problem. In layer-constrained global routing, based on the assignment of the represented intervals with covering compatibility, the represented intervals on the extra tracks can be firstly reassigned onto the constrained tracks by using two separation-and-reassignment operations. Furthermore, the represented intervals can be mapped onto the global wires of the routing nets on the constrained layers for minimization of estimated area. In layer-constrained detailed routing, the boundary-oriented paths of the routing nets or sub-nets can be firstly assigned on the constrained layers for area minimization. Furthermore, the physical paths of the routing nets or sub-nets on the constrained layers can be modified to reduce the number of the used bends or vias of the routing nets. Compared with the combination of Taniguchi’s 2-layer routing algorithm and sequential conflict reassignment (SCR) for the 2BCR problem, the experimental results show that our proposed algorithm only uses 54.7% of CPU time to further reduce 2.6% of the routing area and 1.7% of the number of the used vias for 10 tested bottleneck channels on the average. On the other hand, compared with the combination of Taniguchi’s 3-layer routing algorithm and sequential conflict reassignment (SCR) for the 3BCR problem, the experimental results show that our proposed algorithm only uses 19.3% of CPU time to further reduce 3.0% of the routing area and 1.0% of the number of the used vias for 10 tested bottleneck channels on the average.

items.abstract_text: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) has become a key paradigm for large-scale high-dimensional data retrieval. As a typical ANNS technique, Inverted File with Product Quantization (IVFPQ) provides a promising solution by significantly reducing storage costs through PQ compression. However, IVFPQ suffers from severe redundant memory access issues during retrieval. This paper proposes LAS, a novel ANNS accelerator specifically designed to reduce redundant memory access in IVFPQ. LAS presents two core techniques :dimensionality reduction component and adaptive learned index forest (ALIF). The dimensionality reduction component filters out a large number of non-neighbor vectors in the early retrieval stage. ALIF improves the accuracy of neighbor prediction through a multi-segment indexing design, further reducing redundant accesses caused by prediction errors. Meanwhile, ALIF employs an adaptive search strategy based on query-cluster relationships to dynamically adjust the search range of different clusters. Experimental results demonstrate that LAS achieves significant improvements in retrieval efficiency and effectively reduces redundant memory access in IVFPQ compared to representative works.

items.title: AnalogCoder-Pro: Unifying Analog Circuit Generation and Optimization via Multimodal LLMs
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: Despite recent advances, analog front-end design still relies heavily on expert intuition and iterative simulations, which limits the potential for automation. We present AnalogCoder-Pro, a multimodal large language model (LLM) framework that unifies the stages of circuit topology generation and device sizing optimization. The framework features a multimodal diagnosis-and-repair feedback loop that uses simulation error messages and waveform images to autonomously correct design errors. It also builds a reusable circuit tool library by archiving successful designs as modular subcircuits, accelerating the development of complex systems. Furthermore, it enables end-to-end automation by generating circuit topologies from target specifications, extracting key parameters, and applying Bayesian optimization for device sizing. On a curated benchmark suite covering 13 circuit types, AnalogCoder-Pro successfully designed 28 circuits and consistently outperformed existing LLM-based methods in figures of merit.

items.title: ULTRA-MACE: A Unified Low-Bit Trans-Precision Reconfigurable Multiply-Accumulate Compute Engine for Accelerated Computing
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: The rising demand for energy- and resource-efficient edge-AI platforms calls for compute engines that balance throughput, flexibility, and run-time efficiency under tight bandwidth constraints. This brief presents ULTRA-MACE, a unified low-bit trans-precision reconfigurable multiply-accumulate compute engine (MACE) that supports FP4 (E2M1), FP8 (E4M3), Posit-(8,2), and Posit-(16,3) through a six-stage vectorized pipeline with 128-bit quire accumulation. ULTRA-MACE employs a high-precision split mantissa multiplication scheme and an integrated gated bypass for ReLU, achieving 4×/2×/2×/1× throughput (FP4/FP8/Posit-8/Posit-16) without increasing bandwidth demand. Post-route results in 28nm CMOS demonstrate a peak energy efficiency of 12.8 TFLOPS/W at 0.9 V and a compute density of 8.2 TFLOPS/mm2. Integrated into the TREA accelerator with 64 MACE, the FPGA prototype achieves 89% of theoretical peak performance and maintains practical accuracy with only 1.5% degradation relative to the FP32 baseline. Overall, these results demonstrate an efficient trans-precision compute engine for edge-AI acceleration.

items.abstract_text: Power metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs) are extensively used in high-power and high-frequency applications due to their high current capacity, superior switching performance, and ease of integration with compact designs. However, the reliability of MOSFETs can be significantly compromised by solder joint fractures between the MOSFET and Printed Circuit Board (PCB) during board-level thermal cycling testing. To address this issue, this study develops a three-dimensional (3D) computational model that approximates the thermomechanical properties of the PCB copper trace layer using the rule-of-mixtures principle. The model is used to evaluate the thermal cycle-on-board reliability of the solder joints during thermal cycling between -40°C and 125°C. The accuracy of the simulation model is validated by comparing the predicted out-of-plane deformation of the MOSFET package with the experimental results. The Anand viscoplastic constitutive model is employed to analyze the accumulated plastic work density (ΔW) per cycle in the solder joints over repeated thermal cycles. Additionally, a Taguchi experimental design approach is used to evaluate the influence of eight control factors on the plastic work density (PWD), including the clip layout, type and thickness of the epoxy molding compound, die thickness, solder joint thickness, PCB copper foil coverage, copper foil thickness, and PCB core thickness. By systematically evaluating these parameters, an optimal package design is identified that minimizes ΔW and enhances the reliability of the MOSFET assembly. The Taguchi results reveal that the thermomechanical reliability of the MOSFET package is primarily determined by the type of epoxy molding compound and the thickness of the solder joints.

items.abstract_text: Although deep learning has demonstrated remarkable capability in learning from unstructured data, modern tree-based ensemble models remain superior in extracting relevant information and learning from structured datasets. While several efforts have been made to accelerate tree-based models, the inherent characteristics of the models pose significant challenges for conventional accelerators. Recent research leveraging content-addressable memory (CAM) offers a promising solution for accelerating tree-based models, yet existing designs suffer from excessive memory consumption and low utilization. This work addresses these challenges by introducing RETENTION, an end-to-end framework that significantly reduces CAM capacity requirement for tree-based model inference. We propose an iterative pruning algorithm with a novel pruning criterion tailored for bagging-based models (e.g., Random Forest), which minimizes model complexity while ensuring controlled accuracy degradation. Additionally, we present a tree mapping scheme that incorporates two innovative data placement strategies to alleviate the memory redundancy caused by the widespread use of don’t care states in CAM. Experimental results show that implementing the tree mapping scheme alone reduces CAM capacity requirement by 1.46× to 21.30×, while the full RETENTION framework achieves 4.35× to 207.12× reduction with less than 3% accuracy loss. These results demonstrate that RETENTION is highly effective in minimizing CAM resource demand, providing a resource-efficient direction for tree-based model acceleration.

items.abstract_text: Digital processing-in-memory (PIM) has emerged as a highly promising architecture that significantly enhances computational efficiency by embedding logic operations directly within memory. In particular, the spin-orbit torque magnetic random-access memory (SOT-MRAM)-based PIM approach is regarded as a high-throughput and energy-efficient solution for data-intensive applications, effectively mitigating the inherent memory bottleneck issues in conventional computing systems. In this work, we develop low-cycle arithmetic operations using a 3T2M cell structure composed of two magnetic tunnel junctions (MTJs) that exploit both SOT and voltage-controlled magnetic anisotropy (VCMA) effects, integrated with three transistors to form a compact computational unit capable of full Boolean logic evaluation. The bitwise convolutional operation implemented for convolutional neural network (CNN) computational tasks exhibits higher parallelism and improved memory cell utilization, achieving a throughput approximately 29 times greater than that of low-cycle arithmetic operations. Furthermore, a novel comparison operation based on the 3T2M cell has been proposed and integrated into the computational module of the pooling layer within a digital MRAM-based PIM (DMPIM) architecture. A CNN implementation leveraging the proposed operations achieves an energy efficiency of 4.9 TOPS/W on the CIFAR-10 dataset using 16-bit precision for both inputs and weights.

items.abstract_text: With the rapid advancement of microfluidic technology towards large-scale integration, a new generation of microfluidic systems, known as Fully Programmable Valve Array (FPVA) biochips, has emerged. These biochips offer superior programmability and flexibility, making them ideal for a wide range of biochemical experiments. However, the shrinking size of chip features presents a substantial challenge in automating the physical design process. Furthermore, the occurrence of physical faults in these chips can lead to inaccurate bioassay results, further complicating the design process. The Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) algorithm has proven effective in managing the high-dimensional state space inherent in physical design tasks, enabling the identification of viable solutions even in large-scale faulty circuits. In this paper, we proposeEnFault, an enhanced fault-tolerant physical design framework for FPVA biochips that addresses both placement and routing challenges in the presence of physical faults. Based on the DRL algorithm, we develop fault-tolerant placement and routing decision-making models, named DRL-FTPlacer and DRL-FTRouter, to optimize the solution quality of physical design while ensuring fault tolerance. The framework optimizes the design process by dynamically adjusting placement and routing decisions, thereby enhancing solution quality and chip reliability. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms existing algorithms in terms of completion time of bioassay and total path length of fluid transportation for both small/medium-scale and large-scale circuits. Especially in large-scale circuits, the proposed framework achieves significant improvements in solution quality, fault-tolerance performance, and execution efficiency.

items.summary: Previous research on selective protection for neural network components typically exploits only static vulnerability differences. Although these methods improve upon classical modular redundancy, they still incur substantial overhead for neural network workloads that are both memory-intensive and computeintensive. In this work, we observe that neural network vulnerability is also input-dependent and varies dynamically at runtime. With this observation, we propose an adaptive, vulnerability-aware fault tolerance framework. At its core, a lightweight graph neural network (GNN) model dynamically predicts soft error vulnerabilities across inputs and neural network components, enabling real-time adaptation of fault tolerance policies. This design offers a complementary and more efficient protection scheme compared to traditional approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that the GNN predictor achieves over 95% accuracy in identifying critical inputs and components. Moreover, our adaptive scheme reduces computational overhead by an average of 42.12% while preserving model accuracy, significantly outperforming static selective protection methods.

items.abstract_text: Analog and mixed-signal (AMS) circuit design remains challenging due to the shortage of high-quality data and the difficulty of embedding domain knowledge into automated flows. Traditional black-box optimization achieves sampling efficiency but lacks circuit understanding, which often causes evaluations to be wasted in low-value regions of the design space. In contrast, learning-based methods embed structural knowledge but are case-specific and costly to retrain. Recent attempts with large language models (LLMs) show potential, yet they often rely on manual intervention, limiting generality and transparency. We propose TopoSizing, an end-to-end framework that performs robust circuit understanding directly from raw netlists and translates this knowledge into optimization gains. Our approach first applies graph algorithms to organize circuits into a hierarchical device–module–stage representation. LLM agents then execute an iterative hypothesis–verification–refinement loop with built-in consistency checks, producing explicit annotations. Verified insights are integrated into Bayesian optimization (BO) through LLM-guided initial sampling and stagnation-triggered trust-region updates, improving efficiency while preserving feasibility. On four real-world AMS circuits (OTA, FC-OTA, SACMP, LDO) in a 55-nm CMOS process, TopoSizing achieves 100% correctness in circuit understanding and parameter assignment. In constraint-satisfaction tasks, it delivers 1.4×–4.8× higher sample efficiency and 1.2×–3.5× faster runtime compared with strong baselines, while requiring 2–4× fewer LLM calls than prior LLM-based frameworks. Ablation studies confirm that reliable circuit understanding is essential for these gains.

items.abstract_text: Multi-task transformers have garnered widespread attention for fast task adaptation at edge. However, in addition to matrix-vector multiplication with static and dynamic weights in the data-intensive transformer, task adaptation introduces new challenge of weight updating. Besides, while sparsity can help mitigate the rapid growth in parameter size and computational demand, it requires great hardware flexibility. Compute-in-memory (CIM) is widely explored to overcome the memory bottleneck in neural network acceleration, mainly with single type of memory devices, but struggles to balance the storage density with computing flexibility across multiple tasks. Meanwhile, the conventional pipeline parallel dataflow for high throughput suffers from the underutilization with bubbles caused by variable input sequence length and model sparsity. In this paper, HEIRS-PS, a hybrid three-dimension RRAM- and SRAM-CIM architecture, is proposed for the pipelined multi-task transformer acceleration with sparsity. With the 3D integrated RRAM-CIM and SRAM-CIM arrays, a novel hybrid- CIM paradigm is proposed with the collaborative addition to achieve both high storage density and computing flexibility for multi-task inference. Moreover, by fully leveraging the hybrid-CIM structure in HEIRS-PS, a new dynamic workload scheduling method is proposed with a layer regrouping method to balance the computing latency across pipeline stages. By eliminating the bubbles, the model inference latency is reduced with higher throughput. Experiment shows that the proposed HEIRS-PS architecture improves the energy efficiency by up to 13.3× and 8.68×, compared with state-of-the-art (SOTA) RRAM-CIM and SRAM-CIM works on Llama-1.3B. Moreover, HEIRS-PS also reduces the computing latency by up to 29.5% with the balanced latency across pipeline stages.

items.abstract_text: Diffusion models (DMs) exhibit remarkable generative performance within AI. Despite their outstanding generative capability, DMs still face two major limitations in fast and energy-efficient edge deployment: 1) the large number of parameters in DMs introduces substantial computational overhead during a single inference; 2) The iterative denoising property of DMs requires multiple inference steps, which further amplifies both computational and memory overhead. To alleviate the bottlenecks of DMs described above, we propose an importance-aware dynamic compression framework for hardware-efficient inference of DMs. We design importance metrics for steps, blocks, and layers in DMs based on the observation that not all denoising modules are equally important for a specific input. Guided by importance metrics, we propose a dynamic pruning method to eliminate redundant blocks during iterative denoising, while simultaneously applying binary quantization to the weights and mixed-precision quantization to the activations. To address the accuracy degradation introduced by the compression framework, we further propose tailored supervision losses and novel connection modes to improve the semantic fidelity and perceptual quality of the generated images. Given the binary and mixed-precision operations, along with the dynamic changes in model topology and computation flow due to pruning, we design a dedicated accelerator to more effectively supports our compression framework. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a maximum pruning acceleration of 1.21× and a quantization bit-width of W2.05A4.59. The hardware implementation achieves 2.3× speedup and 76% energy savings compared to the baseline.

items.abstract_text: Recent progress in video generation models (VGMs) has enabled long video generation with strong visual fidelity. VGM architectures have evolved from decomposed 2D attention (e.g., separate spatial/temporal attention) to 3D full attention that jointly processes all frames. However, inference latency remains a major bottleneck due to algorithmic and architectural inefficiencies. Differential methods have become a potential solution by leveraging sparsity to reduce computation. However, existing studies face two challenges:Challenge-1: The existing differential methods fail to identify the weakly connected parts in VGM that can be approximately calculated, leading to many potential redundant computations or severe impacts on generation quality (> 5% loss).Challenge-2: The traditional architecture fails to effectively utilize the unique redundancy distribution (i.e., column-concentrated pattern) in compressed VGMs. To address the above challenges, we proposeDiffAttn, a sparse attention architecture for video generation with differential approximation. Building on our prior conference work (ViDA),DiffAttngeneralizes differential computing to 3D full attention and strengthens architectural support to exploit the resulting column-concentrated sparsity. It combines three tightly coupled techniques. (1) Spatial information-guided differential estimation method utilizes spatial information to estimate the weakly connected regions in attention computation, which reduces the attention computation by 66.84%. (2) Column-concentrated computing architecture fully leverages the unique column-concentrated sparsity characteristics in the compressed VGMs, which achieves 1.52× speedup over a fully dense architecture. (3) Sparsity-aware inter-layer dataflow dynamically adjusts the workload ratio between the two cores by analyzing layer-wise sparsity and column distribution at runtime, improving the utilization by 36.33%. Experiments on advanced VGMs (e.g., CogVideoX1.5, OpenSora2.0) show thatDiffAttnachieves up to 2.62× and 1.89× end-to-end speedup and 3.14×/ and 2.87× energy efficiency improvement over NVIDIA A800 GPU and advanced VGM accelerator, respectively.

items.abstract_text: Deep neural networks (DNNs) enhance the accuracy and efficiency of reconstructing key parameters from time-resolved photon arrival signals recorded by single-photon detectors. However, the performance of conventional backpropagation-based DNNs is dependent on the optical setup and the biological samples, necessitating frequent retraining of the network, either via transfer learning or from scratch. Newly collected data must be stored and transferred to a high-performance GPU server for retraining, introducing latency and storage overhead. To address these challenges, we propose an online training algorithm based on a one-sided Jacobi rotation-based online sequential extreme learning machine (OSOS-ELM). We fully exploit parallelism and partition-independent functions to execute OSOS-ELM on a heterogeneous FPGA with integrated ARM cores. Extensive evaluations of OSOS-ELM and OS-ELM demonstrate that both achieve comparable accuracy across different network dimensions (i.e., input, hidden, and output layers), while OSOS-ELM is more hardware-efficient. By leveraging the parallelism of OSOS-ELM, we implement a holistic computing prototype on an Xilinx ZCU104 FPGA. We validate our approach through three typical case studies involving single-photon signal analysis: fog sensing with a commercial single-photon LiDAR, fluorescence lifetime estimation in fluorescence lifetime imaging, and blood flow index reconstruction in diffuse correlation spectroscopy, all of which use one-dimensional data encoded from photonic signals. From a hardware perspective, we optimize the OSOS-ELM workload by employing multi-tasked processing on ARM CPU cores and pipelined execution on the FPGA’s logic fabric. We also implement our OSOS-ELM on the NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX GPU to comprehensively evaluate its computational performance on another heterogeneous computing platform.

items.title: WTP: Weighted Time Protocol in Fault-Tolerant Automotive Embedded Systems
items.journal: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.venue_name: IEEE Transactions on Computer-Aided Design of Integrated Circuits and Systems
items.summary: The advancement of automotive intelligence necessitates high-bandwidth, low-latency, and highly reliable data transmission within automotive embedded systems. Mainstream automotive embedded systems address the risks associated with link failures by adopting fault-tolerant architectures (i.e., Zonal architectures). While these fault-tolerant architectures enhance system reliability, they impose stringent requirements on communication delays (i.e., time offsets) between nodes. The general Precision Time Protocol (gPTP) facilitates time synchronization among nodes through the Best Master Clock Algorithm (BMCA). However, when the primary link experiences a failure, BMCA must reselect a new server clock and reconstruct the hierarchy, which consequently compromises synchronization accuracy for a certain duration. Existing methods employ fault tolerance strategies based on redundant multi-transmission links to mitigate clock switching. However, they fail to consider noise suppression and dynamic fault adjustments within multi-link scenarios. items.abstract_text: The advancement of automotive intelligence necessitates high-bandwidth, low-latency, and highly reliable data transmission within automotive embedded systems. Mainstream automotive embedded systems address the risks associated with link failures by adopting fault-tolerant architectures (i.e., Zonal architectures). While these fault-tolerant architectures enhance system reliability, they impose stringent requirements on communication delays (i.e., time offsets) between nodes. The general Precision Time Protocol (gPTP) facilitates time synchronization among nodes through the Best Master Clock Algorithm (BMCA). However, when the primary link experiences a failure, BMCA must reselect a new server clock and reconstruct the hierarchy, which consequently compromises synchronization accuracy for a certain duration. Existing methods employ fault tolerance strategies based on redundant multi-transmission links to mitigate clock switching. However, they fail to consider noise suppression and dynamic fault adjustments within multi-link scenarios. In this study, we present a Weighted Time Protocol (WTP) designed for fault-tolerant automotive embedded systems. WTP establishes a redundant synchronization model between server and client clocks through broadcast messages, allowing the server clock to concurrently synchronize with client clocks across multiple independent links. WTP dynamically adjusts the weights of each clock source by analyzing the packet loss rate and delay fluctuations of each link, assigning higher weights to more reliable clock sources. Furthermore, WTP employs a weight-based Kalman filtering to iteratively enhance the filtering process, gradually reducing time offset and jitter. Experimental results demonstrate that WTP significantly enhances the accuracy of redundant time synchronization under link failure, achieving an average time offset improvement of 45.5% and a reduction in recovery time by 24.4%. Additionally, WTP exhibits lower overhead across various clock nodes.

items.abstract_text: Graph neural networks have emerged as a powerful tool for learning circuit representation but largely ignore the dynamic nature of logic optimization (LO), leading to a severe “domain gap” where embedding quality degrades after heuristic transformations. To address this, we propose CircuitFlow, a framework learning representations for both circuits and optimization algorithms. CircuitFlow is distinguished by three features: (1) it employs circuit motifs and DAGTrans for robust encoding; (2) it utilizes a dual-component architecture where OPTrans models optimization operations via Transformers; and (3) it seamlessly integrates into LO pipelines to predict optimized circuit statistics.Experimental results demonstrate that CircuitFlow reduces physical metric prediction loss by up to 72% compared to baselines. Crucially, it effectively bridges the domain gap, bringing the generalization error on optimized circuits down from over 65% to within 20%. Furthermore, integrating CircuitFlow into the LO flow yields an average QoR improvement of 3.97% alongside a 3.11× speedup. Finally, we leverage CircuitFlow to introduceorientational logic optimization, a new paradigm guiding synthesis toward target structures, which reduces the runtime of Combinational Equivalence Checking (CEC) by 76% on average.

In QMR, achieving high qubit fidelity is essential as it ensures reliable execution of a quantum circuit on a quantum computer. However, existing QMR algorithms focus on optimizing the average fidelity (AVF) across all qubits, ignoring theworst case fidelity(WCF) of individual qubits. In practice, a particularly low-fidelity qubit can greatly diminish the reliability of a quantum circuit, as a single qubit failure can lead to the failure of the entire circuit. To address this issue, we introduce QDP, a parallel dynamic programming (DP)-based QMR algorithm that optimizes the WCF while balancing the overall AVF. QDP leverages a state graph as the optimal substructure for our DP formulation to capture all valid quantum circuit execution orders. To enhance performance, QDP introduces a parallel DP-based state traversal algorithm that maximizes WCF through remapping and reduces the size of the state graph via progressive state expansion. Compared with state-of-the-art QMR algorithms, QDP can enhance the WCF by up to 33.88% while achieving comparable AVF on real quantum computers with up to 53 qubits.

items.title: An Energy-Efficient Hybrid Optogenetic Stimulation System With Sub-Threshold Electrical Stimuli and Decaying Exponential Irradiance
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a hybrid optogenetic stimulation system incorporating sub-threshold electrical preconditioning, a high-efficiency switched-capacitor LED driver, and decaying exponential irradiance waveforms to improve both stimulation system efficiency and optogenetic efficacy in wirelessly powered implantable devices. The system consists of an optogenetic switched-capacitor stimulator (OSCS), a sub-threshold electrical stimulator (STES), and a hybrid stimulus configurator, where the OSCS employs an inductor-assisted capacitor charger with a per-LED VTG -matched charging scheme, the STES delivers a sub-threshold biphasic pre-pulse to lower the optical activation threshold, and the configurator synchronizes the stimulation timing for coordinated hybrid stimulation. The proposed system achieves capacitor charging and discharging efficiencies up to 94.05% and 99.14%, respectively, and a peak LED driving efficiency of 90.75%. Ex vivo experiments using ChR2(H134R)-expressing rd10 mouse retinas demonstrate equivalent neural activation with 70.64% lower LED driving energy compared to conventional optogenetics-only stimulation.

items.abstract_text: Flash-mode direct time-of-flight (dToF) light detection and ranging (LiDAR) is widely adopted in autonomous systems and robotics due to its capability for accurate depth measurement and robustness under challenging lighting conditions. However, scaling single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD)-based dToF pixel arrays toward higher resolution 3-D imaging introduces significant challenges in power consumption and on-chip data handling, particularly when large-volume time-correlated single-photon counting (TCSPC) data are uniformly acquired and processed. This work presents a$96\times 64$SPAD-based flash LiDAR sensor employing a dual-mode sensing architecture that combines full-resolution 2-D intensity detection with on-chip edge-guided sparse 3-D depth detection. An on-chip edge extraction circuit (EEC) identifies structurally salient regions from the 2-D intensity map and guides pixel-level skipping during 3-D detection, thereby concentrating time-of-flight (ToF) measurements on informative areas while avoiding unnecessary full-array activation and excessive TCSPC readout. The resulting sparse 3-D depth maps are fused with dense 2-D intensity maps using a multi-modal, AI-assisted reconstruction network, demonstrating that the retained measurements are sufficient to recover full-field depth information. By co-designing on-sensor data acquisition and AI-assisted reconstruction, the proposed architecture reduces the effective 3-D data volume by 87.5% and significantly lowers readout and processing overhead. Fabricated in an 180-nm CMOS process, the prototype operates at 30 f/s with a total power consumption of 64.6 mW and achieves an imaging figure of merit (FoM) of 2853.2 pixel•f/s/mW, corresponding to a$6\times $promotion compared with conventional full-array 3-D detection at the same resolution. The proposed sensing–computation co-designed framework provides an energy-efficient and scalable solution for high-resolution flash LiDAR in power-constrained embedded platforms.

items.title: A Self-Powered 21-Component Transient Piezoelectric Energy Harvester With Single-Stage MPPT and Near-Zero Standby Consumption
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a rectifierless synchronous inversion and optimal charge extraction (SIOCE) interface with single-stage maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for intermittent vibrations, which are common in real-world applications. Unlike conventional rectifiers that suffer from standby power consumption or rely on inefficient multi-stage conversion, the proposed SIOCE interface circuit decouples the input from the output, rendering the output power independent of the load and dependent solely on maximum power point voltage ($V_{\mathrm {MPP}}$). The envelope-scale-flipping-based single-stage MPPT enables continuous energy harvesting and fast MPPT convergence. As a fully self-powered piezoelectric energy-harvesting (PEH) system realized with only 21 components, it operates with near-zero standby power consumption. The proposed design was fabricated using a 180-nm BCD process. Measurements show that the maximum MPPT efficiency and conversion efficiency reach 95.1% and 80.9%, respectively, with the maximum output power reaching 6.2 times that of the full-bridge rectifier (FBR).

items.abstract_text: Computing-in-memory (CIM) has been widely investigated as a solution to the von Neumann bottleneck to reduce data transfer between memory and processor. However, existing CIM macros for neural network (NN) edge applications still suffer from high latency and energy consumption due to the correlation between data precision and the number of multiplication and accumulation (MAC) cycles. Moreover, modern convolutional NN (CNN) models contain massive parameters that are distributed across multiple CIM macros. While multi-macro architectures enable large-scale deployment, they incur inefficient bandwidth utilization during input loading and frequent inter-module communication, both of which cause significant performance degradation. To address these issues, this article presents an array partition multi-macro CIM (APM-CIM) system with dynamic sparse approximation. First, a novel CIM macro incorporating double-input and sparse approximation mechanism is proposed to halve the number of computation cycles and skip insignificant operands during MAC. Second, an array partition mapping scheme for weights is proposed to reduce the bandwidth requirement of a CIM macro, thereby maximizing cache bandwidth utilization to implement high-parallelism computation. Finally, data and task managers are designed to minimize the performance degradation of the CIM macro at the system level. Through cross-level co-design of circuit, architecture, and system, the fabricated 40-nm CMOS chip achieves a system energy efficiency of 67.63 TOPS/W, which reduces the performance loss ratio by$3.7\times $and is$10.4\times $higher than state-of-the-art CIM-based systems. Using the VGG model on the CIFAR-10 dataset, the system delivers an accuracy of 89.95% at a power consumption of 34.0 mW.

items.abstract_text: Boolean satisfiability (SAT or$k$-SAT,$k \ge 3$) is a binary combinatorial optimization problem (COP) that is challenging for traditional classical computing to address in polynomial time. Quantum and quantum-inspired systems have been touted to tackle these and similar nondeterministic polynomial-time (NP) problems. This work describes Medusa, a quantum-inspired$k$-SAT solver capable of addressing problems of up to 200 variables and 1016 clauses. Implemented using analog and mixed-signal circuits, the solver benefits heavily from massive parallelism, continuous-time operation, and excellent energy efficiency, and advances the field of quantum-inspired, analog computing with best-in-class performance and energy efficiency. This performance is achieved with the introduction of three key architectural advancements: dual Make and Break feedback, a distributed logic feedback network, and multi-macro operation. The dual feedback mechanism improves the mean time to solution (TTS) for 50-variable 3-SAT problems by$30\times $when compared with a single feedback mechanism. The distributed logic in the feedback network implements all-to-all spin connectivity with arbitrary order interactions, enabling$k$-SAT operation and supporting the scalability of the solver, which is further enhanced by multi-macro operation. Medusa, implemented in a 28 nm process, achieves a$4.92~\mu $s TTS for the popular SATLIB uf50-218 benchmark with a mean energy to solution (ETS) of 19.1 nJ. For the uf200-860 benchmark the solver achieves a 30.9 ms mean TTS, outperforming quantum annealing for problems of the same size.

items.abstract_text: This article presents an eight-channel dual-polarized Ku-band transmitter (Tx) beamformer integrated circuit (BFIC) fabricated in a 22-nm GlobalFoundries FDSOI process. Each channel integrates independent phase and gain control utilizing a 7-bit active phase shifter (PS) and a 5.5-bit attenuator (ATT). To mitigate performance degradation caused by load impedance variations in dense arrays, the Tx utilizes a load-insensitive source–follower power amplifier (PA) topology. The chip includes an on-chip power management unit (PMU) with low-dropout regulators and temperature-compensated biasing to ensure stable operation across temperature. The Tx occupies a total area of$4.17\times 3.3$mm2. Measurement results demonstrate a peak small-signal gain of 30.9 dB, a peak saturated output power ($P_{\text {sat}}$) of 16.8 dBm, and a peak front-end power added efficiency (PAE) of 31.5%. The peak Tx 1-dB output compression point (Op1dB) measured at 13 GHz is 16.45 dBm, with a corresponding PAE of 30.6%. The PS (ATT) exhibits an rms phase error of$\text {EVM}_{\text {rms}}$) better than −23.4 dB while delivering 7.21–12.07-dBm average output power ($P_{\text {avg}}$) with an average power-added efficiency$\text {PAE}_{\text {avg}}$of 7.9%–18.3%. Under QPSK and 64-QAM, the$P_{\text {avg}}$is 11.4/9.2 dBm with 14.5%/11.6%$\text {PAE}_{\text {avg}}$and$\text {EVM}_{\text {rms}}$better than −26.4 dB at 4/9 Gbit/s, respectively. These results demonstrate that the source–follower PA delivers competitive linear output power with high efficiency while supporting complex modulated signals without compromise, making the Tx suitable for spectrally efficient satellite communication (SATCOM) links.

items.abstract_text: Pursuing a scalable quantum processor based on color centers in diamond, this work presents a novel multi-qubit cryo-CMOS system-on-chip (SoC) with a class-DE radio frequency digital-to-analog converter (RFDAC) and a class-D pulse-density modulation (PDM) driver that controls both electron and nuclear spin qubits of a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center using a shared driving coil. The electron spin driver employs a polar-based architecture with programmable memory for amplitude control and a direct-digital-synthesis (DDS) phase modulation (PM) path for accurate phase and frequency control. The nuclear-spin driver adopts a digital loop filter with resonant feedback to shape quantization noise out of band, while ensuring improved supply rejection thanks to a feedback loop via an analog-to-digital converter (ADC). Fabricated in a 40-nm CMOS process and operating at 6 K, the chip can drive over 80 mA output current with a 52 dB signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) over 50 MHz bandwidth (BW) at the electron-spin target frequency (2.5 GHz), and 36 mA with SNR > 52 dB over 20 kHz BW and a spurious free dynamic range (SFDR)$= {\mathrm {47~\text {dB}}}$across the target nuclear-spin band (1.9 to 2.1 MHz), allowing for driving operations on multiple nuclear spins with high fidelity. Driving the qubits resulted in a Rabi frequency of 2.31 MHz (1.95 kHz) for the electron (nuclear) spins, while drawing 45 mW (17 mW) from the supply. The single-qubit operation on an electron (and a nuclear) spin, characterized using gate-set tomography (GST), achieves a fidelity of 99.3(1)% (99.5(1)%). These results advance the scalability of distributed quantum processors based on color centers in diamond.

items.title: A −251.4-dB FoM Calibration-Free Fractional-N Cascaded PLL With Wideband Oversampling Noise-and-Spur Cancellation
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a calibration-free fractional-N cascaded phase-locked loop (PLL) employing a sampling phase detector (SPD)-bypass-based phase-domain oversampling noise-and-spur cancellation (P-OSNSC) technique. By incorporating an oversampling cancellation path that eliminates the gain errors and noise cancellation bandwidth limitation introduced by the SPD, the proposed architecture suppresses noise from the first-stage RO-based frequency multiplier at minimal power overhead, without invoking high-frequency reference or calibration. This approach enables noise cancellation across a wider bandwidth compared to previous arts. Moreover, the proposed prototype fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS achieves 127.8-fs rms jitter (integrated from 10 kHz to 100 MHz) with 4.48-mW power consumption, corresponding to a figure of merit (FoM) of −251.4 dB.

items.abstract_text: This article presents an electrical impedance tomography (EIT) system featuring a duty-cycling operation for gesture recognition to address the high power consumption of conventional EIT systems in wearable applications. The duty-cycling operation supports a scalable frame rate at proportionally scaled average power consumption. Moreover, a fast-settling high-pass filter (HPF) and digital I/Q demodulation with a digital matched filter are employed to reduce settling time, improving the system throughput. In addition, an intermediate-frequency (IF) shifting chopping technique is utilized to reduce power consumption, while the IF-converted harmonics are suppressed by harmonic-canceling finite-impulse-response (FIR) filters. A multiple-input–multiple-output (MIMO) current-balancing instrumentation amplifier is also proposed, employing a shared common node for multiple transconductance (TC) and transimpedance (TI) stages to minimize power, area, and input parasitics, enabling multi-channel scalability. Fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process, the proposed EIT system achieves 878.9 fps at$662.0~\mu $W and 27.5 fps at$43.8~\mu $W, reducing average power consumption by 62.2% and 97.5%, respectively, compared to continuous operation without duty cycling. The gesture recognition results demonstrate that the system achieves 99.7% accuracy for hand gestures and 84.1% for pinch gestures across four subjects.

items.title: A Reconfigurable Self-Clamp CSCR Converter With Fast-Converging MPPT for Energy Harvesting
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a reconfigurable self-clamp, continuously scalable-conversion-ratio (CSCR) switched-capacitor (SC) converter for photovoltaic (PV) solar energy harvesting (EH). By reducing flying-capacitor voltage stress without additional SC stages, the proposed architecture enables high-density capacitors and mitigates the complexity-loss tradeoff of conventional CSCR converters. A clamp-stage outphasing technique improves the power conversion efficiency (PCE), while a design methodology for selecting the number of flying and clamping capacitors is established. In addition, an insight is revealed for reducing the energy penalty of open-circuit-voltage (OCV)-based maximum power point tracking (MPPT). The reconfigurable-clamp-mode scheme extends the high-PCE voltage conversion-ratio (VCR) range and improves MPPT accuracy. Fabricated in a 180-nm CMOS process, the prototype exhibits 90% peak PCE, a high-PCE VCR ratio of 3.83 using only thirteen capacitors, and MPPT accuracy above 96.7% over a wide light-intensity (LI) range with a 334-$\mu $s convergence time.

items.title: An Intelligent Vision SoC With Fully Analog Sensing-to-Inference Pipeline and Linearity-Recovery RRAM Compute-in-Memory
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: Edge vision systems that integrate image sensing and neural-network inference on a single chip are constrained by inter-layer analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) and on-chip weight storage density, which together limit system efficiency and network scale. This article presents a fully analog vision system-on-chip (SoC) with 2-Mbit multi-level-cell (MLC) resistive random access memory (RRAM) that addresses both limitations through a continuous voltage–time datapath spanning pulsewidth-modulation (PWM) image sensing and multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) inference, eliminating inter-layer ADCs and off-chip memory access. The proposed linearity-recovery analog memory (LR-AMEM) compensates for the RC nonlinearity of direct charge-domain RRAM-based compute-in-memory (CIM), and a self-referenced threshold-variation-cancellation (TVC) mechanism suppresses process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) sensitivity. items.abstract_text: Edge vision systems that integrate image sensing and neural-network inference on a single chip are constrained by inter-layer analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) and on-chip weight storage density, which together limit system efficiency and network scale. This article presents a fully analog vision system-on-chip (SoC) with 2-Mbit multi-level-cell (MLC) resistive random access memory (RRAM) that addresses both limitations through a continuous voltage–time datapath spanning pulsewidth-modulation (PWM) image sensing and multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) inference, eliminating inter-layer ADCs and off-chip memory access. The proposed linearity-recovery analog memory (LR-AMEM) compensates for the RC nonlinearity of direct charge-domain RRAM-based compute-in-memory (CIM), and a self-referenced threshold-variation-cancellation (TVC) mechanism suppresses process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) sensitivity. A parameterized controller supports flexible kernel configurations and dataflow patterns without data reordering. The 55-nm prototype achieves 11.07 pJ/(pixel$\cdot $frame) sensing efficiency and 345.54 TOPS/W system efficiency, a$1.8\times $to$941.5\times $improvement over prior intelligent imagers, and demonstrates feature extraction (7.44% RMSE), image classification (87.4% on CIFAR-10), and five-class object detection (20.5% mAP@0.5) on a single chip.

items.title: A SAR Time-to-Digital Converter Embedding Time-Domain Noise-Shaping Self-Calibration
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article introduces a pipelined successive-approximation time-to-digital converter (SAR–TDC) that employs architectural and calibration techniques to improve linearity and bit utilization under delay mismatch and PVT variations. The design introduces a new bit-stage structure that enables practical decoupling of dominant error sources, and a noise-shaping SAR–TDC (NS-SAR–TDC) operating mode that facilitates in situ characterization of random delay errors and rapid foreground self-calibration without external hardware. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, the prototype achieves 800 MS/s over a ±100 ps input range from a 0.8 V supply, occupying 0.01 mm2, and consuming 1.71 mW. The proposed calibration improves the raw SFDR/SNDR by more than 20/12 dB, corresponding to a 2-bit ENOB enhancement. At Nyquist, the TDC achieves 5.73-bit ENOB with a 3.2 ps LSB, while static integral nonlinearity (INL) remains below 0.23 LSB/0.7 ps, demonstrating robust high-linearity operation and improved bit utilization across multiple chips.

items.title: A 16-Channel Cryo-CMOS Flux Control Pulse Generator ASIC
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article reports a 16-channel cryo-CMOS flux-control pulse generator ASIC demonstrated in conjunction with a superconducting-qubit-based quantum processor unit to advance the state of the art in cryo-CMOS-controlled two-qubit gate error rate. An architecture consistent with future scaled system requirements is presented and discussed. A qubit-limited error rate of 0.084% is achieved, demonstrating that the ASIC has sufficiently low noise, while dissipating <7 mW of power per flux control channel. Low noise with low power is realized using multiple methods. Three 10-bit sub-DACs, all referenced to an on-chip highly stable current reference and operating at different rates (up to 1 Gs/s), are combined to realize a pulse generator with 14-bit level resolution. Pre-compensation functionality is implemented in the on-chip digital processor to compensate for off-chip distortion. A custom SerDes designed for <1-mW power dissipation enables off-chip 2-Gb/s (to the chip) and 250-Mb/s (from the chip) communications.
