items.title: A Valuewise Hybrid-Domain Compute-In-Memory Macro for Energy-Efficient Edge-AI Devices
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a valuewise hybrid (VWH) compute-in-memory (CIM) macro that improves hybrid efficiency by$1.75\times $while simultaneously reducing computation error by$2.02\times $compared to prior bitwise hybrid schemes. The VWH approach performs accurate computations digitally for the most significant values (MSVs) in a small proportion, while the vast majority of the values are processed by lossy analog CIM (ACIM) macros to achieve high energy efficiency. To minimize latency and enhance the energy efficiency of the ACIM macros, a heterogeneous memory fabric (HMF) is introduced, which combines the benefits of static random access memory (SRAM)-CIM and dynamic random access memory (DRAM)-CIM. In addition, an asynchronous sparsity manager (ASM) enables adaptive throughput and power consumption based on sparsity. Fabricated using a 28-nm CMOS process, the prototype VWH-CIM macro achieves energy efficiencies of 470.5 TOPS/W in four-bit mode, 109.8 TOPS/W in eight-bit mode, and 48.5 TOPS/W in 12-bit mode.

items.abstract_text: Environmental sound recognition (ESR) technology has gained increasing prevalence in recent years across various applications such as smart caregiving and hearing-assistive devices, where always-on operation requires both high accuracy and ultra-low power consumption. However, the existing works have two main issues. First, the existing ESR algorithms are mainly implemented on GPUs or FPGAs, which cannot meet the energy constraints of AIoT devices, especially when SOTA ESR algorithms heavily rely on deep neural networks (NNs) to improve accuracy, resulting in large computations. Second, most of the existing ESR algorithms are trained using public datasets that are recorded in different sound environmental conditions (e.g., microphone and room sound environment) from those of their actual use, leading to significant accuracy degradation. Therefore, this work presents, to the best of our knowledge, the first fabricated ASIC-based ESR processor, integrating three co-designed techniques to address the above challenges: 1) a “short-long” progressive spectrogram processing (SLPSP) architecture to reduce the energy consumption; 2) a split-and-merge processing (SMP) architecture to further reduce the energy consumption; and 3) a weight clustering-based adaptive learning (WCAL) combined with offline domain-adversarial training to improve accuracy against sound environmental condition changes with significantly reduced data-access overhead. Fabricated in 65-nm CMOS, the proposed processor achieves an ultra-low energy consumption of 86~\mu J per classification and achieves classification accuracy of 100%, 91.41%, and 82.4% for two-, eight-, and 50-class tasks on the re-recorded ESC-50 dataset under real environment, respectively.

items.abstract_text: This article presents 10–30-GHz reflectionless pseudo-four-path mixer-first receivers. By introducing a balanced input network at the radio frequency (RF) port, the proposed receiver requires only a two-phase local oscillator (LO) to generate differential and orthogonal baseband (BB) signals, significantly reducing the complexity and power consumption of the LO generation circuit. The crosstalk issue caused by LO overlap is topologically mitigated by the inherent isolation (ISO) between the CPL and THU ports. In addition, the balanced input network not only maintains the reflection-based out-of-band (OOB) rejection mechanism of the$N$-path mixer-first receiver but also enables a reflectionless design. To further improve the transition-band roll-off and OOB rejection, two pairs of transmission zeros flanking the passband are introduced. The first pair of close-in transmission zeros is generated by an improved blocker-canceling technique, whereas the second pair is introduced by the$LC$tanks. Benefiting from the balanced input network and the improved blocker-canceling technique, both the input matching and OOB rejection are decoupled from the switch size, enabling the use of small-sized switches and thereby achieving high LO-to-RF ISO. Two receiver versions (Design-1 and Design-2) are presented: Design-1 excludes$LC$tanks, whereas Design-2 incorporates$LC$tanks. Fabricated in a low-cost 130-nm CMOS SOI process, both designs achieve a transition-band roll-off of approximately 40 dB/decade. Across 10–31 GHz, Design-1 achieves an RF-to-BB conversion gain of 7.3–10.3 dB, a double-sideband (DSB) noise figure (NF) of 12.1–16.3 dB, a blocker 1-dB compression point (B${}_{\mathbf {1dB}}$) of 2.15 dBm, an OOB input-referred third-order intercept point (IIP${}_{\mathbf {3}}$) of 11.3 dBm, an OOB rejection exceeding 25 dB, and an LO-to-RF ISO of 38–56.5 dB. Among them, the Pairing-based succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge (zkSNARK), like Groth16 and Plonk, featuring succinct proof size and constant-time verification, is deployed across a promising ecosystem. However, the heavy operations of proof generation that grow rapidly with application sizes and the frequent verification that requires costly Pairing severely hinder broader adoption. Moreover, there are many other cryptographic schemes also constructed based on Pairing, such as Boneh–Lynn–Shacham (BLS) signature, functional encryption (FE), identity-based encryption (IBE), and so on. Unfortunately, existing synthesis-based ZKP accelerators suffer from low area efficiency and incomplete operator coverage, causing poor overall speedup and expensive deployment cost. This work presents the first silicon-proven crypto-processor that supports complete proof generation/verification phases and can adapt to other Pairing-based cryptography (PBC). To achieve high flexibility while maintaining cost efficiency, we employ holistic optimizations across algorithm, architecture, and compiler levels, including the hybrid-grained instruction set, dedicated memory system, reconfigurable datapath, custom Pairing compiler, and utilization-oriented timing scheduling. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, it covers all related operators and achieves a$6.4\times $area reduction compared to prior synthesis-based work LegoZK, which currently makes it the most cost-effective candidate for the practical deployment of ZKP–PBC applications. As a case study, the processor performs$2^{16}$-gate proof generation/verification with 0.15 J/0.11 mJ, offering two orders of magnitude energy savings over a 14-core 2.4-GHz CPU. For the Pairing operator, it achieves development agility to enable fast design space exploration. It delivers$17\times $/$1.8\times $improvements of area-time product (ATP)/energy compared to the prior ASIC work.

items.title: Analysis and Design of a 2--8 GHz Eight-Phase N-Path Passive Mixer-First Receiver With Overlapping LO Signals and Harmonic Loss Suppression
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a technique for suppressing the effects of overlapping LO signals in an eight-phase N-path passive mixer-first receiver. In particular, an architecture for an eight-phase mixer is presented, allowing the receiver to operate at higher frequencies with overlapping 25% duty-cycle LO pulses without incurring significant degradation in loss or noise figure (NF). A theoretical framework is presented that predicts loss and allows efficient optimization of the associated circuitry. To verify these predictions, an experimental prototype eight-phase mixer-first receiver was designed in 45-nm RF silicon-on-insulator (SOI) CMOS, operating from 2 to 8 GHz with a 25% duty-cycle LO. The prototype receiver achieves an NF of 2.5–4.7 dB while consuming 81–176 mW. The out-of-band (OOB) blocker 1 dB compression point (B1dB) is 5.1–7.7 dBm and OOB input-referred third-order intercept point (IIP3) is 22.1–32.3 dBm. The receiver has >40 dB third-/fifth- order harmonic rejection (HR3/HR5), and up to 66 dB rejection with proper recombination weighting in DSP.

items.title: Multi-Mode In/Near-Pixel Processing CMOS Vision Sensor With Time-Memory-Based Temporal Derivative Computing
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a temporal-derivative (TD) computing multi-mode vision sensor. The proposed sensor features a novel frame difference (FD) processing scheme that eliminates the need for frame memory by employing a checkerboard patch-based pixel architecture and column-shared processing circuits. This configuration efficiently detects patch-level temporal changes and generates 1-bit event signals (EVTs). Furthermore, an in-pixel time memory (TM) circuit is introduced to enable area- and power-efficient mixed-signal TD computing. The$324~\times ~252$prototype sensor was implemented in a 0.18-$\mu $m CMOS process. Measurement results demonstrate that the sensor consumes$4.79~\mu $W at 12.5 frames/s, achieving a FoM of 42.2 pJ/pix$\cdot $frame in the patch mode operation for FD-based motion detection and TD generation.

Specifically, a custom frequency synthesizer in combination with injection-locking is proposed to replace the conventional PLL structure, resulting in low power consumption and nanosecond-order settling time due to the near-instantaneous nature of injection-locking. The proposed structure is capable of enhancing the accuracy of a fully-integrated oscillator to satisfy the ±60 ppm BLE frequency accuracy requirements with significant margin, without requiring changes to the standard. This enables crystal-less IoT sensor nodes in multiple applications, requiring only a single XTAL-based central node in the network. The presented prototype serves as a proof-of-concept demonstration of the proposed architecture, and the fully integrated, standalone operation remains for future work.

Compared to state-of-the-art analog in-memory compute MJPEG engines, TD-dAJC achieves$2.8\times $better energy efficiency and$25\times $higher throughput.

items.abstract_text: In this article, we present a nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center magnetometer that incorporates two application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) to implement several key functionalities of the system, marking an important step toward miniaturization and scalable production of NV magnetic field sensors. More specifically, the presented magnetometer utilizes a microwave ASIC (MW ASIC) for generating the required microwave (MW) magnetic field and a current-to-digital interface ASIC (readout ASIC) for reading out the optical quantum sensor signal. The MW ASIC incorporates an on-chip stripe array that produces the required MW magnetic field. The stripe array is driven by an on-chip quadrature modulator and a custom-designed current driver array, which includes a series resonance tuning feature for maximizing generation efficiency. The stripe array achieves a$\mathbf {\pm 5\%}~\mathbf {B_{1}}$-field variation over an area of$300\times 200~\mu $m with a power consumption of 55 mW. The readout ASIC digitizes the current of the photodiode, which collects the fluorescence signal of the NV centers, providing a low-noise readout in the presence of the photodiode’s large capacitance over a wide bandwidth of$\mathrm {500~\text {k}Hz }$while consuming 51 mW. It features a newly proposed autobalancing scheme to suppress fluctuations in the excitation laser light. Both chips are manufactured in a 130-nm CMOS SOI technology. The presented magnetometer, incorporating the two presented chips, achieves a DC magnetic field sensitivity of 2.1 nT/(Hz)1/2, derived from the measured optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) slope and total input-referred noise.

items.title: A 28-nm CMOS 1-Chip In-Pixel Memory Backplane Circuit for 1800 × 1350 6652-PPI MicroLED AR Glasses With Per-Pixel Current Sensing and Compensation
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a 28-nm CMOS 1-chip LED-on-Silicon (LEDoS) backplane (BP) for 6652-pixel-per-inch (PPI) microLED ($\mu $LED) augmented reality (AR) displays. To address power and display quality challenges in AR glasses, the proposed BP employs two low-power techniques: self-refresh and partial update, and introduces four display quality enhancement methods: MSB data shuffling, 2-bit bias calibration and tuning (2BCT), dead-pixel compensation, and spatial/temporal dithering. These functions are enabled by an 8-bit in-pixel memory (iPxM) for data storage and a per-pixel built-in self-test (pBIST) for current sensing. In self-refresh mode at 120 Hz, power consumption is reduced to 24.3 mW, achieving 50% power-reduction compared to normal operation. Display quality measurements show luminance differential nonlinearity (DNL) below ±0.5 LSB across all gray levels, flicker signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of −72 dB at 12 sub-frames, and 47.7% improvement in pixel current uniformity with 2BCT. The chip occupies an area of$8.21\times 7.39$mm and integrates a$1800\times 1350$pixel array.

items.abstract_text: This article presents a high-bandwidth eight-channel single-ended four-level pulse amplitude modulation (PAM-4) transmitter for next-generation pseudo-open drain (POD)-terminated memory interfaces. To reduce power consumption in POD termination, a PAM-4 least-significant-bit (LSB) data bus inversion (DBI) encoding scheme is implemented and compared to previous PAM-4 encoding schemes. Based on a theoretical analysis of termination power, the PAM-4 LSB DBI encoding achieves termination power savings comparable to those of previous schemes while reducing the overall system power by simplifying the DBI flag lane. A series-resistor-shielded, source-series-terminated (SST) driver improves output bandwidth by isolating the parasitic capacitances of pull-up and pull-down segments from the output node. A four-tap ZQ-based feed-forward equalizer (FFE) provides fine coefficient control to alleviate inter-symbol interference (ISI) with a small number of driver segments. Moreover, the transmitter supports two selectable FFE modes (high-ISI mode and low-ISI mode) to optimize power consumption across different channel conditions. A ZQ calibration for the remaining tap segments compensates for impedance mismatch and improves the ratio of level mismatch (RLM). An eight-channel prototype was fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, occupying an area of 0.0222 mm2per lane. The ZQ calibration ensures a minimum RLM of 0.985. Under multi-channel operation, the transmitter achieved a data rate of 42 Gb/s/channel at a worst case channel loss of −4.41 dB, with an energy efficiency of 1.2 pJ/bit, excluding the global clock path.

items.title: A Fully Integrated Wireless Multimodal Biosensing System-on-Chip for Stress Monitoring
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: A fully integrated multimodal biosensing system-on-chip (SoC) for stress monitoring is presented. The proposed SoC integrates electrocardiography (ECG), electrochemical (ECH), photoplethysmography (PPG), and galvanic skin response (GSR) sensing together with an on-chip transmitter (TX), wake-up receiver (WuRX), and power-management unit (PMU) for compact, standalone operation. ECG and ECH share a current-balancing instrumentation amplifier (CBIA), while the PPG and GSR channels employ an enhanced precharge scheme and automatic feedback adjustment (AFA), respectively. Fabricated in a 0.18-$\mu $m CMOS process, the chip occupies$4.67\times 6.85$mm and consumes$125.8~\mu $W in the analog front end (AFE). The ECG readout achieves a 130-dB common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR). The shared ECH front end consumes$16.8~\mu $W. The PPG and GSR readouts achieve dynamic ranges (DRs) of 113.86 and 99.3 dB, respectively. The TX supports 1-Mb/s data transmission, the WuRX achieves −57-dBm sensitivity at 2 kb/s, and the PMU provides$\mu $s transient recovery. Human stress experiments demonstrate real-time, multimodal biosignal acquisition using a system-level validation platform.

items.title: A 31.5--36-GHz Low-Spur Digitally Assisted Gain-Boosting Charge-Sharing Locking PLL Achieving 54-fs RMS Jitter
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a 31.5–36 GHz digitally assisted gain-boosting (GB) charge-sharing locking (CSL) phase-locked loop (PLL) that achieves record-low reference spurs while maintaining sub-60 fs integrated jitter. In conventional CSL PLLs, reference spur suppression is fundamentally traded against loop bandwidth, whereas ping-pong CSL (PP-CSL) approaches typically require complex duty-cycle calibration. The proposed GB-CSL architecture introduces a gain-boosting loop that uses ADC–DAC residue feedback to amplify charge information in the digital domain, thereby breaking the spur–bandwidth tradeoff without calibration overhead. Fabricated in 28-nm CMOS, the prototype achieves 54.6-fs rms jitter at a 33 GHz carrier, a −66-dBc reference spur, and a normalized FoM of −272 dB while consuming 14.76 mW and occupying$0.73\times 1.0$mm2. These results surpass recent state-of-the-art mm-wave PLLs in simultaneous spur and jitter performance.

items.abstract_text: Cryogenic approximate content-addressable memory (ACAM) offers an appealing solution that allows mismatches between the query and the stored data, measured by the Hamming distance (HD). However, in ACAM designs, increasing the word length shrinks the matchline (ML) voltage spacing between adjacent HD tolerance levels, thereby limiting the tunable-HD tolerance range and degrading discrimination. To address this issue, we propose a cryogenic eDRAM-based tunable-HD CAM (CTH-CAM) for reliable approximate search with a small ML voltage spacing. First, we present a cryogenic 4T1C single-finger embedded dynamic random access memory (eDRAM) gain cell with two complementary and decoupled comparison ports, which enables a wide HD tolerance range in approximate search with a small ML voltage spacing. Second, we introduce an adaptive reference voltage generation (ARG) scheme that replicates mismatch-driven ML voltages, enabling fine-grained discrimination with a small ML voltage spacing. Third, the CTH-CAM supports various operations, including memory, approximate BCAM/TCAM search, logic-in-memory (LIM), and matrix transposition operations, enabled by a cryogenic full-swing sense amplifier (FSSA). Measurement results of our test chip in a 28-nm CMOS process show that, compared to a state-of-the-art design (1–8 tunable-HD tolerance range for 64-bit word lengths), CTH-CAM achieves an improved tunable-HD tolerance range of 1–26 for 128-bit word lengths at 77 K, while maintaining a voltage spacing of$\geq 13$mV throughout the tunable range. Moreover, it also achieves an energy consumption of 1.37 fJ/bit at 0.9 V and 77 K.

items.title: A 65 nm Privacy-Preserving Neuromorphic Encoder With 7.13 nJ Efficiency, 2.38 Mb/mm 2 2T--2T Item Memory Density and Federated Learning Support
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: The increasing demand for privacy-preserving personal data analytics in smart assistants and context-aware systems necessitates hardware that is both energy-efficient and secure. This work presents a 65 nm privacy-preserving neuromorphic encoder that addresses these challenges through physically uncloneable and hardware-efficient encoding. At the core of the architecture is a 2T–2T entropy cell that enables compact and uncloneable hyperdimensional representations. The fabricated prototype achieves 7.13 nJ per encoding, 2.38 Mb/mm2item memory (IM) density, and supports in situ decision-making and continual learning with 76.44 nJ per prediction and 357.32 nJ per training update. To support multiuser deployment, a custom federated learning (FL) framework is proposed, enabling efficient cold-start personalization while preserving device-level model privacy. Evaluations on biosignal datasets demonstrate strong classification accuracy—93.2% on electromyography (EMG) and 96.1% on UCI-HAR—with additional gains of up to 14.7% performance gain through federated training.

items.abstract_text: In this article, we present an end-to-end AI-driven design methodology for radio frequency integrated circuits (RFICs) and validate it with silicon measurements spanning 24–150 GHz. RFIC design requires tight co-design among architecture, circuit topology, and electromagnetic (EM) structures, where each decision strongly influences the others. This highly coupled design space has traditionally relied on expert intuition, iterative refinement, and heuristic optimization. We introduce a unified framework that jointly synthesizes architecture, circuit topology, and EM interfaces from specifications to layout, without the EM structures being restricted to pre-defined templates. A reinforcement learning (RL) engine explores architectural (driver stages, combining), topological (amplifier cell circuits), and parameter choices while identifying optimal impedances or scattering parameters for EM interfaces. Once these EM targets are determined, inverse EM synthesis generates corresponding passive structures. A key feature of the methodology is controllable architectural style: the designer can guide the synthesized passive structures from classical transmission-line geometries (or transformers) to arbitrary pixelated layouts, preserving interpretability and debugging capability while accessing a broader design space. We validate the framework with millimeter-wave (mmWave) power amplifiers (PAs) and low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) implemented in 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology across 24–150 GHz, demonstrating state-of-the-art performance across all designs. The formulation is not tied to a specific process in principle, though all designs reported here are implemented in a single 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. Within a given technology, the methodology enables faster RFIC development, accurate near-Pareto front estimation, and exploration of design spaces beyond conventional human intuition.

items.abstract_text: This article proposes a 13.56-MHz wireless power and synchronized full-duplex data transceiver (WPSFDT) IC using a single inductive link for compact wearable and biomedical systems. Conventional full-duplex (FD) data telemetry systems are limited by their use of additional antennas or externalLCnetworks to create data channels in separate frequency bands, which increases system complexity and power consumption. On the contrary, the proposed WPSFDT system implements synchronized FD data telemetry without additional components by utilizing transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) synchronization (TRXS), which keeps the TX and RX always synchronized at the same frequency. The proposed WPSFDT significantly reduces system size and complexity by integrating both TX and RX functions into a single chip using a reconfigurable transceiver architecture. For the downlink, this system employs off-duration shift keying (ODSK), which ensures stable power delivery with a predetermined off-duration time regardless of data rate. For the uplink, it utilizes short-pulse load shift keying (SP-LSK) to minimize power delivery losses using SP-LSK signals. In addition, an envelope hold scheme effectively mitigates self-interference (SI) caused by uplink data transmission, which enables robust FD data telemetry. The proposed WPSFDT IC is fabricated using an 180-nm BCD process and has a chip size of$2.4\times 1.9$mm2. This system achieves a high bidirectional data rate of up to 400 kb/s. This novel WPSFDT system is expected to contribute to progress in wearable and biomedical applications, which require robust and high-speed bidirectional data telemetry, by enabling synchronized FD data telemetry over a single inductive link without additional components.

items.abstract_text: By vertically stacking device layers, advanced 3-D integration overcomes traditional planar scaling limits, delivering the bandwidth and power efficiency essential for modern artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) integrated systems. However, continued scaling of conventional through-silicon vias (TSVs) and microbumps presents critical bottlenecks due to inherent thermo-mechanical stress, complex manufacturing, and poor heat dissipation. Consequently, wireless interconnects based on electromagnetic (EM) coupling have emerged as a robust alternative. By pushing operating frequencies into the terahertz (THz) band, these wireless links exploit abundant spectrum to support the massive data throughput requirements. In this work, a THz through-silicon interconnect (THz-TSI) module for advanced 3-D integration is presented, which achieves a record-high data rate of 264 Gb/s and efficiency of 0.33 pJ/bit with the help of an offline equalization. Both bidirectional point-to-point link and broadcast mode are successfully demonstrated. This scheme offers highly competitive bandwidth and density with significantly simpler fabrication and lower cost. Furthermore, its high flexibility enables real-time adjustable interconnect topology to effectively reduce AI/HPC system latency.

items.title: A Hybrid Inner--Outer-Product SRAM Compute-in-Memory GEMM Engine With Precision-Adaptive Systolic Dataflow
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents an efficient SRAM compute-in-memory (CIM) macro design for general matrix multiplication (GEMM). A hybrid inner–outer product (HIOP) architecture is designed to enable long-time weight reusing and short-time input reusing, reducing 1.57–$2.69\times $overall SRAM access. A data-precision-adaptive dataflow is developed to scale the CIM macros with balanced bandwidth (BW) across varying data precisions. Our CIM-friendly dataflow obtains 19%–38.5% reduction in operation cycles with the CIM capability of concurrent read/write and computing. Fabricated in 22-nm technology, the CIM macro achieves energy efficiency (EE) of 56.2 TOPS/W for GEMM and 71.65 TOPS/W for multiply–accumulate operation (MAC) in 8-bit inputs and weights. The macro and system area efficiency (AE) are 3.18 and 1.89 TOPS/mm2, respectively, which is$1.42\times $and$1.12\times $compared with prior state-of-the-art (SOTA) designs.

items.abstract_text: Computing-in-memory (CIM) architectures are promising for edge-AI devices, as they mitigate the von Neumann bottleneck and reduce data movement. Bit-parallel CIM macros with direct memory mapping and low toggle rate are well-suited for computing systems. However, severe routing congestion, inefficient signed computation, and unnecessary toggling of intermediate signals in local multiply-accumulate (MAC) circuits remain unsolved. This article presents a 28-nm bit-parallel SRAM CIM macro for efficient INT8 and BF16 MAC operations, featuring three techniques: 1) a transition-counting-line (TCL) that performs sparsity-adaptive, lossless bit-column compression by recording full-swing transitions derived from partial products, thereby mitigating routing congestion while preserving full precision; 2) a bus-based TCL that reuses sign-bit multiply-multiplex units (MMUs) to realize embedded sign extension with only 3% area overhead and no additional cycles; and 3) a shared ten-phase generator that enables TCLs and accumulations in a stage-wise manner to suppress spurious toggling, improving energy efficiency by 42%. The macro achieves a 4.1-ns access time at 0.9 V, with peak energy efficiencies of 106.85 TOPS/W in INT8 mode and 77.68 TFLOPS/W in BF16 mode, and peak area efficiencies of 1.73 TOPS/mm2and 1.24 TFLOPS/mm2, respectively.

items.abstract_text: Future full-duplex (FD) radio systems require highly tunable self-interference (SI) cancellers with rapid adaptation to mitigate dynamic SI profiles in wireless environments. This article presents a 2.4-GHz RF SI canceller chip with extensive tuning capabilities that operates with a machine-learning (ML)-augmented adaptation loop for FD transceivers. The proposed design improves the depth of SI cancellation, canceller linearity, and convergence speed. The prototype canceller chip, fabricated using a 40-nm CMOS process, features enhanced tuning capabilities of the filter coefficients, delay spread, and linearity. A custom-designed neural network (NN) is implemented on an FPGA within a Xilinx RFSoC evaluation board to accelerate the convergence time during the canceller’s adaptation process. The RF canceller, realized as a six-tap complex finite impulse response (FIR) filter with programmable delay spread, achieves 30-dB SI cancellation over a 40-MHz bandwidth in a real wireless channel and 32 dB with a static load, with a post-calibration input-referred third-order intercept point (IIP3) of +38 dBm. The NN computes an initial canceller setting, followed by a dithered linear search (DLS) algorithm, achieving a convergence time of less than 10.5 ms. The SI canceller chip demonstrates a maximum group delay variation of 2 ns, an output noise density of −184 dBV/$(\text {Hz})^{1/2}$, and an S11of −10 dB across 2.3–2.8 GHz. The RF SI canceller chip occupies an active area of approximately 1.8 mm2and consumes 39 mW.

items.abstract_text: This article presents a 10-bit source-driver (SD) IC for high-resolution OLED-on-silicon (OLEDoS) microdisplays in augmented reality (AR)/virtual reality (VR) applications. To address the stringent constraints of aggressive area scaling, sub-microsecond settling time, and high output uniformity, three key techniques are proposed. First, a demultiplexer (DEMUX)-based channel width expansion method combined with deep-N-well (DNW)-based voltage-domain transformation enables the source driver IC (SD-IC) to fit within the 1.33-$\mu $m sub-pixel pitch of the OLEDoS panel. This DNW-based voltage-domain transformation allows the DAC and channel logic circuits to operate in a low-voltage (LV) domain, allowing the use of compact LV devices and thereby significantly reducing the channel area. Second, a data-difference-dependent dynamic current source (D3DCS) is introduced to meet the sub-microsecond driving-time requirements of 4K$\times{\,}4$K resolution at a 120-Hz frame rate of the OLEDoS displays. This technique selectively boosts the slew rate (SR) of the amplifier based on most significant bit (MSB) transitions without increasing static current or introducing dead-zone behavior. Third, an all-channel automatic offset calibration (ACAOC) scheme is proposed to suppress intrinsic amplifier offsets and improve output-voltage uniformity. Unlike conventional frame-to-frame polarity alternation techniques, which are less effective for OLEDoS panels due to their narrow data-voltage range, the proposed scheme directly minimizes the offset magnitude through simultaneous calibration across all channels, enabling uniform driving voltages without additional frame-level compensation. Fabricated in a 65-nm CMOS process, the proposed SD-IC occupies$2273~\mu $m2per channel. Measurement results show a settling time of$0.69~\mu $s and a reduction in maximum deviation of voltage output (DVO) from 26.6 to 1.9 mV. The measured differential nonlinearity (DNL) and integral nonlinearity (INL) are +0.27/−0.22 and +0.59/−0.33 LSB, respectively.

Based on our observations, the imbalanced operational intensities across diffusion model layers lead to suboptimal hardware utilization due to inadequate bandwidth optimization. Additionally, emerging 3-D and video generation tasks require computationally intensive multi-view consistency operations to ensure smooth transitions between perspectives and frames. In this work, we presentMTDiff, a multi-task diffusion accelerator featuring three key innovations: 1) a dynamic bandwidth-aware memory partitioning scheme optimizing hardware utilization and reducing external memory accesses; 2) an efficient bitline (BL)-segmented compute-in-memory (CIM) macro together with a reuse-aware weight update scheduler; and 3) a hierarchical multi-frame consistency management (MFCM) skips redundant operations at frame and pixel levels to improve computational efficiency. items.title: A 6-A 93.8%-Peak-Efficiency 5-V-to-Sub-1-V Segment-Interlaced SC-Parallel-Inductor Converter Featuring Inherently Balanced Ganging for Wafer-Scale Computing System
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: A segment-interlaced switched-capacitor-parallel-inductor (SI-SCPL) converter is proposed to power a wafer-scale computing system and accommodate unbalanced load-current distribution. Benefiting from quad-path operation across all switching states, the proposed segment interlacing (SI)-SCPL achieves continuous reduction in inductor current over a wide range of control duty cycles (D). Furthermore, the symmetric power-segment operation mitigates inductor-current imbalance without complex active-balancing control. To address the challenges of non-uniform power delivery, a comprehensive analytical model is developed to quantify the impact of spatial load asymmetries on system efficiency and stability. Fabricated in a 65-nm FCCSP CMOS process, the proposed SI-SCPL successfully clamps the voltage undershoot within 69.7 mV against a 2.5-A switching load. It achieves a peak efficiency of 93% at around 1 A and maintains 76.5% at 6 A. Compared to prior-art dual-inductor hybrid converter designs, it achieves 33% and 28% improvements in peak output current and planar current density, respectively.

items.abstract_text: Computing in memory (CIM) has emerged as a promising architecture that can significantly reduce power consumption and latency in edge artificial intelligence (AI) devices. For battery-constrained edge devices, non-volatile memories (NVMs) are ideal due to their ability to retain neural network parameters even when powered down, ensuring rapid response time upon device wake-up. However, the tradeoff between energy efficiency and computing precision in CIM implementation limits their ability to support various computational workloads in edge AI. In this article, we propose a logic-compatible embedded-flash macro with two-step time-domain computation. The proposed macro computes through dual capacitors operating in a ping-pong manner, enabling simultaneous activation of up to 128 cells with signed weights and achieving 10-bit output precision with the option of further scalable resolution. A pipelined time-to-digital conversion architecture further reduces conversion latency by performing computation in parallel, and an on-chip rectified linear unit (ReLU) suppresses unnecessary time-to-digital conversions for negative outputs, further improving energy efficiency. The proposed CIM prototype achieves a peak throughput of 639.38 GOPS and peak normalized energy efficiency of 1517.16 TOPS/W using 3-bit weights, 4-bit activations, and 10-bit outputs, with a measured matrix-vector multiplication (MVM) error deviation of less than 1%.

items.title: An Energy-Efficient 8 λ × 38-Gb/s/ λ Optical WDM Transmitter in 45-nm CMOS SOI
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a monolithically integrated eight-channel optical transmitter (OTX) based on wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM), which is implemented in a 45-nm CMOS SOI process. A scalable inductorless level-boosting driver is proposed to generate large output swings without level shifters or additional supply domains, enabling energy- and area-efficient operation. The driver is co-designed with microring modulators (MRMs) featuring capacitive fine-tuning with near-zero static power, supplemented by thermal tuning for coarse alignments when needed. An autonomous digital wavelength-locking loop ensures robust resonance alignment across all channels. The transmitter operates at 38 Gb/s per wavelength, achieving an aggregate data rate of 304 Gb/s and a bandwidth density of 2.1 Tb/s/mm2. Concurrent error-free operation (BER${\lt }~10{^{-12}}$) across all channels is demonstrated. The driver-MRM pair achieves an energy efficiency of 106 fJ/b, while the complete eight-channel transmitter achieves a chip-level energy efficiency of 330 fJ/b, including the pre-drivers and wavelength-locking circuitry with a minimum thermal-tuning overhead.

items.title: A 60-V High-Linearity Shunt-Based In-Line Current Sensor With DLL-Assisted Dynamic Body-Biasing and High dV/dt PWM Rejection Up to 2 MHz
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a fully integrated shunt-resistor-based in-line current sensor for high-voltage (HV) pulse-width modulation (PWM)-based power systems. Floating-Gm current sensors are effective at rejecting HV PWM common-mode (CM) interference, but their linearity degrades at high CM voltages due to the substrate current-induced body effect (SCBE) in HV laterally diffused metal-oxide-semiconductor (LDMOS) devices. This article proposes a delay-locked loop (DLL)-assisted dynamic body-biasing (DBB) technique to suppress SCBE-induced distortion while avoiding large switching glitches during PWM transitions. By dynamically controlling the body connection of the LDMOS devices, the proposed scheme significantly improves sensor linearity. The DLL predicts the PWM falling edge and provides accurate timing for the DBB control over a wide PWM frequency range. Implemented in a 0.18-$\mu $m BCD process, the sensor achieves up to 31-dB HD2 and 14-dB total harmonic distortion plus noise (THD+N) improvement, with a peak THD+N of −82.3 dB at 4 A and 1 kHz. It supports a 60-V CM voltage, rejects PWM interference up to 2 MHz with high$dV\mathrm {/}dt$(~1.5 V/ns), and consumes 1.7-mA current.

items.title: A Continuous-Time Incremental Zoom ADC With Extended Quantization, Easy-to-Drive Capacitive Input and Deadband-Embedded Gm-C Loop Filter
items.journal: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.venue_name: IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits
items.summary: This article presents a continuous-time (CT) analog-to-digital converter (ADC) featuring an incremental zoom with extended quantization architecture. The proposed MASH topology comprises an 8-bit oversampled successive-approximation register (SAR) ADC as the first stage, a 1-bit incremental CT delta-sigma modulator (CT-DSM) as the second stage, and a 12-bit Nyquist SAR ADC as the final stage. This architecture achieves a high signal-to-quantization noise ratio (SQNR) with a low oversampling ratio (OSR). To relax the requirements on the input driver, the ADC incorporates a chopped coupling-based capacitive input network. Furthermore, to achieve high efficiency and a high signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), a high-linearity Gm-C integrator employing low-noise deadband operation is introduced. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, the ADC achieves 94.4 dB signal-to-noise-and-distortion ratio (SNDR) and a 95.5 dB dynamic range (DR) over a 100 kHz analog bandwidth under 1 MS/s sampling rate. Consuming only 793 uW of power, the ADC yields a state-of-the-art Schreier figure of merit (FoMs) of 182.3 dB.

The Boolean satisfiability (SAT), a canonical nondeterministic polynomial (NP)-complete problem, has remained a focal point due to its wide applicability in artificial intelligence, cryptography, and formal verification. items.abstract_text: Recent years have seen growing interest in custom and nature-inspired computing methods for solving computationally challenging combinatorial optimization problems. The Boolean satisfiability (SAT), a canonical nondeterministic polynomial (NP)-complete problem, has remained a focal point due to its wide applicability in artificial intelligence, cryptography, and formal verification. This article presents a custom mixed-signal hardware SAT solver that maps the cost function of three-SAT instances onto an array of current-coupled computational nodes. The system progressively minimizes the cost function while employing an integrated perturbation mechanism to escape local minima. The proposed architecture is implemented in a standard 65-nm CMOS technology and experimentally evaluated. A central open question in the analog computation domain is the scalability of analog and mixed-signal architectures under inherent nonidealities. Beyond demonstrating functional correctness, this work systematically characterizes the impact of deviations inherent to analog computation, including coupling strength mismatch and nodal threshold variations. Measurement results reveal that solver performance is highly sensitive to random mismatch and largely insensitive to threshold variation. These effects are further elucidated through controlled experiments, such as random clause shuffling, selective sample pruning, and autozeroing, offering design guidance for scalable analog and mixed-signal optimization accelerators. Experimental results show that the fabricated integrated circuit achieves a median solution time of$9.75~\mu $s per instance with a median energy consumption of 118 nJ across the uniform random 50-variable SATLIB benchmark instances.

This article presents a fully digital, reference-less droop detection and mitigation circuit utilizing a shared dual-mode delay line (SDMDL). The proposed circuit unifies a time-to-digital converter (TDC)-based droop detector and a digitally controlled oscillator (DCO)-based droop mitigator into SDMDL, enabling direct ratio-based frequency reduction. Furthermore, a time-domain glitch-free recovery circuit (GFRC) is employed to guarantee seamless clock source switching from DCO to the input clock through phase alignment, preventing timing violations during the recovery phase. Fabricated in a 28-nm CMOS process, the proposed design demonstrates a droop mitigation latency of only half a clock cycle and frequency reduction range of 60% with a fine resolution of 2.5%. In addition, compared to prior art, the design achieves the highest${V} {_{\min }}$reduction of 14.8% and a throughput improvement of 42.9% under a 15%${V} {_{\text {DD}}}$droop while consuming 7.11 mW and occupying 0.0131 mm2.

report.title: AI for IC 研究动向分析（发表日 2026-11-01 至 2026-11-14 窗口）

overview.text: 本窗口共 26 条材料：25 篇论文（17 篇 ACM TODAES 期刊题录、8 篇 arXiv 作者预印本）与 1 条芯片设计博客新闻。内容集中在 AI for IC 的四类议题：LLM 辅助 RTL 与模拟电路设计、物理设计与 PPA/时序预测、可靠性与硬件安全分析、EDA 数据与问答工具。整体有两条主线：其一，以大语言模型为中心，把仿真器或综合工具放进生成循环，用工具反馈驱动生成与修复；其二，用图神经网络、CNN、RNN 等专用模型充当昂贵分析（时序、拥塞、电迁移、TDDB、光刻热点）的快速代理。新闻侧只有 1 条简介级材料，主要提供产业叙事，不能作为技术结论的证据。

evidence.quote: SPICE simulation feedback and current LLM advancements, such as reasoning, significantly increase the solve rate
an end-to-end layout-aware timing prediction approach that can achieve better accuracy by leveraging important layout information

trends.title: 从文本生成到“工具在环”：LLM 设计闭环以物理反馈与细粒度奖励为核心

observation.text: 多篇材料把外部工具反馈作为机制核心：在 PCB 开关电源设计中引入 SPICE 仿真反馈后，269 个手工基准任务求解率由 15% 升至 91%；在 C++ 到 Verilog 的高层综合流程中，作者训练 QoR 预测奖励模型，以低成本连续奖励替代反复调用真实综合；在 RTL PPA 优化中，作者用商业综合结果训练偏好奖励模型，在固定综合调用预算下筛选候选；在模拟电路设计中，作者用仿真反馈增强的强化微调进一步优化模型。

evidence.quote: SPICE simulation feedback and current LLM advancements, such as reasoning, significantly increase the solve rate
we design the QoR Prediction Reward Model (QoR RM), which predicts latency and resource metrics by encoding RTL into long-context semantic representations
we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes
simulation feedback-augmented reinforcement fine-tuning, which further optimizes models using simulation-grounded rewards

interpretation.text: 据本期材料推断，研究关注点已从“模型能否写出电路”转向如何把昂贵且稀缺的工具反馈压缩成可优化信号，并同时控制调用预算；射频参数提取工作中把高级优化决策映射为商业工具可执行命令，也属于同一取向。这些工作基准与工艺节点各异，其数值增益不可横向比较。

evidence.quote: high-level optimization decisions are mapped into executable commands for commercial extraction tools
we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes

trends.title: 验证被前置：形式化断言与等价性检查进入 AI 生成硬件流程

observation.text: 两篇材料把验证直接嵌入生成与恢复流程：一篇提出快照式方法，用 LLM 自动生成并迭代修复 SystemVerilog 断言，把设计当前功能固化为一组形式断言；另一篇在门级网表恢复 RTL 时以独立验证建立恢复结果与原电路的等价关系。

evidence.quote: a novel snapshot methodology that captures the current functionality of a design as a comprehensive set of formal assertions
Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit.

interpretation.text: 由此推断，验证不再只是流程末端的过滤器，而成为可复用资产（断言集、等价证明）与训练信号来源；材料同时指出仿真通常只给出模块级通过或不通过，这种粗粒度结果会丢弃部分正确实现中的可用证据，说明验证反馈本身的粒度也需设计。

trends.title: 物理与可靠性分析的代理模型走向“物理约束＋可解释＋轻量化”

observation.text: 一批材料用学习模型替代昂贵的数值或仿真分析：布局感知的时序预测模型利用布线耦合信息提升精度；跨工艺角时序预测采用 XGBoost，并用 SHAP 量化关键贡献因素；时钟网格采用图神经网络代理模型，同时预测功耗、延迟与偏差直方图。

evidence.quote: an end-to-end layout-aware timing prediction approach that can achieve better accuracy by leveraging important layout information
we employ SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis to interpret the XGBoost model, quantifying key contributors to cross-corner timing variations
We propose a Graph Neural Network (GNN) based surrogate model of the clock mesh with a new graph representation and a new architecture

interpretation.text: 可解释性在部分材料中已从附加说明变为可信度的一部分（片上遥测异常检测强调因果保留的互信息与 SHAP 归因），同时出现轻量化部署诉求（多模态拥塞预测强调参数规模与推理速度）。是否构成整体趋势，本窗口材料不足以判断，仅能说明这些关注点同时出现。

evidence.quote: a hybrid explainability framework that integrates Causal-Preserving Mutual Information (CP–MI) with SHAP-based feature attribution
a novel lightweight multimodal model for congestion prediction that simultaneously processes feature maps and heterogeneous graphs

connections.text: 产业侧博客提出的“智能体化 AI 采用路径”强调把灵活的 AI 栈与可信的、基于物理的工程工具结合，与本期论文中把仿真/综合工具置入生成循环的做法方向一致。但该新闻仅为简介级材料（只有标题与一句话提要），且与论文出自不同发布方，不能视为对论文结论的独立验证；此处仅作方向性对照。

evidence.quote: combine flexible AI stacks with trusted, physics-based engineering tools

connections.text: 跨子领域存在一个共性技术问题：把粗粒度结果转换为细粒度可优化信号。RTL 生成侧提出语句级信用分配，综合优化侧用成对排序构造偏好奖励，射频参数提取侧把高级决策转换为确定性工具命令。三者的方法不同、任务不同，此处联系属于基于摘要的比较性推断，而非相互引用或同一实验的重复报道。

we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes
high-level optimization decisions are mapped into executable commands for commercial extraction tools

question.text: 在固定的商业综合/仿真调用预算下，如果把 RTL 改写前后的形式化断言快照作为跨迭代持久回归信号，并与语句级信用分配结合构成复合奖励，能否在保持功能等价的前提下稳定改善综合后 PPA？

The resulting changes in signal-level errors are combined with behavioral agreement to form a continuous statement credit
we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes

motivation.text: 动机来自三处材料拼接：断言快照被描述为可用于校验后续（人或 AI 所做）变更的回归套件；现有仿真反馈多为模块级通过或不通过，难以定位是哪条语句造成输出行为；同时综合调用昂贵，已有工作以偏好奖励模型在预算约束下筛选候选。三者组合后，一个尚未在本期材料中被同时处理的问题是：等价性约束如何以细粒度、可持续的方式进入同一条优化回路。此问题仅为候选建议，材料并未表明其新颖性或无人研究。

evidence.quote: a novel snapshot methodology that captures the current functionality of a design as a comprehensive set of formal assertions
simulation commonly provides a coarse module-level pass/fail outcome
we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes

approach: 选定 RTL 改写基准与种子模块集，对每个种子自动生成 SystemVerilog 断言并做去重与集合扩展，形成版本化的断言快照，作为后续每次改写的回归基线。
搭建迭代改写回路：LLM 生成候选 RTL，先用编译与快速仿真做等价粗筛，再对输出驱动赋值片段做反事实干预，得到语句级信用，仅对高信用候选调用商业综合并回收 PPA 指标。
把等价性通过与断言回归通过作为硬约束或门控项，与 PPA 增益共同构成复合奖励；训练偏好或奖励模型时显式记录并限制每轮综合调用次数，对比有/无断言快照两种设定。
validation: 功能正确性：对最终设计执行独立形式等价检查与断言回归，报告等价通过率、断言覆盖率与失败类型分布，而非仅汇报模块级通过或不通过。
收益与成本：在相同综合调用预算下比较 PPA 改进的分布与所需调用次数，并做三组消融，分别去掉断言快照、语句级信用、奖励模型。
稳健性：在至少两个工艺节点及未参与训练的设计上复测，检查增益是否保持；因属候选设计，结论只可声明在所用基准与工艺范围内成立。

limitations: 仅依据题名与摘要/简介分析，未阅读全文，无法核验实验设置、基准细节与统计显著性。
材料仅覆盖本地所选窗口（26 条），未做系统检索，不能据此推断领域整体规模，也不能用单一窗口证明任何增长或下降趋势。
新闻材料仅 1 条且为简介级（标题加一句话提要），与论文之间缺少可核验的对应关系，相关关联仅作方向性对照，不构成独立证据。
25 篇论文中 8 篇为 arXiv 作者预印本，未经同行评审；期刊题录亦仅有摘要级信息，两类来源证据强度不同，正文措辞已相应弱化。
多篇材料各自报告的性能数字（如求解率、加速比、误差）来自不同基准与工艺节点，不可横向比较或合并为总体结论。
日期筛选依据发表日，收录时间与发表时间可能不一致，预印本的 publication_year 字段缺失，历史补录情况无法排除。
