sources.title: Type-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Network for Circuit Link Prediction
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Link prediction for circuit completion is a crucial task in Electronic Design Automation (EDA), aiming to infer missing connections in incomplete circuits to accelerate design workflows and ensure Printed Circuit Board (PCB) reliability. However, due to the practical reality that circuit connectivity is defined by nets that connect specific pins of component instances, existing methods that rely on homogeneous representations and scalar shortest path distances collapse pin-level constraints into a single proximity signal. This collapse obscures component identities and pin semantics, and fails to capture long-range functional paths, which can slow design closure and potentially compromise PCB reliability by increasing the risk of electrically invalid links and subsequent rework. Addressing these challenges, we present a T ype-aware H eterogeneous G raph network for C ircuit link prediction ( THGC ), which enables accurate circuit link prediction by explicitly preserving component functional semantics and modeling type-aware dependencies. Specifically, THGC constructs a circuit-aware heterogeneous graph from netlists to preserve physical connectivity and component semantics, and refines representations through a multi-view encoder with Type-Aware Distance Encoding (TADE) to capture non-local dependencies. It then performs circuit-oriented link prediction using a heterogeneous graph network with dense convolutions and global sort pooling, optimized by a composite objective enforcing topological and semantic consistency, to predict electrically feasible missing connections for circuit completion. Comprehensive experiments are performed on 6,195 circuits collected from three benchmarks, and the results demonstrate that THGC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to a 47.51% relative improvement in terms of AUC. These results confirm that THGC effectively preserves component functional semantics and captures type-aware non-local dependencies for accurate circuit link prediction. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/THGC .
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: X-OCTANE: eXplainable On-Chip Telemetry-based Anomaly Notification Engine for Silicon Lifecycle Management
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Silicon Lifecycle Management (SLM) is essential for ensuring the reliability, security, and performance of modern computing platforms. Conventional SLM approaches rely on off-chip or software-only analytics, which lack on-die interpretability. We present X-OCTANE, an explainable on-chip telemetry-based anomaly notification engine. X–OCTANE is a hybrid explainability framework that integrates Causal-Preserving Mutual Information (CP–MI) with SHAP-based feature attribution for interpretable feature ranking and selection. The proposed feature rank-and-selection procedure retains competitive safety-oriented anomaly detection and bolsters security-specific in-field monitoring of compute platforms. For the 7 nm ASAP technology, X-OCTANE achieves competitive anomaly detection performance with less than 0.50% CPU die area and 1.0% non-idle power overhead. In addition, X–OCTANE improves anomaly-driven diagnosis accuracy by over 7% on average. Experimental validation using the PAMPAR benchmark suite on two separate experimental platforms demonstrates enhanced anomaly detection and diagnosis through the proposed explainable feature-rank-and-selection method. X–OCTANE establishes a scalable and transparent foundation for on-chip SLM analytics, unifying detection fidelity with causal interpretability.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: Evaluating LLM-based Workflows for Switched-Mode Power Supply Design
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) have great potential to enhance productivity in many disciplines, such as software engineering. However, it is unclear to what extent they can assist in the design process of electronic circuits. This article focuses on the application of LLMs to switched-mode power supply (SMPS) design for printed circuit boards (PCBs). We present multiple LLM-based workflows that combine reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a custom toolkit that enables the LLM to interact with the SPICE circuit simulator to receive physical feedback. Two benchmark experiments are presented to analyze the performance of LLM-based assistants on various design tasks. These include parameter tuning and topology adaption, as well as design optimization of SMPS circuits through optimal catalogue component selection to maximize circuit efficiency or balance multiple objectives like size, ripple, and component loss. Experiment results show that SPICE simulation feedback and current LLM advancements, such as reasoning, significantly increase the solve rate on 269 manually created benchmark tasks from 15% to 91%. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that most parameter tuning design tasks can be solved, while limits remain for certain topology adaption and multi-objective optimization tasks. Our experiments offer insights for improving current concepts, for example by adapting text-based circuit representations.
topics: AI辅助模拟与射频电路设计

sources.title: LLMsafe-Spectre: Efficient Spectre Attack Detection in LLM Environments using An Intelligent HPC events Selection Methodology
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) is transforming computing paradigms while introducing new challenges in hardware security vulnerability detection. Existing hardware performance counter (HPC)-based detectors demonstrate high efficacy for conventional applications (e.g., editing Office files, and playing videos) as well as web-accessible LLMs; however, our novel observation reveals that locally deployed large-scale LLMs exhibit access patterns with striking similarity to Spectre attacks. This similarity causes a dramatic deterioration in attack detection accuracy, plummeting from 99.86% to just 66.16% for DeepSeek-7b. To effectively mitigate detection performance degradation, we propose for the first time, LLMsafe-Spectre, a novel intelligent HPC event selection methodology designed for efficient Spectre attack detection in LLM environments. LLMsafe-Spectre is composed of two phases: (1) AI-assisted clustering of HPC events to efficiently narrow the search space, (2) ANOVA-based statistical analysis of inner-group and inter-group variances to pick out Top-K Spectre attack-LLMs discriminative events under limited registers in processors. This approach uniquely addresses the interference caused by LLM access while maintaining detection robustness. We comprehensively evaluate LLMsafe-Spectre across diverse Spectre variants, hardware architectures, web accessible LLMs and locally deployed large-scale LLMs scaling up from 1.5b to 14b. Experimental results demonstrate that our novel solution achieves superior detection accuracy up to 99.91% on average of scaling LLMs, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art approaches.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: Will AI mess my RTL? A snapshot-based approach to verifying AI-written RTL
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: With the growing interest in using AI (Artificial Intelligence) for RTL (Register-Transfer Level) hardware development, robust and comprehensive verification has become more important than ever. As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly assist in creating and modifying RTL designs, ensuring that these changes preserve existing functionality is paramount for building trust in AI-driven workflows. We present SVApshot, a fully automated framework that leverages LLMs to generate and systematically attempt to correct SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) for RTL modules, completely removing the human from the generation loop. SVApshot introduces a novel snapshot methodology that captures the current functionality of a design as a comprehensive set of formal assertions, creating a regression suite for validating future changes--whether made by humans or AI. The framework features automated duplicate detection, assertion set expansion, and iterative repair of failing assertions using LLM-guided debugging with formal verification feedback. Our experimental evaluation across diverse RTL modules demonstrates high coverage for complex modules, with successful detection of both manually-injected and AI-introduced bugs. Additionally, this framework opens the door for automatic generation of formal testbenches to benchmark LLMs for hardware design, moving beyond binary pass/fail metrics towards nuanced assertion-based scoring.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: Causal Signal Credit Assignment for Verilog Code Generation via Counterfactual Hardware Verification
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Large language models have improved Verilog generation, yet functional correctness remains difficult to optimize because simulation commonly provides a coarse module-level pass/fail outcome. Such feedback discards useful evidence from partially correct RTL modules and cannot determine whether a source statement is functionally responsible for an observed output behavior. We present a new method named Causal Signal Credit Assignment (CSCA), which is a counterfactual preference-optimization framework for Verilog generation. CSCA first performs continuous signal-level behavioral verification on sampled candidate modules. It then locates output-driving assignment spans and applies five interventions while holding the remaining module and testbench fixed. The resulting changes in signal-level errors are combined with behavioral agreement to form a continuous statement credit, which is mapped to response-token weights for strict weighted direct preference optimization. This enables CSCA to learn from locally supported statements without uniformly reinforcing an otherwise incorrect response. Built on Icarus Verilog and a CodeV-derived corpus, CSCA is evaluated on VerilogEval~2.0 and RTLLM~v2.0, including both code completion and specification-to-RTL tasks. With a Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct backbone, CSCA leads the evaluated 7B-scale models and remains comparable to the much larger GPT-5.4-mini on the reported Verilog-generation benchmarks.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: Agentic AI Should Fit the Way You Engineer
sources.excerpt: Explore three agentic AI adoption paths that help chip design teams combine flexible AI stacks with trusted, physics-based engineering tools.

sources.title: PRISM: Preference-based Reward and Uncertainty-Integrated Synthesis Minimization for RTL PPA Optimization
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: This paper introduces a budget-aware, multi-objective framework (called PRISM) for RTL optimization that improves power, performance, and area (PPA) while sharply limiting expensive commercial synthesis tool calls. Starting from a synthesizable baseline and functional testbench, the method iterates through LLM-driven rewrite generation, fast compile/simulation equivalence filtering, low-cost proxy feature extraction, and selective commercial synthesis tool (Synopsys Design Compiler (DC)) evaluation. To prioritize which candidates deserve high-quality synthesis, we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes, and combine ensemble uncertainty with a diversity-aware acquisition rule to avoid early bias and redundant evaluations. A key advantage is that PRISM maintains a best-tradeoff set G of non-dominated designs throughout the run: G preserves the best solutions found so far, is fed back into generation and refinement, and enables consistent, cumulative improvements rather than repeatedly restarting from the baseline. Across RTLLM v2.0 modules, the approach consistently yields post-synthesis gains under fixed commercial synthesis tool call budgets, and ablations confirm that reward-guided selection and candidate dropping are central to sample-efficient progress. PRISM efficacy is evaluated across multiple technology nodes (7 nm, 15 nm, and 45 nm) using identical pipelines without retraining.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: AutoC2V: Synthesis-Guided LLM Training for QoR-Optimized C++-to-Verilog Generation
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: High-level synthesis (HLS) can translate C/C++ kernels into register-transfer level (RTL) designs, yet generating high-quality hardware still relies heavily on manual pragma tuning and repeated synthesis evaluation. We propose AutoC2V, a C++-to-Verilog generation framework driven by real synthesis feedback that enables large language models (LLMs) to directly generate RTL with improved quality of results (QoR) from synthesizable C++ kernels. We construct training data from real synthesis results, including synthesizable C++ source code, the corresponding Verilog RTL, QoR metrics, and optimization objectives. Using this dataset, we align the model toward synthesis-aware RTL generation through Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To reduce the high cost of repeatedly invoking real synthesis during GRPO, we design the QoR Prediction Reward Model (QoR RM), which predicts latency and resource metrics by encoding RTL into long-context semantic representations, thereby providing low-cost and continuous QoR reward signals for policy optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that AutoC2V not only substantially improves RTL functional pass rates, but also achieves superior latency and resource optimization compared to the unfine-tuned base model, representative HLS optimization approaches (HLSPilot, LLM-DSE, and AutoDSE), and advanced general-purpose commercial models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek v4 Pro, and GLM-5.2). These results indicate that combining real synthesis data with efficient QoR reward modeling can further improve the ability of LLMs to generate high-quality RTL.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Recovering high-level RTL from such representations therefore helps engineers understand a circuit's functionality and enables RTL rewriting and resynthesis. A plausible function model is also insufficient unless the generated RTL is equivalent to the original circuit for all input combinations. In this paper, we present RTLREX, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools for function recovery, RTL generation, independent verification, and cost-guided rewriting. Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit. The LLM uses tool feedback to select further analyses, revise candidate RTL, and propose syntax-cost reductions. Experiments on 30 benchmarks from Problem A of the ICCAD 2022 CAD Contest show that RTLREX recovers equivalent high-level RTL for all benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art method WolFEx in recovery coverage. On benchmarks recovered by both methods, RTLREX reduces mean syntax cost by 20.5% relative to WolFEx. On complete truth-table benchmarks from the IWLS 2026 Contest, our framework reduces mean syntax cost by 95.7% relative to an LLM agent baseline on the benchmarks validated by both methods.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: ModelAuflow: A Highly Scaffolded LLM-Orchestrated Framework for RF Passive Device Parameter Extraction
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Accurate parameter extraction for RF passive devices is a critical step in semiconductor design because compact models directly determine the reliability of circuit simulation. Conventional extraction remains highly iterative and depends on substantial expert intervention for parameter grouping, optimizer selection, range adjustment, and curve-quality assessment. This article presents ModelAuflow, a highly scaffolded LLM-orchestrated framework for RF passive-device parameter extraction. The framework combines structured LLM reasoning with deterministic strategy conversion so that high-level optimization decisions are mapped into executable commands for commercial extraction tools. To improve convergence efficiency, the system integrates sensitivity-aware parameter filtering, historical self-reflection, and a classification knowledge base. Across the evaluated RF passive-device cases, the framework reduced the RMSE of a complex inductor below 3.5%, a capacitor below 2%, and a resistor below 1%. Under favorable initial conditions, the shortest successful extraction required 134 seconds and one optimization attempt. These results indicate that schema-constrained LLM orchestration can substantially reduce continuous manual intervention while maintaining accurate extraction for the evaluated RF passive-device workflows.
topics: AI辅助模拟与射频电路设计

sources.title: A CNN-Based Technique to Assist Layout-to-Generator Conversion for Analog Circuits
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: We propose a technique to assist in converting a reference layout of an analog circuit into the procedural layout generator by efficiently reusing available generators for sub-cell creation. The proposed convolutional neural network (CNN) model automatically detects sub-cells that can be generated by available generator scripts in the library, and suggests using them in the hierarchically correct places of the generator software. In experiments, the CNN model examined sub-cells of a high-speed wireline receiver that has a total of 4,885 sub-cell instances including 145 different sub-cell designs. The CNN model classified the sub-cell instances into 51 generatable and one not-generatable classes. One not-generatable class indicates that no available generator can generate the classified sub-cell. The CNN model achieved 99.3% precision in examining the 145 different sub-cell designs. The CNN model greatly reduced the examination time to 18 seconds from 88 minutes required in manual examination. Also, the proposed CNN model could correctly classify unfamiliar sub-cells that are very different from the training dataset.
topics: AI辅助模拟与射频电路设计

sources.title: DECODE: Detecting Structural Obfuscation in HLS based DSP Designs using Machine Learning Framework
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Structural obfuscation has been a widely used hardware security technique that is used to transform the internal structure of a high-level synthesis (HLS) digital signal processing (DSP) intellectual property (IP) design such that it becomes unobvious and obscure. The intent is to thwart deobfuscation/reverse-engineering (RE) attempts. These transformations in structurally obfuscated DSP designs are elusive and non-intuitive, making them arduous to identify and detect from an attacker's perspective. In this article, we for the first time, present a novel strategy for detecting structural obfuscation in HLS based DSP designs using machine learning (ML) frameworks. This article presents a novel technique called ‘DECODE’ : DE tecting Stru C tural O bfuscation in HLS based D SP Designs using Machine L E arning Framework . The presented approach introduces a set of unique/distinct features that can successfully classify between structurally obfuscated HLS DSP designs and its non-obfuscated versions. The article also presents a novel ML database consisting of several instances of structurally obfuscated and un-obfuscated DSP HLS designs that can be fed into our ML framework (logistic regression and random forest classifier). Results of the proposed approach revealed successful detection of structurally obfuscated DSP designs with high accuracy.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: SAFTAC: Simulation-Augmented Fine-Tuning of Open-Source LLMs for Analog Circuit Design
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Circuit design for analog integrated circuits (ICs) is challenging because circuit topology, device sizing, and circuit performance are tightly coupled. Existing large language model (LLM)-based methods either rely on inference-time correction around frozen models or train on limited circuit types without directly using simulation outcomes as training signals. A key bottleneck is that existing datasets do not provide sufficient task information for training LLMs on end-to-end specification-conditioned design. To fill this gap, we first construct a large-scale simulation-grounded dataset with 8,626 design tasks across 10 different types of analog circuits, where each task includes a textual description, labeled I/O ports, loading condition, target specifications, a testbench, and a reference netlist. Using this dataset, we present SAFTAC, a simulation-augmented fine-tuning framework that trains LLMs to generate and revise analog circuit design. SAFTAC combines three-stage supervised fine-tuning, which progressively builds the capabilities required for analog circuit design and feedback-guided correction, with simulation feedback-augmented reinforcement fine-tuning, which further optimizes models using simulation-grounded rewards. We evaluate SAFTAC under single-pass generation and two-pass generation with simulation feedback, showing improvements over the strongest closed-source LLM by 15.9% and 7.8%, respectively.
topics: AI辅助模拟与射频电路设计

sources.title: Power Switch Network Optimization Using Machine Learning for Inrush Current and Wakeup Latency Prediction
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Today’s large-scale designs leverage power gating to achieve low power consumption, which necessitates the design of an efficient power switch network that accounts for both inrush current and wakeup latency. Optimizing this power switch network involves striking a balance between minimizing inrush current and reducing wakeup latency. However, analyzing inrush and wakeup latency for a given network is computationally expensive, particularly for complex systems, making optimization frameworks that rely on analysis engines prohibitively slow. To address this challenge, we frame the analysis of inrush and wakeup latency as a regression problem and train machine-learning (ML) models to predict these metrics. The ML model achieves mean errors of less than 10% for inrush current prediction and for wakeup latency prediction, while providing a speedup of over 50× compared to SPICE. By leveraging an ML model, we efficiently explore the design space and identify optimized power switch network patterns that minimize both wakeup latency and inrush current.
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: Fast Electromigration Analysis of Multi-segment Interconnects Based on Recurrent Neural Networks
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Predicting electromigration (EM) stress is a critical reliability challenge in power delivery networks. Existing semi-analytical Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) models neglect the Markovian sequential dependencies of EM diffusion and suffer from severe scalability issues due to global topological evaluations. To address these architectural and computational bottlenecks, this article proposes a dynamic spatiotemporal stress forecasting framework. Specifically, a physics-aligned Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) is constructed to directly model the Markovian sequential evolution of EM stress. This is integrated with a tensor mapping-based dynamic local subgraph extraction strategy, effectively isolating spatial complexity from the global interconnect scale. At the numerical integration level, we develop a physics-driven adaptive hybrid convolution algorithm. Regulated by a stress relaxation time constant, this algorithm dynamically invokes discrete convolution during the early acceleration phase to strictly preserve the abrupt variations of the auxiliary function used for stress computation, and seamlessly switches to Gauss-Legendre quadrature during stable periods to maximize precision while eliminating smoothing artifacts. Furthermore, a simulation-time-based optimization strategy is incorporated to mitigate the prediction error gap between early and late simulation stages. Experimental results validate the efficiency of the proposed framework. Compared with the MLP baseline, our model achieves up to a 93.2% reduction in relative error and a 117.79× computational speedup. Against the Finite Element Method (FEM), it delivers up to 1335.6× acceleration while maintaining engineering-grade accuracy.
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: LE-Timing: Layout-Aware and Explainable Timing Prediction
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Accurate and fast timing prediction at early design stages is crucial for achieving timing closure in very-large-scale integration (VLSI) design. Machine learning (ML) based approaches have been widely adopted for timing prediction to pursue both accuracy and speed. Unfortunately, these approaches fail to fully exploit the layout features, which can significantly impact the timing metrics, thus leading to great accuracy degradation. In this article, we propose LE-Timing, an end-to-end layout-aware timing prediction approach that can achieve better accuracy by leveraging important layout information. The key insight is that crucial information about coupling capacitance between routing wires can significantly impact timing metrics, and fully exploiting this layout information in the timing prediction model can substantially improve its accuracy. However, efficiently leveraging layout features while maintaining accuracy poses three key challenges: node-level layout-graph integration, domain experience utilization and training efficiency. To address these, we further propose three key technologies specially designed for LE-Timing correspondingly, including a layout-encoding net model, an explainable cell model, and an explicit-message-passing scheme. Experimental results on 16 open-source designs with an advanced 7-nm technology node demonstrate that LE-Timing achieves R 2 score 0.94 for arrival time prediction and lower error accumulation compared to the baselines.
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: Fast TDDB Hotspot Detection of Large-Scale BEOL Circuits Using Physics-Informed Central Emphasized CNN
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Time-Dependent Dielectric Breakdown (TDDB) has emerged as a critical reliability concern in Back-End-of-Line (BEOL) interconnects. In Electric Path Generation (EPG) based TDDB analysis, the evolution of metal ion concentration is governed by a Partial Differential Equation (PDE). Traditional numerical methods for solving this equation are time-consuming and demand considerable computational resources, making them impractical for large-scale circuits analysis. To address this challenge, we propose a physics-informed learning framework for fast prediction of ion concentration distributions in large BEOL layouts. The framework represents BEOL patterns as two-dimensional images, partitions large layouts into overlapping sub-graphs for encoding, and predicts transient concentration fields for each sub-graph. Based on the reconstructed full-layout concentration map, the method supports efficient TDDB hotspot analysis. The proposed Physics-Informed Central Emphasized Convolutional Neural Network (PICE-CNN) is applicable to diverse interconnect patterns and operating conditions, including different line widths, line spacings, and supply voltages. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves up to 357.1× speedup over conventional numerical solvers while maintaining high prediction accuracy, with the mean squared error below 1× 10 -4 in the emphasized central region.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: CHARIOT: A Communication-Aware Exploration Framework for 2.5D/3D Silicon Interposer Design
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Interposer design is crucial for optimizing inter-chiplet communication efficiency, performance, and energy consumption in 2.5D/3D integrated systems. To facilitate performance analysis and design space exploration (DSE) of interposers, this work presents CHARIOT, a fast, comprehensive exploration framework that establishes a systematic methodology for analyzing and exploring the design space of both passive and active interposers’ architecture. The design space of interposers is first developed to evaluate system performance. Then a roofline model-based methodology is introduced to analyze the bottleneck of performance. A multi-objective Bayesian optimization-based DSE framework, CHARIOT, is proposed, featuring a scheduling engine tailored to different interposer types and a communication-aware exploration engine for coordinated multi-objective exploration of the design space. Compared to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) chiplet system, the CHARIOT-generated optimal passive and active interposer designs achieve energy efficiency improvement up to 1.33× and 1.96×, as well as performance gains up to 1.49× and 1.75× speed-up. The Pareto frontiers of competitive design choices enable selecting the most suitable option based on the designers’ requirements.
topics: AI辅助芯粒与架构搜索

sources.title: CGNet: A Lightweight Multimodal Framework for Congestion Prediction in VLSI Physical Design
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Early access to accurate congestion information can effectively optimize the physical design flow of modern very large scale integration (VLSI) circuits. Existing unimodal models suffer from limited feature utilization and insufficient prediction accuracy, while current multimodal approaches typically involve large parameter sizes, slow inference, and high computational complexity, making them difficult to apply in time-critical tasks. To address these limitations, we propose CGNet, a novel lightweight multimodal model for congestion prediction that simultaneously processes feature maps and heterogeneous graphs. To enable efficient feature fusion without significantly increasing model complexity, we incorporate a cross-stitch module. Furthermore, we propose a heterogeneous graph compression method that significantly simplifies the graph structure, thereby reducing the computational complexity of processing heterogeneous graphs and improving the prediction speed of the model. Additionally, we design a composite loss function that jointly captures global structures and local details. For a more comprehensive evaluation, we propose a localized metric, intersection over union (IOU), and integrate the predicted congestion maps into the downstream design rule check (DRC) violation prediction task. Experimental results in the CircuitNet-N28 dataset demonstrate that CGNet consistently outperforms the best-performing model in both prediction accuracy and prediction speed.
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: PolarGate: Breaking the Functionality Representation Bottleneck of And-Inverter Graph Neural Network
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Understanding the functionality of Boolean networks is crucial for processes such as functional equivalence checking, logic synthesis, and malicious logic identification. With the proliferation of deep learning in electronic design automation (EDA), graph neural networks (GNNs) are widely used to embed and-inverter graphs (AIGs)—a standard form of Boolean networks—into vectorized representations. A key challenge in applying GNNs for Boolean representation is that although GNNs can effectively encapsulate the structural properties of AIGs, they struggle to efficiently capture Boolean logic functionality. In this work, we focus on breaking this bottleneck by enhancing the functional representation capability of GNNs, proposing PolarGate, an efficient solution that not only aligns message passing with AIG logical functionality but also effectively integrates global information. Leveraging the intrinsic ambipolar states (0 and 1) of AIG nodes, PolarGate maps gate behavior into an ambipolar state space, customizes differentiable logical operators, and designs a functionality-aware message passing strategy. To further capture global circuit information, PolarGate integrates a structure-aware preprocessing module and a global linear attention module, transcending the locality constraint of message passing. Experimental results on two functionality-related basic tasks (signal probability prediction and truth-table distance prediction) and a downstream task (logic equivalence prediction) show that PolarGate outperform state-of-the-art GNN-based methods.
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: PCB-QA: A Task-Specific Question Answering Framework for Text-Centric Chip Datasheet Queries in PCB Design
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: In PCB design, engineers often rely on datasheets to obtain crucial chip information, a process that is both time-consuming and labor-intensive. To streamline this workflow, we present PCB-QA, a task-specific Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based question-answering system that automatically addresses text-centric chip-related queries using the latest datasheets. Rather than aiming to replace broader commercial AI-assisted EDA platforms, this work focuses on a narrower and reproducible research problem: grounded datasheet question answering over a maintained corpus. While existing RAG technologies have made significant progress in document-based question answering, several challenges remain, primarily due to the erroneous segmentation of documents, the retrieval of inaccurate references, and under-specified user queries. To improve the accuracy of PCB-QA’s responses, our framework incorporates three key components. First, we propose a datasheet segmentation model that is specifically trained to divide the corpus into semantically coherent chunks. Second, we integrate a correlation estimation module to better assess the relevance of retrieved references and reduce the influence of distractors. Finally, recognizing that user inputs may lack critical details, we employ a query-rationalization mechanism to facilitate further reasoning and refine the query for under-specified technical and application-related questions. These task-specific customizations improve retrieval quality and support more accurate grounded answers for datasheet-centric QA. Experimental results on our customized ChipQuestion benchmark demonstrate that PCB-QA achieves consistent improvements over representative RAG baselines on text-grounded datasheet QA. We also clarify the current scope of PCB-QA: the present implementation is primarily text-centric and does not yet fully address image-only figures, waveform plots, complex visual tables, or other visuallygrounded datasheet content.
topics: AI辅助EDA工具、数据与评测

sources.title: Multi-Scale Feature Refinement Network for Lithography Hotspot Detection
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: As semiconductor manufacturing advances toward smaller process nodes and more complex layouts, lithography hotspot detection faces increasing challenges. Traditional methods often struggle to capture subtle geometric variations in complex layouts, resulting in low recall and high False Alarm Rate (FA). To address this problem, we propose a Multi-Scale Feature Refinement Network (MSFRN). The key innovation lies in a collaborative “Extraction–Refinement–Decision” framework specifically designed for Hard-To-Classify samples: the Multi-Scale Feature Extraction module comprehensively captures rich information ranging from local geometric details to global layout context; the Feature Refinement Network enhances responses to critical geometric features through a lightweight gating mechanism; and finally, ConvNeXt serves as the decision module, integrating and classifying the refined features for final hotspot prediction. Experimental results show that on the most challenging ICCAD 2019-2 benchmark, MSFRN improves recall by up to 11.3%, with the FA varying from a 0.2% increase to a 5.8% reduction, demonstrating superior detection capability.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: Interpretable Cross-Corner Timing Prediction Based on XGBoost-SHAP Solution
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: With the continuous advancement of semiconductor technology, the explosive increase in the number of corners to be covered during chip design has imposed severe challenges on timing analysis resource and time cost. Recent studies on machine learning-based cross-corner timing prediction have emerged as a promising paradigm for accelerating multi-corner timing analysis. Those existing approaches predominantly rely on precomputed multi-corner timing analysis results or process technology parameters for model training, but suffer from limited industrial adoption due to the large number of training corners, the complex pre-training flow, and the opaque nature of the black-box architecture. In case of this, we propose an XGBoost-based cross-corner timing analysis framework that requires only a single-corner static timing analysis report as input to achieve high-precision timing prediction with an average mean absolute error of approximately 1.604 ps across corners. The proposed methodology has been validated through commercial projects based on different deep nanometer process nodes (7 nm and below), demonstrating robust performance stability. In the task of critical path identification and optimization, this proposed method achieves near-100% coverage with acceptable increase in additional STA overhead. Furthermore, we employ SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis to interpret the XGBoost model, quantifying key contributors to cross-corner timing variations. This not only enhances the explainability of the black-box model but also provides insights for design optimization and robustness improvement.
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: A Global Routing Method for Electronic Circuit Design Integrating Flow Matching and Constrained A*
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Global routing is a fundamental issue in the design of electronic circuits, as it directly relates to the efficiency, reliability, and compactness of the overall layout of integrated systems. As the demand for higher functionality and reliability within a limited chip area increases, the importance of routing as a design consideration has never been greater. Efficient global routing optimization techniques are therefore required to connect all pins with minimal wirelength (WL), while avoiding congestion and interference across multiple nets within the design space. As the number of nets to be routed increases, global routing inherently suffers from a combinatorial explosion in the design space, making it increasingly difficult to obtain feasible solutions. In this paper, we focus on solving constrained global routing problems based on a heuristic A*-based framework. Based on this concept, a hybrid approach is proposed by integrating constrained A* with flow matching (FM). The method utilizes FM to construct a global cost map that captures routing tendencies across the design space, which is then used to guide the constrained A* search process. This enables efficient exploration of the solution space while satisfying routing constraints. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves comparable WL and via usage to baseline methods while maintaining constraint satisfaction across a wide range of scenarios. Notably, the framework shows strong capability in solving complex routing instances that are difficult to handle using conventional approaches. Additionally, the method shows robust generalization performance across different problem sizes and net configurations.
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: A Surrogate Model for Variation-Aware Clock-Mesh Analysis and Design-Space Exploration using Graph Neural Networks
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Clock meshes are widely used in high-performance VLSI systems to minimize skew and tolerate On-Chip Variation (OCV) in nanometer technologies. However, analyzing meshes is difficult because reconvergent paths and multi-source drivers prevent static timing analysis (STA) tools from handling mesh loops, making SPICE the industrial standard. SPICE simulations are accurate but slow, so clock-mesh synthesis relies on approximate models that overlook critical effects such as non-linear buffer driving caused by input slew and input skew. We propose a Graph Neural Network (GNN) based surrogate model of the clock mesh with a new graph representation and a new architecture that predicts power while also improving the delay and slew predictions at the sinks and capturing the skew histogram under OCV. Trained on SPICE data and tested on unseen real designs, our model achieves average errors of $3.40$~ps in delay, $4.14$~ps in slew and $4.46$~ps in skew, compared with $6.28$~ps, $12.35$~ps, and $11.62$~ps for our prior model, and $74.37$~ps delay and $27.51$~ps skew for the approximate method used in current state-of-the-art works. Our model predicts power within $3.4\%$ of SPICE on average, while delivering $18\times$-$1706\times$ speed-ups over the approximate method under OCV modeling, enabling faster and more accurate clock-mesh design-space exploration. A case study on a real design further shows that our surrogate model finds buffering candidates that, at a balanced tradeoff, improves $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile skew by $49.1\%$, reduces power by $25.7\%$, and reduces area by $37.3\%$ at the cost of a $6.8\%$ increase in $99^{\text{th}}$-percentile maximum slew as compared to the state-of-the-art work.
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: Type-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Network for Circuit Link Prediction
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Link prediction for circuit completion is a crucial task in Electronic Design Automation (EDA), aiming to infer missing connections in incomplete circuits to accelerate design workflows and ensure Printed Circuit Board (PCB) reliability. However, due to the practical reality that circuit connectivity is defined by nets that connect specific pins of component instances, existing methods that rely on homogeneous representations and scalar shortest path distances collapse pin-level constraints into a single proximity signal. This collapse obscures component identities and pin semantics, and fails to capture long-range functional paths, which can slow design closure and potentially compromise PCB reliability by increasing the risk of electrically invalid links and subsequent rework. Addressing these challenges, we present a T ype-aware H eterogeneous G raph network for C ircuit link prediction ( THGC ), which enables accurate circuit link prediction by explicitly preserving component functional semantics and modeling type-aware dependencies. Specifically, THGC constructs a circuit-aware heterogeneous graph from netlists to preserve physical connectivity and component semantics, and refines representations through a multi-view encoder with Type-Aware Distance Encoding (TADE) to capture non-local dependencies. It then performs circuit-oriented link prediction using a heterogeneous graph network with dense convolutions and global sort pooling, optimized by a composite objective enforcing topological and semantic consistency, to predict electrically feasible missing connections for circuit completion. Comprehensive experiments are performed on 6,195 circuits collected from three benchmarks, and the results demonstrate that THGC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to a 47.51% relative improvement in terms of AUC. These results confirm that THGC effectively preserves component functional semantics and captures type-aware non-local dependencies for accurate circuit link prediction. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/THGC .
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: X-OCTANE: eXplainable On-Chip Telemetry-based Anomaly Notification Engine for Silicon Lifecycle Management
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Silicon Lifecycle Management (SLM) is essential for ensuring the reliability, security, and performance of modern computing platforms. Conventional SLM approaches rely on off-chip or software-only analytics, which lack on-die interpretability. We present X-OCTANE, an explainable on-chip telemetry-based anomaly notification engine. X–OCTANE is a hybrid explainability framework that integrates Causal-Preserving Mutual Information (CP–MI) with SHAP-based feature attribution for interpretable feature ranking and selection. The proposed feature rank-and-selection procedure retains competitive safety-oriented anomaly detection and bolsters security-specific in-field monitoring of compute platforms. For the 7 nm ASAP technology, X-OCTANE achieves competitive anomaly detection performance with less than 0.50% CPU die area and 1.0% non-idle power overhead. In addition, X–OCTANE improves anomaly-driven diagnosis accuracy by over 7% on average. Experimental validation using the PAMPAR benchmark suite on two separate experimental platforms demonstrates enhanced anomaly detection and diagnosis through the proposed explainable feature-rank-and-selection method. X–OCTANE establishes a scalable and transparent foundation for on-chip SLM analytics, unifying detection fidelity with causal interpretability.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: Evaluating LLM-based Workflows for Switched-Mode Power Supply Design
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) have great potential to enhance productivity in many disciplines, such as software engineering. However, it is unclear to what extent they can assist in the design process of electronic circuits. This article focuses on the application of LLMs to switched-mode power supply (SMPS) design for printed circuit boards (PCBs). We present multiple LLM-based workflows that combine reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a custom toolkit that enables the LLM to interact with the SPICE circuit simulator to receive physical feedback. Two benchmark experiments are presented to analyze the performance of LLM-based assistants on various design tasks. These include parameter tuning and topology adaption, as well as design optimization of SMPS circuits through optimal catalogue component selection to maximize circuit efficiency or balance multiple objectives like size, ripple, and component loss. Experiment results show that SPICE simulation feedback and current LLM advancements, such as reasoning, significantly increase the solve rate on 269 manually created benchmark tasks from 15% to 91%. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that most parameter tuning design tasks can be solved, while limits remain for certain topology adaption and multi-objective optimization tasks. Our experiments offer insights for improving current concepts, for example by adapting text-based circuit representations.
topics: AI辅助模拟与射频电路设计

sources.title: LLMsafe-Spectre: Efficient Spectre Attack Detection in LLM Environments using An Intelligent HPC events Selection Methodology
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) is transforming computing paradigms while introducing new challenges in hardware security vulnerability detection. Existing hardware performance counter (HPC)-based detectors demonstrate high efficacy for conventional applications (e.g., editing Office files, and playing videos) as well as web-accessible LLMs; however, our novel observation reveals that locally deployed large-scale LLMs exhibit access patterns with striking similarity to Spectre attacks. This similarity causes a dramatic deterioration in attack detection accuracy, plummeting from 99.86% to just 66.16% for DeepSeek-7b. To effectively mitigate detection performance degradation, we propose for the first time, LLMsafe-Spectre, a novel intelligent HPC event selection methodology designed for efficient Spectre attack detection in LLM environments. LLMsafe-Spectre is composed of two phases: (1) AI-assisted clustering of HPC events to efficiently narrow the search space, (2) ANOVA-based statistical analysis of inner-group and inter-group variances to pick out Top-K Spectre attack-LLMs discriminative events under limited registers in processors. This approach uniquely addresses the interference caused by LLM access while maintaining detection robustness. We comprehensively evaluate LLMsafe-Spectre across diverse Spectre variants, hardware architectures, web accessible LLMs and locally deployed large-scale LLMs scaling up from 1.5b to 14b. Experimental results demonstrate that our novel solution achieves superior detection accuracy up to 99.91% on average of scaling LLMs, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art approaches.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: Will AI mess my RTL? A snapshot-based approach to verifying AI-written RTL
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: With the growing interest in using AI (Artificial Intelligence) for RTL (Register-Transfer Level) hardware development, robust and comprehensive verification has become more important than ever. As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly assist in creating and modifying RTL designs, ensuring that these changes preserve existing functionality is paramount for building trust in AI-driven workflows. We present SVApshot, a fully automated framework that leverages LLMs to generate and systematically attempt to correct SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) for RTL modules, completely removing the human from the generation loop. SVApshot introduces a novel snapshot methodology that captures the current functionality of a design as a comprehensive set of formal assertions, creating a regression suite for validating future changes--whether made by humans or AI. The framework features automated duplicate detection, assertion set expansion, and iterative repair of failing assertions using LLM-guided debugging with formal verification feedback. Our experimental evaluation across diverse RTL modules demonstrates high coverage for complex modules, with successful detection of both manually-injected and AI-introduced bugs. Additionally, this framework opens the door for automatic generation of formal testbenches to benchmark LLMs for hardware design, moving beyond binary pass/fail metrics towards nuanced assertion-based scoring.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: Causal Signal Credit Assignment for Verilog Code Generation via Counterfactual Hardware Verification
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Large language models have improved Verilog generation, yet functional correctness remains difficult to optimize because simulation commonly provides a coarse module-level pass/fail outcome. Such feedback discards useful evidence from partially correct RTL modules and cannot determine whether a source statement is functionally responsible for an observed output behavior. We present a new method named Causal Signal Credit Assignment (CSCA), which is a counterfactual preference-optimization framework for Verilog generation. CSCA first performs continuous signal-level behavioral verification on sampled candidate modules. It then locates output-driving assignment spans and applies five interventions while holding the remaining module and testbench fixed. The resulting changes in signal-level errors are combined with behavioral agreement to form a continuous statement credit, which is mapped to response-token weights for strict weighted direct preference optimization. This enables CSCA to learn from locally supported statements without uniformly reinforcing an otherwise incorrect response. Built on Icarus Verilog and a CodeV-derived corpus, CSCA is evaluated on VerilogEval~2.0 and RTLLM~v2.0, including both code completion and specification-to-RTL tasks. With a Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct backbone, CSCA leads the evaluated 7B-scale models and remains comparable to the much larger GPT-5.4-mini on the reported Verilog-generation benchmarks.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: PRISM: Preference-based Reward and Uncertainty-Integrated Synthesis Minimization for RTL PPA Optimization
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: This paper introduces a budget-aware, multi-objective framework (called PRISM) for RTL optimization that improves power, performance, and area (PPA) while sharply limiting expensive commercial synthesis tool calls. Starting from a synthesizable baseline and functional testbench, the method iterates through LLM-driven rewrite generation, fast compile/simulation equivalence filtering, low-cost proxy feature extraction, and selective commercial synthesis tool (Synopsys Design Compiler (DC)) evaluation. To prioritize which candidates deserve high-quality synthesis, we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes, and combine ensemble uncertainty with a diversity-aware acquisition rule to avoid early bias and redundant evaluations. A key advantage is that PRISM maintains a best-tradeoff set G of non-dominated designs throughout the run: G preserves the best solutions found so far, is fed back into generation and refinement, and enables consistent, cumulative improvements rather than repeatedly restarting from the baseline. Across RTLLM v2.0 modules, the approach consistently yields post-synthesis gains under fixed commercial synthesis tool call budgets, and ablations confirm that reward-guided selection and candidate dropping are central to sample-efficient progress. PRISM efficacy is evaluated across multiple technology nodes (7 nm, 15 nm, and 45 nm) using identical pipelines without retraining.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: AutoC2V: Synthesis-Guided LLM Training for QoR-Optimized C++-to-Verilog Generation
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: High-level synthesis (HLS) can translate C/C++ kernels into register-transfer level (RTL) designs, yet generating high-quality hardware still relies heavily on manual pragma tuning and repeated synthesis evaluation. We propose AutoC2V, a C++-to-Verilog generation framework driven by real synthesis feedback that enables large language models (LLMs) to directly generate RTL with improved quality of results (QoR) from synthesizable C++ kernels. We construct training data from real synthesis results, including synthesizable C++ source code, the corresponding Verilog RTL, QoR metrics, and optimization objectives. Using this dataset, we align the model toward synthesis-aware RTL generation through Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To reduce the high cost of repeatedly invoking real synthesis during GRPO, we design the QoR Prediction Reward Model (QoR RM), which predicts latency and resource metrics by encoding RTL into long-context semantic representations, thereby providing low-cost and continuous QoR reward signals for policy optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that AutoC2V not only substantially improves RTL functional pass rates, but also achieves superior latency and resource optimization compared to the unfine-tuned base model, representative HLS optimization approaches (HLSPilot, LLM-DSE, and AutoDSE), and advanced general-purpose commercial models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek v4 Pro, and GLM-5.2). These results indicate that combining real synthesis data with efficient QoR reward modeling can further improve the ability of LLMs to generate high-quality RTL.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Recovering high-level RTL from such representations therefore helps engineers understand a circuit's functionality and enables RTL rewriting and resynthesis. A plausible function model is also insufficient unless the generated RTL is equivalent to the original circuit for all input combinations. In this paper, we present RTLREX, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools for function recovery, RTL generation, independent verification, and cost-guided rewriting. Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit. The LLM uses tool feedback to select further analyses, revise candidate RTL, and propose syntax-cost reductions. Experiments on 30 benchmarks from Problem A of the ICCAD 2022 CAD Contest show that RTLREX recovers equivalent high-level RTL for all benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art method WolFEx in recovery coverage. On benchmarks recovered by both methods, RTLREX reduces mean syntax cost by 20.5% relative to WolFEx. On complete truth-table benchmarks from the IWLS 2026 Contest, our framework reduces mean syntax cost by 95.7% relative to an LLM agent baseline on the benchmarks validated by both methods.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

approach: 选取RTLLM v2.0等公开RTL模块作为基准，固定商用综合调用预算，构建LLM重写候选生成与快速编译/等价性过滤流程。
对通过功能过滤的候选，提取低成本代理特征并用商用综合结果训练偏好奖励模型；同时用形式断言/等价性验证生成功能保持信号，与奖励不确定性一起构成排序规则。

sources.title: Type-Aware Heterogeneous Graph Network for Circuit Link Prediction
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Link prediction for circuit completion is a crucial task in Electronic Design Automation (EDA), aiming to infer missing connections in incomplete circuits to accelerate design workflows and ensure Printed Circuit Board (PCB) reliability. However, due to the practical reality that circuit connectivity is defined by nets that connect specific pins of component instances, existing methods that rely on homogeneous representations and scalar shortest path distances collapse pin-level constraints into a single proximity signal. This collapse obscures component identities and pin semantics, and fails to capture long-range functional paths, which can slow design closure and potentially compromise PCB reliability by increasing the risk of electrically invalid links and subsequent rework. Addressing these challenges, we present a T ype-aware H eterogeneous G raph network for C ircuit link prediction ( THGC ), which enables accurate circuit link prediction by explicitly preserving component functional semantics and modeling type-aware dependencies. Specifically, THGC constructs a circuit-aware heterogeneous graph from netlists to preserve physical connectivity and component semantics, and refines representations through a multi-view encoder with Type-Aware Distance Encoding (TADE) to capture non-local dependencies. It then performs circuit-oriented link prediction using a heterogeneous graph network with dense convolutions and global sort pooling, optimized by a composite objective enforcing topological and semantic consistency, to predict electrically feasible missing connections for circuit completion. Comprehensive experiments are performed on 6,195 circuits collected from three benchmarks, and the results demonstrate that THGC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving up to a 47.51% relative improvement in terms of AUC. These results confirm that THGC effectively preserves component functional semantics and captures type-aware non-local dependencies for accurate circuit link prediction. The source code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/THGC .
topics: 学习方法辅助综合、物理设计与PPA评估

sources.title: X-OCTANE: eXplainable On-Chip Telemetry-based Anomaly Notification Engine for Silicon Lifecycle Management
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Silicon Lifecycle Management (SLM) is essential for ensuring the reliability, security, and performance of modern computing platforms. Conventional SLM approaches rely on off-chip or software-only analytics, which lack on-die interpretability. We present X-OCTANE, an explainable on-chip telemetry-based anomaly notification engine. X–OCTANE is a hybrid explainability framework that integrates Causal-Preserving Mutual Information (CP–MI) with SHAP-based feature attribution for interpretable feature ranking and selection. The proposed feature rank-and-selection procedure retains competitive safety-oriented anomaly detection and bolsters security-specific in-field monitoring of compute platforms. For the 7 nm ASAP technology, X-OCTANE achieves competitive anomaly detection performance with less than 0.50% CPU die area and 1.0% non-idle power overhead. In addition, X–OCTANE improves anomaly-driven diagnosis accuracy by over 7% on average. Experimental validation using the PAMPAR benchmark suite on two separate experimental platforms demonstrates enhanced anomaly detection and diagnosis through the proposed explainable feature-rank-and-selection method. X–OCTANE establishes a scalable and transparent foundation for on-chip SLM analytics, unifying detection fidelity with causal interpretability.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: Evaluating LLM-based Workflows for Switched-Mode Power Supply Design
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) have great potential to enhance productivity in many disciplines, such as software engineering. However, it is unclear to what extent they can assist in the design process of electronic circuits. This article focuses on the application of LLMs to switched-mode power supply (SMPS) design for printed circuit boards (PCBs). We present multiple LLM-based workflows that combine reasoning, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a custom toolkit that enables the LLM to interact with the SPICE circuit simulator to receive physical feedback. Two benchmark experiments are presented to analyze the performance of LLM-based assistants on various design tasks. These include parameter tuning and topology adaption, as well as design optimization of SMPS circuits through optimal catalogue component selection to maximize circuit efficiency or balance multiple objectives like size, ripple, and component loss. Experiment results show that SPICE simulation feedback and current LLM advancements, such as reasoning, significantly increase the solve rate on 269 manually created benchmark tasks from 15% to 91%. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that most parameter tuning design tasks can be solved, while limits remain for certain topology adaption and multi-objective optimization tasks. Our experiments offer insights for improving current concepts, for example by adapting text-based circuit representations.
topics: AI辅助模拟与射频电路设计

sources.title: LLMsafe-Spectre: Efficient Spectre Attack Detection in LLM Environments using An Intelligent HPC events Selection Methodology
sources.venue: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
sources.excerpt: The widespread adoption of large language models (LLMs) is transforming computing paradigms while introducing new challenges in hardware security vulnerability detection. Existing hardware performance counter (HPC)-based detectors demonstrate high efficacy for conventional applications (e.g., editing Office files, and playing videos) as well as web-accessible LLMs; however, our novel observation reveals that locally deployed large-scale LLMs exhibit access patterns with striking similarity to Spectre attacks. This similarity causes a dramatic deterioration in attack detection accuracy, plummeting from 99.86% to just 66.16% for DeepSeek-7b. To effectively mitigate detection performance degradation, we propose for the first time, LLMsafe-Spectre, a novel intelligent HPC event selection methodology designed for efficient Spectre attack detection in LLM environments. LLMsafe-Spectre is composed of two phases: (1) AI-assisted clustering of HPC events to efficiently narrow the search space, (2) ANOVA-based statistical analysis of inner-group and inter-group variances to pick out Top-K Spectre attack-LLMs discriminative events under limited registers in processors. This approach uniquely addresses the interference caused by LLM access while maintaining detection robustness. We comprehensively evaluate LLMsafe-Spectre across diverse Spectre variants, hardware architectures, web accessible LLMs and locally deployed large-scale LLMs scaling up from 1.5b to 14b. Experimental results demonstrate that our novel solution achieves superior detection accuracy up to 99.91% on average of scaling LLMs, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art approaches.
topics: AI辅助器件、制造、测试与安全

sources.title: Will AI mess my RTL? A snapshot-based approach to verifying AI-written RTL
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: With the growing interest in using AI (Artificial Intelligence) for RTL (Register-Transfer Level) hardware development, robust and comprehensive verification has become more important than ever. As Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly assist in creating and modifying RTL designs, ensuring that these changes preserve existing functionality is paramount for building trust in AI-driven workflows. We present SVApshot, a fully automated framework that leverages LLMs to generate and systematically attempt to correct SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) for RTL modules, completely removing the human from the generation loop. SVApshot introduces a novel snapshot methodology that captures the current functionality of a design as a comprehensive set of formal assertions, creating a regression suite for validating future changes--whether made by humans or AI. The framework features automated duplicate detection, assertion set expansion, and iterative repair of failing assertions using LLM-guided debugging with formal verification feedback. Our experimental evaluation across diverse RTL modules demonstrates high coverage for complex modules, with successful detection of both manually-injected and AI-introduced bugs. Additionally, this framework opens the door for automatic generation of formal testbenches to benchmark LLMs for hardware design, moving beyond binary pass/fail metrics towards nuanced assertion-based scoring.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: Causal Signal Credit Assignment for Verilog Code Generation via Counterfactual Hardware Verification
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Large language models have improved Verilog generation, yet functional correctness remains difficult to optimize because simulation commonly provides a coarse module-level pass/fail outcome. Such feedback discards useful evidence from partially correct RTL modules and cannot determine whether a source statement is functionally responsible for an observed output behavior. We present a new method named Causal Signal Credit Assignment (CSCA), which is a counterfactual preference-optimization framework for Verilog generation. CSCA first performs continuous signal-level behavioral verification on sampled candidate modules. It then locates output-driving assignment spans and applies five interventions while holding the remaining module and testbench fixed. The resulting changes in signal-level errors are combined with behavioral agreement to form a continuous statement credit, which is mapped to response-token weights for strict weighted direct preference optimization. This enables CSCA to learn from locally supported statements without uniformly reinforcing an otherwise incorrect response. Built on Icarus Verilog and a CodeV-derived corpus, CSCA is evaluated on VerilogEval~2.0 and RTLLM~v2.0, including both code completion and specification-to-RTL tasks. With a Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct backbone, CSCA leads the evaluated 7B-scale models and remains comparable to the much larger GPT-5.4-mini on the reported Verilog-generation benchmarks.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: PRISM: Preference-based Reward and Uncertainty-Integrated Synthesis Minimization for RTL PPA Optimization
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: This paper introduces a budget-aware, multi-objective framework (called PRISM) for RTL optimization that improves power, performance, and area (PPA) while sharply limiting expensive commercial synthesis tool calls. Starting from a synthesizable baseline and functional testbench, the method iterates through LLM-driven rewrite generation, fast compile/simulation equivalence filtering, low-cost proxy feature extraction, and selective commercial synthesis tool (Synopsys Design Compiler (DC)) evaluation. To prioritize which candidates deserve high-quality synthesis, we train a preference-based reward model using pairwise ranking supervision derived from commercial synthesis tool outcomes, and combine ensemble uncertainty with a diversity-aware acquisition rule to avoid early bias and redundant evaluations. A key advantage is that PRISM maintains a best-tradeoff set G of non-dominated designs throughout the run: G preserves the best solutions found so far, is fed back into generation and refinement, and enables consistent, cumulative improvements rather than repeatedly restarting from the baseline. Across RTLLM v2.0 modules, the approach consistently yields post-synthesis gains under fixed commercial synthesis tool call budgets, and ablations confirm that reward-guided selection and candidate dropping are central to sample-efficient progress. PRISM efficacy is evaluated across multiple technology nodes (7 nm, 15 nm, and 45 nm) using identical pipelines without retraining.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: AutoC2V: Synthesis-Guided LLM Training for QoR-Optimized C++-to-Verilog Generation
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: High-level synthesis (HLS) can translate C/C++ kernels into register-transfer level (RTL) designs, yet generating high-quality hardware still relies heavily on manual pragma tuning and repeated synthesis evaluation. We propose AutoC2V, a C++-to-Verilog generation framework driven by real synthesis feedback that enables large language models (LLMs) to directly generate RTL with improved quality of results (QoR) from synthesizable C++ kernels. We construct training data from real synthesis results, including synthesizable C++ source code, the corresponding Verilog RTL, QoR metrics, and optimization objectives. Using this dataset, we align the model toward synthesis-aware RTL generation through Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). To reduce the high cost of repeatedly invoking real synthesis during GRPO, we design the QoR Prediction Reward Model (QoR RM), which predicts latency and resource metrics by encoding RTL into long-context semantic representations, thereby providing low-cost and continuous QoR reward signals for policy optimization. Experimental results demonstrate that AutoC2V not only substantially improves RTL functional pass rates, but also achieves superior latency and resource optimization compared to the unfine-tuned base model, representative HLS optimization approaches (HLSPilot, LLM-DSE, and AutoDSE), and advanced general-purpose commercial models (Claude Opus 4.8, GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek v4 Pro, and GLM-5.2). These results indicate that combining real synthesis data with efficient QoR reward modeling can further improve the ability of LLMs to generate high-quality RTL.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复

sources.title: RTLREX: LLM-Guided Framework for Exact High-Level RTL Recovery
sources.venue: arXiv
sources.excerpt: Hardware designs may be available only as gate-level netlists or input-output descriptions when the original register-transfer-level (RTL) design and documentation are not accessible. Low-level representations obscure word-level computation and its finite-width behavior. Recovering high-level RTL from such representations therefore helps engineers understand a circuit's functionality and enables RTL rewriting and resynthesis. A plausible function model is also insufficient unless the generated RTL is equivalent to the original circuit for all input combinations. In this paper, we present RTLREX, a large language model (LLM)-guided framework that coordinates domain-specific tools for function recovery, RTL generation, independent verification, and cost-guided rewriting. Independent verification establishes equivalence between the recovered RTL and the original circuit. The LLM uses tool feedback to select further analyses, revise candidate RTL, and propose syntax-cost reductions. Experiments on 30 benchmarks from Problem A of the ICCAD 2022 CAD Contest show that RTLREX recovers equivalent high-level RTL for all benchmarks, surpassing the state-of-the-art method WolFEx in recovery coverage. On benchmarks recovered by both methods, RTLREX reduces mean syntax cost by 20.5% relative to WolFEx. On complete truth-table benchmarks from the IWLS 2026 Contest, our framework reduces mean syntax cost by 95.7% relative to an LLM agent baseline on the benchmarks validated by both methods.
topics: LLM辅助RTL设计、验证与修复
